title: MRI radiomics-based machine learning model for complete response classification after chemoradiotherapy in advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Low and mid rectal cancer (upper rectum excluded)
stage_detail: Advanced / locally advanced rectal cancer treated with NCRT; cTNM not reported
data_source_detail: Gachon University Gil Medical Center; 3.0T post-NCRT T2WI MRI of patients diagnosed Dec 2012-Jul 2025
n_source: Results section 3 and Table 2 (223 patients: 47 CR, 176 non-CR; 417 ROIs)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify complete responders after NCRT to select candidates for watch-and-wait
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy then watch-and-wait vs surgery
data_modality_detail: Post-NCRT axial T2-weighted 3.0T MRI; 107 PyRadiomics features from manual ROIs
algorithm: 16 combinations of feature selection (ANOVA, RFE, SBS, LASSO) x classifier (LR, SVM, RF, XGBoost); best RFE+SVM
input_features: 107 radiomic features (first order, GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, GLDM, NGTDM, shape) from post-NCRT T2WI; RFE kept 10
comparator_detail: Other feature-selection/classifier combinations; no clinician or clinical-model comparator
primary_outcome: Complete response (pathologic CR, or sustained CR with >=5y follow-up without surgery) vs non-CR
performance_value: Independent test set, RFE+SVM: sensitivity 0.84 (0.73-0.94), specificity 0.80 (0.72-0.89), accuracy 0.82 (0.76-0.88), F1 0.82 (0.76-0.88), AUC 0.86 (0.80-0.92) (Table 3); training 5-fold CV mean AUC 0.89 (abstract, Fig 3)
performance_source: Table 3 (SVM row) and Abstract; primary_metric_value = sensitivity for CR class
patient_outcomes_detail: No survival or recurrence analysis by predicted class
validation_detail: Patient-level stratified split into training set and independent test set from the same single-center cohort; 5-fold CV and tuning inside training set; test-set size and split ratio not reported; no external validation
funding: Korean MOTIE program (RS-202502305698, Digital Medical Products Development Based on Medical Data Synthesis and AI Technologies)
key_finding: RFE+SVM on post-NCRT MRI radiomics classified CR vs non-CR with test sensitivity 0.84 and specificity 0.80; exploratory, single-center, no external validation.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single center; small CR group (47) with class imbalance; no external validation; no calibration or decision curve analysis; single-observer ROI without interobserver testing; TotalEnergy dependence on voxel geometry.
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: Table 3 test AUC for SVM is 0.86 (RF 0.89) whereas text/abstract cite RFE+SVM AUC 0.89 as 5-fold CV in training set; Methods also say CV was on the entire 223-patient cohort. Test set size and split ratio not reported (n_performance/n_train/n_test NR). Multiple ROIs per CR patient were averaged to patient-level vectors. CR label mixes pCR (43) and 5-year sustained clinical CR (4). Sensitivity chosen as headline (abstract test metrics).

title: Metabolic dynamic score and machine learning: a novel approach to predicting pathological complete response in rectal cancer after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer, mean distance from anal verge about 5.6 cm
stage_detail: cT1-4 (cT3-4 about 95%), cN0 vs cN+ (about 77% cN+); AJCC 8th; all received preoperative NCRT
data_source_detail: Two hospitals in Fujian (Center 1 n=846; Center 2 n=454), Jun 2010-Jul 2017; Center 2 used as external validation
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR after NCRT to support MDT decisions (watch-and-wait or organ preservation if high probability; early surgery or intensified adjuvant therapy if low)
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (IMRT 45 Gy + boost; CapeOX, capecitabine or FOLFOX) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Serum biochemistry before and after NCRT (Metabolic Dynamic Score: GGT, ALP, delta-LDL, post-HDL, ApoA) plus cT, cN, tumor size
algorithm: XGBoost (selected among 10 ML algorithms); MDS built by multivariable logistic regression
input_features: MDS, tumor size, clinical T stage, clinical N stage (MDS requires post-NCRT laboratory values)
comparator_detail: Nine other ML algorithms (RF, DT, LR, LightGBM, AdaBoost, kNN, SVM, naive Bayes, MLP); logistic nomogram
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (no viable tumor cells in primary and regional nodes)
performance_value: XGBoost external validation (Center 2, n=454): AUC 0.92, AUPRC 0.779; training: AUC 0.93, AUPRC 0.732; internal validation (n=196): reported only in figures (Fig 3D-E); external AUC male 0.92 / female 0.91; logistic nomogram AUC 0.929 (0.902-0.956), AP 0.791
performance_source: Abstract; Results 3.5 (Figures 4B-C)
validation_detail: Random stratified 70/30 split of Center 1 (training n=650, internal validation n=196), 10-fold CV for tuning, and independent retrospective cohort from Center 2 (n=454, same province); one external site only
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82172800); Fujian Provincial special funds (2020B019); Fujian Joint Funds (2020Y9125); First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University talent program (YJRC3600)
key_finding: XGBoost using a Metabolic Dynamic Score (pre/post-NCRT serum lipids and enzymes) plus cT, cN and tumor size predicted pCR with external AUC 0.92; authors frame it as exploratory pending prospective validation.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective with selection bias; heterogeneous CRT regimens without stratification; no nutritional covariates; both centers in same Chinese province limiting generalizability; applicability to TNT/short-course RT unproven.
other_models_outcomes: Logistic nomogram (MDS, cT, cN, tumor size): AUC 0.929 (0.902-0.956), AP 0.791 (Fig 2); nine other ML models compared in figures/heatmaps only
extraction_note: Code at GitHub panzhen1998/MDS; data 'available without undue reservation' coded upon_request; guideline STROCSS (coded other). n_test = 196 internal + 454 external. MDS text formula signs differ from Table 1 (table coefficients used) and Discussion calls variables 'pretreatment baseline' although MDS needs post-NCRT labs. Interactive web tool provided (Supp Fig 1). Primary metric CI not reported in text; internal-validation numbers only in figures.

title: Prediction of Pathological Complete Response after Chemoradiation for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Using Machine Learning with Clinical Features, the INTERCEPTOR Study Preliminary Model.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer; distance to anorectal junction categories reported
stage_detail: LARC per Dutch guideline (cT4, or cT3 with MRF <1 mm, cN2, EMVI or extra-mesorectal nodes); cT3 about 49%, cT4 about 51%; cN+ about 79%; cM0
data_source_detail: Prospectively maintained institutional registry, Erasmus MC Cancer Institute, TME 2004-2018 after long-course CRT
n_source: Results 'Included patients' and Table 1 (238; 30 pCR); 218 in multivariate XGBoost analysis
therapeutic_decision_detail: Pretreatment prediction of pCR after CRT to help patients decide on CRT and to identify candidates for organ preservation / watch-and-wait
treatment_context: Long-course chemoradiotherapy (50-50.4 Gy + capecitabine) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pretreatment clinical and radiological-report variables (positive node count on MRI, cN, cT, weight, BMI, distance to anorectal junction)
algorithm: XGBoost with handcrafted feature-subset search; 5-fold cross-validation
input_features: Best combination: number of radiologically positive nodes, weight, cN stage
comparator_detail: Single-variable XGBoost (positive node count) and other handcrafted feature combinations
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (ypT0N0M0, Mandard TRG1)
performance_value: Combination 1 (positive nodes + weight + cN), 5-fold CV mean±SD: AUC 0.74±0.11, sensitivity 0.500±0.279, specificity 0.835±0.032, balanced accuracy 0.667±0.130; single positive-node model: AUC 0.65±0.04, sens 0.83±0.15, spec 0.45±0.10
performance_source: Table 2 (Case 1); Abstract and Results for single-variable model
validation_detail: Internal 5-fold cross-validation only within the same single-center dataset; no independent test or external cohort; metrics reported as mean ± SD across folds
funding: No specific grant or funding
key_finding: Pretreatment clinical variables gave only poor-to-fair pCR discrimination (single positive-node count AUC 0.65; best combination AUC 0.74) in an XGBoost CV analysis of 238 LARC patients.
limitations_as_stated: No external validation; class imbalance (12.6% pCR) and small sample with overfitting risk; no lateral lymph node data; clinical-only features without imaging/pathology/molecular data.
other_models_outcomes: Other handcrafted combinations (AUC): positive nodes+weight 0.72; positive nodes+distance 0.62; positive nodes+number nodes 0.65; positive nodes+cT 0.65; cN stage 0.63
extraction_note: Main model choice: abstract anchors on single positive-node model (AUC 0.65) while Methods/Results single out the best multivariate model (Combination 1, AUC 0.74); by rule 2(b) Combination 1 taken as primary and the single-variable model recorded in performance_value. Table 2 label 'Case 6: cN stage' vs footnote 'Combination 6: positive nodes with cT and cN' differ. 20 of 238 patients excluded from multivariate analysis for missing data (median imputation for continuous). Feature subset chosen by handcrafted search on the same CV data (possible optimistic bias). Figure/supplement references (Figures X, Z) are placeholders in the text.

title: Tumour cell density quantified by artificial intelligence is associated with differential benefit from irinotecan-based chemo-radiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer: a post-hoc study of the phase 3 ARISTOTLE trial.
tumor_site_detail: MRI-defined locally advanced rectal cancer
stage_detail: MRI T2 6%, T3 78%, T4 17%; N0 24%, N1 46%, N2 30%; LARC in long-course nCRT
data_source_detail: ARISTOTLE phase 3 trial (ISRCTN09351447), 414 of 564 participants with digitised pre-treatment biopsy H&E WSIs; AI quality assessed on 116 external WSIs and 100 ARISTOTLE resection WSIs
n_source: Abstract and Methods 'Study design'; pCR analysis restricted to 355 (Table 3)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Candidate predictive biomarker (TCD) to select patients for irinotecan-intensified neoadjuvant CRT vs standard CRT
treatment_context: Capecitabine + RT (CRT) vs capecitabine + irinotecan + RT (IrCRT)
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide images of pre-treatment biopsies (20x); tissue classifier plus cell detector
algorithm: EfficientNet tissue classifier (trained on NCT-CRC-HE-100K) + pre-trained SoftCTM cell detector; TCD = tumour cells / classifiable cells in tumour and stroma regions; cut-off 0.5 (cohort median)
input_features: Digitised H&E biopsy WSIs; outputs TCD-high (>=0.5) vs TCD-low
comparator_detail: AI-derived TCD compared with pathologist-annotated TCD; treatment arm CRT vs IrCRT used for interaction analysis
primary_outcome: DFS and OS (primary) and pCR (secondary) by TCD status and treatment arm; AI TCD agreement with manual TCD for tool quality
performance_value: AI vs manual TCD: Lin CCC 0.831 (0.760-0.886) in 116 external WSIs; CCC 0.801 (0.732-0.857) in 100 ARISTOTLE resection WSIs; categorical agreement 93%, kappa 0.854; tissue classifier precision 0.873, recall 0.984. Treatment-TCD interaction: DFS chi2 6.88 p=0.009, OS chi2 10.61 p=0.001
performance_source: Results 'Tumour cell density identified by AI' and Fig 2a
patient_outcomes_detail: TCD-high: IrCRT vs CRT DFS HR 0.57 (0.36-0.90), OS HR 0.50 (0.30-0.84), pCR 23% vs 11% (adjusted p=0.13); TCD-low: no benefit, OS trend worse (HR 1.55, 0.96-2.51); TCD alone not prognostic
validation_detail: AI tools trained on public NCT-CRC-HE-100K (not on ARISTOTLE) then applied to 414 trial biopsies; cut-off 0.5 = median, not outcome-optimised; measurement agreement checked on 116 external WSIs and 100 trial resection WSIs; clinical value tested only as treatment-by-TCD interaction in a post-hoc trial analysis, no prospective test
funding: Cancer Research UK Radiation Research Network seed funding; CRUK ARISTOTLE sample collection grant (A18745); UKRI Future Leadership Fellowship (MR/T040785/1); CRUK City of London Centre Award (C7893/A2899)
conflicts_of_interest: NPW reports grants from Yorkshire Cancer Research, NIHR, GSK, Pierre Fabre, Roche Diagnostics and consulting fees from BMS, Astellas, Pfizer, GSK, Amgen, Servier; other authors none
key_finding: AI-derived tumour cell density from pre-treatment biopsies showed a significant treatment-by-TCD interaction: irinotecan-intensified CRT improved DFS and OS only in TCD-high patients (post-hoc, hypothesis-generating).
limitations_as_stated: Post-hoc analysis of a trial sub-cohort without prespecified protocol; needs independent and prospective validation; AI measurement could be refined; molecular correlates not comprehensively evaluated.
other_models_outcomes: NR
extraction_note: Not a predictive classifier of an outcome: the AI quantifies TCD and the clinical claim is treatment-effect heterogeneity. Primary metric is AI-vs-manual agreement (CCC) in the 116 external WSIs (n_test=116; n_unit mixes patients/WSIs); validation_basis=outcome_association because the 414-patient trial cohort has no TCD reference label. Tissue-classifier training/validation split and metrics only in Table S3 (n_train NR, supplement_needed=yes). The ARISTOTLE trial patients may overlap with other ARISTOTLE post-hoc biomarker studies cited in the paper. Interaction results in abstract (chi2) vs HR 0.44 in Results are different statistics of the same test.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics to Predict Response to Neoadjuvant Therapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Retrospective Study.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal adenocarcinoma, LARC (low-rectal example given; location per baseline MRI)
stage_detail: Baseline MRI T2-T4 (T3 about 72%, T4 about 16%); N0 3.5%, N1 about 34%, N2 62.8%; EMVI present 36%
data_source_detail: University of Pisa tertiary center, 2017-2022; 86 of 400 eligible patients with baseline and restaging MRI and surgery
therapeutic_decision_detail: Early identification of non-responders to neoadjuvant therapy (mrTRG>=3 at restaging) to tailor treatment and reduce unnecessary toxicity
treatment_context: Heterogeneous neoadjuvant therapy: CRT 61.6%, short-course RT 19.8%, induction chemotherapy then CRT 16.3%, chemotherapy 1.2%, RT 1.2%
data_modality_detail: Baseline oblique axial T2-weighted MRI (3 scanners, 1.5T and 3T); 107 PyRadiomics features with and without N4 bias correction
algorithm: LASSO feature selection followed by elastic-net logistic regression
input_features: 107 radiomic features from manually segmented baseline T2w tumour ROI (5-12 selected per iteration); no clinical variables
comparator_detail: No comparator; clinical models not compared
primary_outcome: Non-response on restaging MRI (mrTRG 3-5) vs response (mrTRG 1-2); not pathological response
performance_value: Repeated stratified 5-fold CV (20x), mean (95% CI): AUC 0.73 (0.70-0.76), accuracy 0.72 (0.70-0.75), sensitivity 0.79 (0.77-0.81), specificity 0.50 (0.46-0.54), balanced accuracy 0.64 (0.60-0.69), PPV 0.84, NPV 0.42, F1 0.81
performance_source: Results section 3, paragraph after Figure 4 (and Abstract)
patient_outcomes_detail: No survival or pathological outcome analysis
validation_detail: Repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (20 repetitions, 100 test folds) within a single-center cohort; preprocessing, LASSO and tuning inside training folds; no external or hold-out validation
funding: European Union NextGenerationEU via Italian MUR PNRR, project PE_00000019 HEAL ITALIA (CUP I53C22001440006)
key_finding: Baseline T2 MRI radiomics with LASSO plus elastic-net logistic regression predicted mrTRG non-response with CV AUC 0.73, sensitivity 0.79 and specificity 0.50; no external validation.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single center with small cohort; no external validation; heterogeneous neoadjuvant regimens not modelled; no class balancing; no ComBat harmonization across three scanners; no inter/intra-observer or feature stability analysis; no calibration or clinical-model comparison; mrTRG reference standard may overestimate residual tumour.
other_models_outcomes: NR
extraction_note: Outcome is mrTRG at restaging (positive class = non-responder), not pathological response. Only 1 patient mrTRG1 and 19 mrTRG2 (23% responders). Data availability: 'included in the article; further inquiries to corresponding authors' coded upon_request. Percentages for T stage derived from Table 3 counts.

title: Development and evaluation of an explainable machine learning selection pipeline for predicting neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy response in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer; distance from anal verge reported
data_source_detail: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, 128 consecutive LARC patients, Sep 2013-Nov 2022, EMR data
n_source: Methods 'Data selection and pre-processing' (89 train / 39 test) and Results baseline data
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pathological response (pCR, TRG) to nCRT from pretreatment clinical variables within an explainable ML model-selection pipeline
treatment_context: Long-course nCRT (45-50.4 Gy; XELOX or capecitabine) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pretreatment general indicators, blood counts and inflammatory indices, tumour markers (CEA, CA19-9, CA125, CA153, CA724) and treatment variables; best models used tumour markers only
algorithm: Decision tree (selected) among SVM, DT, RF, LR with default hyperparameters; SHAP explanation
input_features: Selected pCR model (DT'): tumour markers only (CEA, CA19-9, etc.); all-feature set also tested across 15 feature-group scenarios
comparator_detail: SVM, random forest and logistic regression compared with DT in the algorithm pool
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (also TRG 0-1 vs 2-3 as parallel endpoint)
performance_value: DT with tumour markers only, hold-out test set (n=39), pCR: accuracy 0.82 (0.68-0.92), F1 0.71, precision 0.90, recall 0.68 (Table 3); 5-fold CV: accuracy 0.65±0.03, AUROC 0.71, AUPRC 0.61. TRG-DT' (tumour markers) test accuracy 0.76, F1 0.72; CV accuracy 0.68±0.03, AUROC 0.64, AUPRC 0.59
performance_source: Abstract and Results 'Experimental results based on all or part of the clinical features'; Table 3 (CI); CV in Table 4
validation_detail: Stratified 70/30 hold-out split of one single-center cohort (n=89 train, n=39 test) plus five-fold CV and bootstrap CIs; 15 feature-group scenarios compared on the same test set; no external validation
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82073476); National Key R&D Program of China (2022YFC2503700, 2022YFC2503703); Jiangsu Province special fund (BE2022727); Jiangsu Provincial Medical Key Discipline (ZDXK202235); Suzhou innovation project (SLJ2021005)
key_finding: Under a performance-plus-explainability screening pipeline, decision trees using pretreatment tumour markers alone predicted pCR with test accuracy 0.82 (F1 0.71); CEA and CA19-9 were the key predictors.
limitations_as_stated: Clinical and blood variables only (no imaging); modest performance with wide CIs and risk of unstable or optimistic model selection; default hyperparameters; no calibration analysis; single hold-out test from small single-center Asian cohort without external validation.
other_models_outcomes: TRG 0-1 vs 2-3 DT' (tumour markers): test accuracy 0.76, F1 0.72; TRG-DT (all features): F1 0.63, accuracy 0.68, CV accuracy 0.64±0.06, AUROC 0.64, AUPRC 0.68; all-feature pCR models SVM/RF excluded (F1 <0.60)
extraction_note: Co-primary endpoints (pCR and TRG): pCR tumour-marker DT chosen because it leads the abstract/results and gives the headline accuracy 0.82; TRG results in other_models_outcomes. Study is mainly methodological (model-selection pipeline). The tumour-marker-only subset was chosen after comparing 15 scenarios on the same 39-patient test set (selection on test data, as the authors acknowledge). Several CV/AUROC tables are in supplementary tables S1-S4 (supplement_needed=yes). 'Sanity check' adding the other endpoint as a feature is intentional leakage, not performance, and not used. Table 3 is badly extracted; CI for pCR DT' taken from the row matching accuracy 0.82/F1 0.71.

title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting postoperative complications after transanal total mesorectal excision: a multicenter study.
tumor_site_detail: Mid-to-low rectal adenocarcinoma treated with taTME (inferior margin within 10 cm of anal verge or below peritoneal reflection)
stage_detail: Postoperative TNM: stage 0 1.3%, I 40.0%, II 25.3%, III 31.4%, IV 1.3% (as reported); no adjacent organ invasion or distant metastasis at inclusion; neoadjuvant therapy in 26.9%
data_source_detail: Three Chinese centers (Fujian Medical University First Affiliated Hospital for development; Xiamen University First Affiliated Hospital and Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital for external validation), taTME Feb 2017-Dec 2024
n_source: Abstract and Methods 'Data source' (185 development + 60 external)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify high-risk patients for 30-day complications after taTME for targeted perioperative interventions (nutrition support, closer monitoring)
treatment_context: Transanal total mesorectal excision (laparoscopic-assisted taTME)
data_modality_detail: Preoperative clinical/laboratory variables and postoperative day-1 CRP (final 6 predictors: postoperative CRP, preoperative total protein, smoking, age group, neoadjuvant therapy, ASA)
algorithm: AdaBoost (best of 11 algorithms); LASSO plus multivariable logistic regression for feature selection; 10-fold CV; SHAP
input_features: Six predictors: postoperative CRP, preoperative TP, smoking history, age group (>=80), neoadjuvant therapy, ASA score
comparator_detail: Ten other ML algorithms compared on development and external sets (RF, GBM, SVM, LR, KNN, NN, XGBoost, NB, discriminant analysis, LASSO); nomogram from logistic regression
primary_outcome: Any 30-day postoperative complication (Clavien-Dindo)
performance_value: AdaBoost external validation (n=60): AUC 0.872 (0.771-0.972), accuracy 83.3%, sensitivity 56.25%, specificity 94.7%; development (n=185): AUC 0.822 (0.751-0.892), training accuracy 99.4%
performance_source: Abstract and Results 'Model validation and performance on the test set' (Fig 4)
patient_outcomes_detail: Outcome is the predicted complication itself; no outcome change from model use
validation_detail: Development at one center (n=185) with 10-fold CV; temporally unspecified external cohort pooled from two independent centers (n=60); no prospective validation
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82403558); Fujian Joint Funds for Innovation of Science and Technology (2024Y9208); Fujian Provincial Chu Ying Plan (SCYJHJRC-ZGW2024)
key_finding: AdaBoost with six clinical variables (top SHAP predictor: postoperative day-1 CRP) predicted 30-day complications after taTME with external AUC 0.872 (n=60, two centers).
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective design with selection bias; small external cohort (n=60, 17 events); regional data only; composite all-grade endpoint with few severe events (n=16); prospective multiregional validation needed.
other_models_outcomes: Random forest and a boosting method development AUC 0.809; other models' external metrics only in Fig 4A/C
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: external cohort stated as 17 complication events in Limitations, but reported sensitivity 56.25% implies 16 positives (9/16). Authors label the design 'multicenter case-control' although patients were consecutive; coded retrospective_cohort. Prediction uses postoperative day-1 CRP (not available preoperatively); the outcome is surgical complication, not an oncologic treatment decision. Training accuracy 99.4% indicates overfitting on the development set. External cohort time period not separated from development.

title: Photoacoustic-ultrasound endoscopy for assessment of rectal cancer treatment response: A prospective study with T2-weighted MRI radiomics comparison.
tumor_site_detail: Biopsy-proven rectal cancer within 15 cm of anal verge, scheduled for resection
stage_detail: ARPAM-US cohort: any stage; post-treatment T0 16%, T2 40%, T3 32%, T4 12%; 3 of 25 untreated (staging only); retrospective MRI cohort mostly nCRT
data_source_detail: Prospective ARPAM-US endoscopy cohort (n=25, NCT04339374, May 2024-Aug 2025) plus retrospective T2w MRI XNAT cohort (n=119, 2020-2024) used for MRI radiomics comparison; Washington University
n_source: Methods 2.2 and 2.4.1, Results 3.1 (25 prospective + 119 retrospective); about 400 selected B-scans in the prospective cohort
therapeutic_decision_detail: Accurate identification of pCR after nCRT for non-operative watch-and-wait strategies
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery (all imaged patients proceeded to resection)
data_modality_detail: Co-registered acoustic-resolution photoacoustic microscopy and ultrasound (ARPAM-US) endoscopic B-scans acquired intraoperatively; comparison arm used T2w MRI radiomics
algorithm: ResNet50 (RadImageNet-pretrained) with CORAL ordinal head on whole B-scans, 5-fold CV ensemble with patient-level majority vote; pCR taken as probability of TRG 0
input_features: Whole 512x512 co-registered PA and US B-scans (about 8 tumour-bed and 8 normal-rectum scans per patient)
comparator_detail: T2w MRI radiomics logistic regression models (RFpre/post/delta/joint) and radiomics plus ResNet-18 features SVM trained on retrospective cohort; US-only and PA-only models
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (ypT0N0, TRG 0) on surgical specimen
performance_value: ARPAM-US early fusion 5-fold CV mean AUC 0.956 (0.912-1.000); PA-only 0.947 (0.896-0.998); US-only 0.881 (0.767-0.995). MRI radiomics (trained on XNAT, tested on prospective cohort): RFjoint 0.877 internal CV -> 0.654 prospective; RFpre 0.777->0.543; RFpost 0.816->0.537; RFdelta 0.642->0.569; radiomics+DL SVM 0.929->0.720
performance_source: Abstract; Results 3.3 and Fig 6; MRI results in Table 3
patient_outcomes_detail: Reference is surgical pathology; no survival or watch-and-wait outcomes
validation_detail: ARPAM-US model: patient-level 5-fold CV within one single-center prospective cohort (n=25, 3 pCR); MRI radiomics models separately tested on the prospective cohort as external test (n=19-24) after training on the retrospective cohort; no independent test of the ARPAM-US model
funding: NIH R01EB034398; Alvin J. Siteman Cancer Center institutional support
key_finding: Deep-learning ARPAM-US endoscopy identified pCR with CV AUC 0.956 in 25 prospective patients (3 pCR), while T2w MRI radiomics models lost accuracy on prospective testing (AUC 0.54-0.65).
limitations_as_stated: Very small cohort (25 patients, ~400 B-scans) with few pCRs; all patients proceeded to surgery; no external validation of ARPAM-US; MRI comparison confounded by different training paradigms, T2w only and domain shift; single-wavelength system.
other_models_outcomes: Late fusion ARPAM-US+MRI (Table 4): best PA+RFpost AUC 0.967 (0.92-1.00); PAUS+RFpost 0.967; RFdelta degraded to 0.51-0.72; MRI-only retrained on prospective cohort AUC about 0.5
extraction_note: Main model = ARPAM-US early-fusion ResNet50 (anchors title/abstract/conclusion). Data collected prospectively but ARPAM-US performance is internal CV only (validation_level=internal_cv); clinical_translation_stage coded research_only because the ARPAM-US model has internal CV only (data were collected prospectively; rule 13 ambiguity between prospective design and internal-only validation). Only 3 pCR in 25 patients; AUC CI upper bound capped at 1.000; 3 of 25 patients had no neoadjuvant treatment. n_analytic = 25 prospective + 119 retrospective MRI. Minor numeric inconsistencies in text (SVM 0.929 vs 0.925; fusion 0.967 vs 0.968). Code link is for the acquisition/annotation interface (ArpamGui), not the model; data 'available on request'. [Blind-QA adjudication 2026-10-07: n_analytic: 144 -> 25; code_availability: yes -> NR]

title: Radiomics analysis of restaging MRI for detection of pathological complete response in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer, histologically confirmed
data_source_detail: University of Pisa tertiary center, 2017-2022; 86 selected from 400 eligible patients; 3 MRI scanners (3T GE, 1.5T GE, 1.5T Siemens)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify pCR after neoadjuvant therapy to support treatment stratification, organ-preserving strategies (watch-and-wait) or intensification of non-responders
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant therapy (CT-RT 61.6%, short-course RT 19.8%, induction CT then CT-RT 16.3%, CT 1.2%, RT 1.2%), followed by surgery
data_modality_detail: Restaging (post-neoadjuvant) oblique axial T2-weighted MRI, manual tumor segmentation (ITK-SNAP), 107 PyRadiomics features
algorithm: z-score normalization, LASSO feature selection, logistic regression with Elastic Net regularization; hyperparameters by grid search
input_features: 107 radiomic features (first-order, shape, GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, NGTDM, GLDM) from restaging T2w MRI
comparator_detail: No comparator (only published studies discussed)
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (pCR) at surgery
performance_value: Repeated stratified 5-fold CV (20 repeats, 100 folds), mean: AUC 0.74; accuracy 67.4%; sensitivity 60.1%; specificity 71.0%
performance_source: Abstract; Results p.3 (Fig. 2 histograms)
validation_detail: Repeated stratified 5-fold CV x20; feature standardization, LASSO selection and tuning done within training folds; no external or holdout set
funding: European Union NextGenerationEU via Italian MUR PNRR (HEAL ITALIA, PE_00000019); some authors recipients
key_finding: Restaging-MRI radiomics model showed moderate discrimination for pCR (mean CV AUC 0.74, sensitivity 60%, specificity 71%), better at identifying non-responders.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single-center, small sample, no external validation; possible center-specific bias; no feature reproducibility/segmentation variability analysis; specific acquisition protocols limit applicability.

title: KRAS<sup>G12V/A146T</sup> mutations are associated with nCRT resistance via enhanced DNA double-strand break repair and support a deep learning prediction framework in LARC.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma treated with nCRT then TME
stage_detail: cT3-T4 and/or N+ on CT/MRI (all patients)
data_source_detail: Internal cohort: 115 patients, National Cancer Center/Cancer Hospital CAMS (WES n=67 tumor-blood pairs; H&E WSI n=106); external WES-only cohort: 22 published cases (Gu et al.; Lin et al.), no WSI. Plus in vitro (RKO, Caco-2) and mouse xenograft experiments
n_source: Methods 'Sample collection and grouping'; Results 'Patient cohort' (115 internal + 22 external)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Pretreatment prediction of response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for risk-adapted treatment selection and escalation/de-escalation; adjunct to MDT discussion

input_features: WES-derived mutations, mutational signatures and H&E WSI patches (M/S/P fusion)
comparator_detail: Unimodal models (M,S,P,U,B) and alternative fusion combinations (e.g., M+P) compared internally; no clinician or clinical-model comparator

performance_source: Results 'Development and evaluation of the fusion model' p.19; Fig. 3C-D; Abstract

The external patients lack WSI so the fusion model could not use P for them. Model selection among fusion combinations used test-set metrics (Supplementary Table S5) despite statement that test sets were not used for selection. Unimodal M/S model algorithms not described in text (S-tables). Exploratory mechanistic KRAS work is not a prediction model. title: Personalized neoadjuvant treatment regimen selection in locally advanced rectal cancer based on regimen-specific response modeling.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma
stage_detail: MRI-confirmed T3-4 or node-positive; training cohort cT3 ~55-94% / cT4 ~6-43%, cN0 6-41% by regimen (Table 1)
data_source_detail: Retrospective: West China Hospital, Sun Yat-sen Univ Cancer Center, Sixth Affiliated Hospital of SYSU (2015-2022; n=760); prospective non-interventional test cohort: West China, SYSUCC, Yunnan Cancer Hospital (2024-2025; n=95; ChiCTR2400085797)
n_source: Results 'Patient clinical characteristics' and Table 1 (760 retrospective + 95 prospective)

input_features: Pretreatment T2WI and ADC (10 central slices, tumor+mesorectum ROIs) plus clinical features (cT, cN, EMVI, CRM, LLNM, tumor location) and regimen encoding
comparator_detail: Clinical-only models (best LightGBM, AUC 0.584 validation / 0.639 test); also ablations/baselines (UNet, UNet-MoE, ResNet-2D/3D, PoE therapy selection)

performance_source: Table 2 (test cohort); Results 'Neoadjuvant therapy response prediction performance'; Abstract

validation_detail: Random split of 760 retrospective patients into training (618) and validation (142); independent prospective non-interventional test cohort (n=95, 3 centers incl. one new site), clinicians blinded to model output; IPTW sensitivity analysis
funding: National Key R&D Program of China (2024YFF1207400); NSFC (62333022, 92359302, 92259301, 62576361); Beijing NSF (JQ23034); Shaanxi NSF; Sichuan S&T Support Project; China Postdoctoral Science Foundation; Fundamental Research Funds for Central Universities. Funders had no role in the study

limitations_as_stated: Non-randomized real-world allocation, counterfactual estimates unobserved and hypothesis-generating, residual confounding; immunotherapy/MSI-H not modeled; nCT patients from a single center; no dynamic response information; no multimodal (WSI, genomics) inputs; need prospective randomized validation.
other_models_outcomes: Per-regimen AUC of UNet-MoE-Cli: TNT 0.804, nCRT 0.820, nCT 0.748; ablations UNet AUC 0.730/0.650, UNet-MoE 0.755/0.702 (validation/test); model-supported escalation 53.16% and de-intensification 5.91% of combined validation+test

Study design coded retrospective_cohort because 760/855 patients are retrospective, with a prospective registered test cohort captured in validation_level. Validation cohort (n=142) is a random split, so not counted in n_test. Per-regimen AUC cohort not explicitly stated. Image model with clinical variables kept as radiology_imaging (rule 9). title: Integrating CT-Based Radiomics Analysis With Serum CEA Level to Predict Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy Response in Colorectal Cancer.

title: Automated deep learning model for predicting pathological complete response in rectal cancer: A tool to organ-preserving strategies.

comparator_detail: No comparator model or clinician reading

title: Prediction of tumor regression grading in rectal cancer neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy: a habitat radiomics analysis of imaging biomarker.

title: Transformer-based Siamese multimodal imaging model for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.

title: Variant-to-Biomarker Integration and Mechanistic Validation Identify CES1 as a Copy Number-Linked Predictor of Radiotherapy Response in Rectal Cancer.

treatment_context: Neoadjuvant radiotherapy/chemoradiotherapy for rectal cancer

Clinical details (sample type, treatment regimen, response definition per GEO cohort) minimal; response labels merged from responder/complete/partial. title: Exploring Machine Learning Approaches for Decision Support in Neoadjuvant Therapy of Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.

The two models are fit separately per treatment arm and do not estimate a treatment effect; decision framing (whether to add CT) coded as neoadjuvant_response because the target is downstaging. title: Interpretable machine learning models based on CT radiomics for predicting chemoradiotherapy response in rectal cancer.

External cohort has 40.8% responders vs ~21-22% in training/internal (Table 1); text labels this rate as pCR although response is defined as TRG 0-1. Selection of XGBoost as best by training AUC. Table 3 sensitivity/specificity layout is garbled in text extraction; combined-model values read as listed.

title: Interpretable Artificial Intelligence in Assisting Treatment Response Prediction for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer After Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy: A Prospective, Multicenter, Human-Model Interaction Study.
journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer, cT3-4 or node-positive, non-metastatic
stage_detail: cT3-T4 or N+ non-metastatic LARC treated with neoadjuvant chemo(radio)therapy then TME
data_source_detail: Retrospective cohort 2010-2018 from 2 tertiary institutions (n=823; random split 575/248); prospective consecutive cohort 2020-2023 from the same 2 institutions (n=207; NCT04278274)
n_source: Abstract; Results Patient characteristics (823 retrospective + 207 prospective)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Preoperative pCR assessment after neoadjuvant therapy to support anorectal organ preservation and individualised therapy
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with or without radiotherapy (post-treatment, pre-TME MRI)
data_modality_detail: Post-neoadjuvant/pre-TME multiparametric MRI (T2WI, DWI, DCE) radiomics; cT, cN, pre- and post-treatment CEA added to the model (authors call it multimodality)
algorithm: RAPIDS-II: Deep Residual Shrinkage Network on 19 selected radiomic features (Radscore) integrated with clinicopathological factors by XGBoost; SHAP
input_features: Radscore (944 PyRadiomics features per sequence -> 19 selected), cT, cN, pre-CEA, post-CEA
comparator_detail: Six radiologists (junior 3, senior 3) visual assessment alone and with RAPIDS-II assistance; DRSN-only and single-sequence radiomics models

performance_source: Abstract; Results RAPIDS-II performance in prospective validation; Table 2
patient_outcomes_detail: In the retrospective cohort (n=823, median follow-up 40 mo) predicted pCR associated with better OS (P=0.0031), DFS, LRFS and DMFS (all P<0.0001)

funding: National Key R&D Program of China; National Science Fund for Distinguished Young Scholars (82225040); Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province; National Science Fund for Outstanding Young Scholars (82122057); NSFC (82302307); National Postdoctoral Program for Innovative Talents
key_finding: Post-neoadjuvant MRI radiomics (DRSN Radscore) plus CEA and cT/cN gave prospective AUC 0.795 for pCR; model assistance improved radiologists AUC and sensitivity, especially junior readers.

extraction_note: Prospective validation was run at the same 2 institutions that contributed the retrospective development cohort (not independent sites). Human-model interaction changed radiologists diagnostic calls (diagnostic performance), not documented treatment decisions or patient outcomes, so validation_level coded prospective rather than decision_impact. Uses post-treatment MRI (not baseline prediction). Clinical variables added to MRI model so coded radiology_imaging per rule 9 although authors say multimodality. Axis tox_surg inherited. Prospective-cohort Table 2 values read from layout mode. Abstract says RAPIDS-II AUC "comparable" to DRSN in testing set (P=0.020).

title: Integrative analysis of transcriptomic data reveals a predictive gene signature for chemoradiotherapy response in rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer, pre-treatment biopsies
stage_detail: LARC (stage II-III per introduction) treated with nCRT; TNM/cT/cN annotation inconsistent or absent in GEO datasets
country: Switzerland (in-house GeoMx cohort); public GEO cohorts NR

n_source: STAR Methods (Differential gene expression: 226 samples retained from 266; 338 identified); in-house GeoMx n=53 and external Domingo n=NR additional

treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (regimens heterogeneous across datasets)
data_modality_detail: Bulk gene expression (microarray and RNA-seq) from GEO pre-treatment biopsies; GeoMx spatial transcriptomics (tumor/stroma) for in-house cohort
algorithm: 186-gene signature fed to glmnet (L2-regularized logistic regression) and Random Forest; limma DEA in cross-validation loop for feature selection
input_features: 186 genes selected by differential expression (intersection of 6- and 4-dataset analyses)
comparator_detail: glmnet vs Random Forest; correlation compared with 10 published signatures (not performance comparison)
primary_outcome: Responder vs non-responder to nCRT (pathologic TRG; mid-responders excluded)
performance_value: 5-fold CV on pooled six datasets (n=226): AUC 0.80 for both glmnet and Random Forest (no CI/SD in text); external Domingo et al. dataset AUC 0.62; in-house GeoMx pseudo-bulk (n=53) random forest AUC 0.6071
performance_source: Results: Evaluating performance on an external dataset (Figure S3); CV AUC 0.80 in Results and Figures 1C/1D
validation_detail: 5-fold CV on six pooled GEO datasets; external validation on Domingo et al. 2024 microarray dataset (AUC 0.62, no batch correction) and on in-house GeoMx pseudo-bulk (AUC 0.61)

Headline CV AUC 0.80 is in-sample-cohort cross-validation; per rule 4 the most demanding reported cohort (external Domingo, AUC 0.62, n not reported) is coded as primary metric, with CV 0.80 in performance_value. The 186 genes were selected by averaging DEA p-values over CV runs and intersecting two analyses on the full pooled set before the 5-fold ML CV, which may leak information into CV performance. n_analytic counts the 226 samples used for modeling (266 after filtering, 338 identified); external and GeoMx cohorts additional. Stage not annotated in datasets; coded from LARC setting.

title: A noninvasive AI model based on multi-dimensional MRI features for predicting tertiary lymphoid structures, immunotherapy response, and prognosis in rectal cancer.

comparator_detail: AdaBoost and LightGBM; models with radiomics alone and radiomics + matrix features

Therapeutic decision coded immunotherapy_msi_selection because the stated clinical use is selecting immunotherapy; no MSI/dMMR status reported. title: Integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomes identifies B cell features associated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy sensitivity in rectal cancer.

title: MR-DELTAnet: A Longitudinal MRI-Transformer Model Predicting Pathological Complete Response and Revealing Immune Microenvironment via scRNA-seq in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer

title: A comprehensive feature importance analysis of surgical site infection following colorectal cancer surgery.

Funding and COI sections not found in PDF text. Response label mixes pCR, cCR and nCR (clinical, radiological, pathological). [Recoded other -> discovery_no_decision after validator vocabulary fix.]

title: Deep Learning-Based Multimodal Prediction of NAC Response in LARC by Integrating MRI and Proteomics.

stage_detail: LARC treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy; cTNM not reported
data_source_detail: Harbin Medical University Cancer Hospital, Jan 2012-Dec 2021; 274 patients (91 with MRI+proteomics, 175 MRI only, 8 proteomics only)

treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (capecitabine 89.8%, 5-FU 7.7%, both 2.5%) without radiotherapy
data_modality_detail: Pretreatment T2-weighted MRI (3D VOI 128^3) + FFPE tissue proteomics (4D-DIA) + clinical features (age, sex, tumor diameter, anal distance); zero-imputation for missing modality

comparator_detail: MRI-only, proteomics-only (full and 10-protein) models; ablation without clinical variables (test AUC 0.781)

Test set n=16 only (very wide CI); n_test=16 and validation set 16 separate. Text says model exceeded 0.80 in calibration but no calibration curve shown, coded no. Of 91 patients with both modalities only 32 used for validation/test.

title: Predicting near-complete pathological response to (chemo)radiotherapy in patients with rectal cancer: A federated learning study.

Main-text discussion cites expert+data AUC 0.71 vs Table 2 0.72 (Table value used). Docker image and R code public repository (code yes); no patient data shared. Pathology outcome (post-treatment) with some M1 patients in cohort.

title: Inclusion of tumor periphery in radiomics analysis of magnetic resonance images does not improve predictions of preoperative therapy response in patients with rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Primary non-metastasized rectal adenocarcinoma, locally advanced

NAR score AUC cROI+T2w+DWI 0.84 vs wROI 0.66/0.69 and cROI+T2w 0.73; recurrence AUC 0.69-0.71. Pooled LASSO+LR pCR accuracy 0.85, sensitivity 0.82, precision 0.84

algorithm: SRADL: SVM ensemble of sub-regional radiomics signature (PyRadiomics, K-means subregions, LASSO) and 3D ResNet50 deep-learning signature (LASSO-selected features, SVM)

comparator_detail: Radiomics, sub-regional radiomics, deep learning single signatures and RADL ensemble (DeLong, NRI, IDI)

Two external cohorts; test 1 chosen as headline (larger, listed first in abstract); test 2 AUC in performance_value. Heterogeneous scanners/protocols across centers. Data available on reasonable request (statement present).

title: A Machine Learning Model Based on MRI Radiomics to Predict Response to Chemoradiation Among Patients with Rectal Cancer.

stage_detail: Baseline cTNM stage II or III; nCRT 50.4 Gy with 5-FU or capecitabine then TME
data_source_detail: University of Padova, 1 Jan 2016-31 Dec 2022; substudy of a large prospective study; 102 of 174 eligible patients after imaging exclusions
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR to preoperative chemoradiotherapy from staging MRI to identify candidates for rectal-sparing approaches (watch and wait, local excision)
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pretreatment high-resolution axial oblique T2-weighted MRI, 802 IBSI radiomic features (Trace4Research)
algorithm: Ensemble of random forest classifiers (best of RF, SVM, kNN ensembles) with PCA/FDR/Gini; ADASYN oversampling; nested 10-fold CV
input_features: 6 selected radiomic features from T2W VOI
comparator_detail: Random forest vs SVM vs kNN ensembles (SVM internal-test AUC 0.69, kNN 0.51)
primary_outcome: pCR vs non-responding (residual disease) at TME
performance_value: RF ensemble nested-CV: training AUC 1.00, validation 0.74 (72-77), internal test 0.73 (0.65-0.81); internal test accuracy 70, sensitivity 78, specificity 48, PPV 80, NPV 46. performance_source: Abstract; Table 1A (internal testing mean); Results text for 30-patient cohort

funding: No external funding

Authors affiliated with DeepTrace Technologies (platform vendor) but declare no conflicts. Study states STARD followed. [Blind-QA adjudication 2026-10-07: performance_metric: AUC -> accuracy; primary_metric_value: 0.73 -> 80; performance_cohort: cross_validation -> internal_test; n_performance: 72 -> 30; primary_metric_ci_low: 0.65 -> NR; primary_metric_ci_high: 0.81 -> NR]

title: Combined transrectal ultrasound and radiomics model for evaluating the therapeutic effects of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Biopsy-confirmed solitary rectal cancer, locally advanced
stage_detail: LARC clinical stage II (T3-4N0M0) or III (T1-4N1-2M0); distant metastasis excluded
data_source_detail: West China Hospital, Jan 2017-Dec 2022; 190 of 478 LARC patients; 3128 TRUS images after screening (two ultrasound systems)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict tumor regression grade after NCRT (good vs poor response) to allow watch-and-wait for pCR and personalize treatment
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pre- and post-NCRT transrectal ultrasound (2D radiomics plus conventional/CEUS ultrasound parameters); single imaging family
algorithm: Combined model: multi-parameter ultrasound logistic regression (MPU-LR) + pre-NCRT RF radiomics + post-NCRT autoencoder radiomics (FeAture Explorer, PCA, RFE), nomogram
input_features: 8 TRUS parameters (4 independent in MPU-LR: PSVpre, CEUS-IGpost, LD change rate, RI change rate) plus pre- and post-NCRT radiomics scores
comparator_detail: MPU-LR, single TRUS parameters, pre-NCRT and post-NCRT radiomics models, US-RADpre and US-RADpost combinations (DeLong)
primary_outcome: Good (TRG 0-1, n=53) vs poor (TRG 2-3, n=137) response by AJCC 7th TRG
performance_value: Combined US-RADpre-RADpost AUC 0.913, accuracy 0.863 (evaluation cohort not specified, no CI); US-RADpre 0.877; US-RADpost 0.902; MPU-LR AUC 0.851 (0.792-0.909), acc 0.816, sens 0.566, spec 0.912; RADpre RF CV 0.601/test 0.740; RADpost AE CV 0.662/test 0.602 (Table 8)
performance_source: Abstract; Results Combined model; Fig. 6a; Table 9

limitations_as_stated: Small sample and image-level heterogeneity from two ultrasound systems; overfitting/model complexity and class imbalance; retrospective, NCRT regimen differences not considered; single center, multicenter study planned
other_models_outcomes: See performance_value; all other models in comparison
extraction_note: Evaluation cohort of the combined model (AUC 0.913) is not stated; images (n=3128) were randomly split 7:3 at image level, so same-patient images may appear in train and test (not stated otherwise). Model uses post-NCRT TRUS, so it is not a pre-treatment predictor. Coded validation_level=none because no independent test of the combined model/MPU-LR is described. Stated reporting guideline STROBE (coded other). Data statement: no datasets generated or analysed.

title: Computed Tomography Scan and Clinical-based Complete Response Prediction in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer after Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy: A Machine Learning Approach.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal adenocarcinoma, AJCC stage II-III, planned nCRT then surgery
stage_detail: AJCC stage II and III; clinical T2 44%, T3 44%, T4 12%; nCRT 50.4 Gy + capecitabine then resection 6-8 weeks later
data_source_detail: Radiation oncology clinic patients 2019-2021 (Babol University of Medical Sciences); 68 referred, 18 excluded, 50 analysed
n_source: Abstract; Materials and Methods Patient series

treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (capecitabine) followed by surgical resection
data_modality_detail: Pretreatment radiotherapy-planning CT radiomics (PyRadiomics, 851 features); 7 clinical/pathological variables added to the model (clinical variables do not make it multimodal per rule 9)
algorithm: Random forest on mRMR-selected features, three-class (no/partial/complete response); oversampling; best of 100 random 70/30 splits retained
input_features: Top 10 mRMR CT radiomic features + 7 clinical/pathological features (initial T and N, sex, tumor grade, LVI, PNI, age)
comparator_detail: Clinical features only and radiomics features only RF models
primary_outcome: Complete response (pCR) vs partial vs no response after nCRT (three-class); 8 complete, 34 partial, 8 no response
performance_value: All-features RF AUC (Table 2): complete response 0.99, no response 0.97, partial response 0.90; complete response sens 0.87, spec 0.95, PPV 0.87, NPV 1.00, F1 0.87. Radiomics alone AUC 0.99/0.94/0.83 (complete/no/partial); clinical alone 0.80/0.74/0.33; accuracy about 80%
performance_source: Abstract; Table 2; Fig. 5

limitations_as_stated: Small sample (50 patients); more reliable data require larger samples
other_models_outcomes: Radiomics-only and clinical-only RF models (see performance_value)
extraction_note: Design (retrospective vs prospective) not stated, coded other. Clinical features include surgical pathology data (pT, pN, grade, LVI, PNI) described as inputs, i.e. not all available pre-treatment; oversampling (duplicating patients) applied before the train/test split and best model chosen over 100 splits (possible optimism/leakage, stated factually). Test set size derived as 30% of 50 (n=15, only about 2 complete responders); exact test n not reported. Primary metric = complete-response class AUC from three-class task (rule 4). Abstract says "disturbed forest" for random forest.

title: Pathomics-based machine learning models for predicting pathological complete response and prognosis in locally advanced rectal cancer patients post-neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy: insights from two independent institutional studies.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma
stage_detail: Clinical stage II-III (cT3/4 or cN1/2) by MRI; cT2 present in few (Table 1)
data_source_detail: Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (training, 244 pts, 2012-2018); First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University (external test, 50 pts, 2020-2022)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR and DFS after NCRT to formulate effective treatment plans / personalised strategies and organ preservation
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (long-course CAPE/CAPOX or short-course RT + CAPOX) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pre-NCRT biopsy H&E: one 1000x1000 px field at x400 per patient; 684 CellProfiler pathomics features (663 after QC); clinical variables only in the separate DFS Cox/nomogram
algorithm: XGBoost (best of LR, Elasticnet, RF, XGB, stacking) on LASSO-selected features
input_features: 47 LASSO-selected CellProfiler pathomics features
comparator_detail: LR, Elasticnet, RF, stacking models; nomogram vs XGB for DFS
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (pCR) after NCRT
performance_value: XGB pCR AUC: internal/training 1.000 (CI 0.999-1.000); external 0.908 (CI 0.815-1.000). Other models external: LR 0.571, Elasticnet 0.551, RF 0.600, stack 0.536. DFS nomogram C-index internal 0.721 (0.656-0.786), external 0.658 (0.591-0.725)

validation_detail: Training set 244 (no CV or holdout reported; training AUC 1.000); one external retrospective center n=50 (8 pCR)
funding: Fujian Medical University startup fund; Fujian provincial health and finance funds; hospital talent program
key_finding: Pathomics XGB model predicted pCR (external AUC 0.908, n=50) and stratified DFS in the training center; prognostic separation not significant in external set

other_models_outcomes: Internal AUC: LR 0.940, Elasticnet 0.923, RF 1.000, stack 1.000; DFS Cox nomogram (tumor length, post-NCRT CEA, XGB score) with time-dependent AUC higher than XGB alone

Abstract/Discussion also vary on DFS p (0.074 vs 0.072) and 2- vs 3-year DFS. Training AUC 1.000 for RF/XGB/stack with no internal validation; training metrics are resubstitution. title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Volumetric Analysis of Muscle Mass as a Predictor of Tumor Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Patients with Rectal Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal cancer within 15 cm of anal verge treated with nCRT then curative resection
stage_detail: cStage I 5, II 23, III 58 (AJCC 8th); nCRT candidates per MDT; stage IV excluded
data_source_detail: Hallym University Sacred Heart Hospital, Mar 2010-Aug 2021 (127 screened, 86 included)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict nCRT response (good vs poor, MRI T/N downstaging) from pre-nCRT volumetric sarcopenia; prognosis by SMI change
treatment_context: nCRT 50.4 Gy/28 fx with fluorouracil-based chemotherapy, then surgery 6-8 weeks later
data_modality_detail: Pre- and post-nCRT abdominopelvic CT; AI-derived volumetric skeletal muscle index (SMI) dichotomised at sample Q1 (sarcopenia)
algorithm: Commercial DeepCatch v1.3.0 3D U-Net body-composition segmentation (radiologist-adjusted) -> volumetric SMI -> logistic regression (response) and Cox (RFS/OS)
input_features: Volumetric SMI (sarcopenia yes/no, Q1 cutoff), SMI change (>5% gain/stable/loss), age, sex, cStage, CEA
primary_outcome: nCRT response (good = T or N downstaging on MRI vs poor = no change/worsening)
performance_value: Multivariate OR for good response, sarcopenia vs non-sarcopenia: 0.34 (95% CI 0.12-0.96; p=0.041); univariate OR 0.35 (0.13-0.95). Good response 45.5% vs 70.3% (p=0.043). No discrimination metric (AUC) reported
performance_source: Abstract; Table 2 (multivariate); Results 3.2
patient_outcomes_detail: SMI loss during nCRT associated with worse RFS (aHR gain vs loss 0.26, 0.08-0.83) and OS (aHR 0.41, 0.17-0.99); pre-nCRT sarcopenia not prognostic
validation_detail: Association analysis in the whole single-center cohort (n=86); no split, CV or external data; AI segmentation software itself previously validated (97% vs manual, cited)
funding: Hallym University Research Fund 2020 (HURF-2020-39)
key_finding: AI-measured pre-nCRT volumetric sarcopenia was associated with poor nCRT response (multivariate OR 0.34); SMI reduction during nCRT was prognostic for RFS and OS
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective, selection bias, unmeasured confounders (nutrition, comorbidity); small single-center sample (n=86); mechanisms not elucidated; no comparison with single-slice L3 method
other_models_outcomes: Cox models for RFS and OS by SMI change (Table 3); pre-nCRT sarcopenia not associated with RFS (HR 0.83) or OS (HR 1.42)
extraction_note: AI is used only for CT muscle segmentation (commercial 3D U-Net); the "prediction" is a logistic regression association with OR as headline metric (performance_metric=other, cohort=train as apparent whole-sample estimate). stage_context coded locally_advanced_rectal although cStage I (n=5) included. Q1 cutoff derived from the study sample itself.

title: Prediction of T Stage of Rectal Cancer After Neoadjuvant Therapy by Multi-Parameter Magnetic Resonance Radiomics Based on Machine Learning Algorithms.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy then TME
stage_detail: Baseline clinical T2 5, T3 75, T4 91; cN0 38, cN1 64, cN2 69 (Table 1; counts summed from low/high pT groups)

key_finding: Fusion LR model combining T2WI and CE-T1WI radiomics with clinical features best predicted post-neoadjuvant pT stage (test AUC 0.932, n=34)
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective, modest sample, selection bias; manual ROI segmentation; no pathology/genomic data; deep learning not compared
other_models_outcomes: Clinical LightGBM train/test AUC 0.857-0.858/0.702; T2WI SVM 0.969/0.839; CE-T1WI SVM 0.868/0.760 (text); DeLong: fusion superior to clinical in test cohort only
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: Table 2 lists CE-T1WI as LR (train AUC 0.928, test 0.736) whereas abstract/text report CE-T1WI SVM (0.868/0.760); T2WI row in Table 2 labelled SVM. Table 2 value used for fusion. Target is ypT stage (T0-2 vs T3-4), not pCR. Test set of 34 also used for algorithm selection; performance on test cohort should be read as optimistic.

title: CLIP-based multimodal endorectal ultrasound enhances prediction of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy response in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer (uT3-4 on ERUS) treated with nCRT then surgery
data_source_detail: Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, Jan 2018-Dec 2023
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict TRG (good TRG0 vs poor TRG1-3) before nCRT to tailor treatment and identify poor responders for early plan adjustment
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by TME

RN50 chosen as principal (abstract first, highest AUC). IRB-restricted images/text; extracted feature data in supplementary xlsx.

title: ResNet-Vision Transformer based MRI-endoscopy fusion model for predicting treatment response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer: A multicenter study.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma
stage_detail: cT3-4 or any cT with cN1-2 by MRI, no distant metastasis (some cT1-2/cN0 in Table 1)

therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict response (good = TRG 0-1) to nCRT to provide personalised treatment / select appropriate nCRT candidates

extraction_note: Good response defined as TRG 0-1 (not pCR). n_test = 57 internal temporal + 129 external; n_performance = 129 external. Sample-size/power calculation and selection of external patients are in supplementary methods (not used). No data or code availability statement found in main text.

title: Exploring Intratumoral Budding in Colorectal Cancer Using Computational Pathology: A Biopsy-Based Evaluation.
tumor_site_detail: Test cohort: colorectal cancer (555, surgery without neoadjuvant therapy); validation cohort: 285 rectal cancers after long-course nCRT
stage_detail: Test cohort clinical stage I-IV (Table 1); validation cohort rectal cancer receiving preoperative chemoradiotherapy (cTNM from records, not tabulated in text)
data_source_detail: Test: Radboudumc 2010-2020 (555). Validation: Radboudumc 114, St Vincent's Dublin 96, RAPIDO trial standard arm 59, Erasmus MC 16 (2003-2022)
n_source: Abstract; Materials and Methods "Patients" (555 test + 285 validation)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Value of biopsy tumor budding to predict response to neoadjuvant therapy (pCR, downstaging) and prognosis
treatment_context: Long-course preoperative chemoradiotherapy for rectal cancer
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide images of diagnostic biopsies and resections; AI-detected tumor buds (counts per hotspot; present vs absent in biopsy)
algorithm: In-house CNN tumor-budding detection algorithm (epithelium segmentation + nuclear detection; previously published, not trained here) followed by logistic/Cox regression
input_features: Biopsy tumor bud count (budders vs non-budders, TB>0); Bd grades in resections; gender and clinical stage as covariates
comparator_detail: Peritumoral budding (PTB) vs intratumoral budding compared for prognosis in resections

performance_source: Abstract; Results "Incidence and Clinical Relevance of Tumor Budding in Rectal Biopsies" (logistic regression for pCR)

funding: KWF Program Grant (KWF 2016-2-10602)
key_finding: AI-detected tumor budding in rectal biopsies was associated with lower odds of pCR (adjusted OR 0.3) and worse OS; superficial intratumoral buds predicted final budding grade

title: Is an Electronic Nose Able to Predict Clinical Response following Neoadjuvant Treatment of Rectal Cancer? A Prospective Pilot Study.
tumor_site_detail: Intermediate- or high-risk rectal cancer scheduled for neoadjuvant scRT or CRT
stage_detail: Intermediate risk (cT1-3 MRF-, N1) or high risk (cT4, MRF+, cN2, extramesorectal nodes and/or EMVI); synchronous metastases excluded

therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict response to neoadjuvant therapy (partial vs (near) complete clinical response) to improve selection for watch-and-wait

data_modality_detail: Exhaled-breath volatile organic compounds measured with Aeonose eNose sensor array (breath test)

input_features: eNose sensor signals of breath VOC pattern
primary_outcome: Clinical response at multidisciplinary-board evaluation: partial vs (near) complete response

performance_source: Abstract; Results 3.3 and Table 2
validation_detail: Model trained on first breath tests (group A) vs controls (group B) for cancer detection; the response-prediction "test set" is the second breath test of the same 45 group-A patients; no internal validation/overfitting correction of the training set
funding: Partly European Regional Development Fund (PROJ00913) for first author; eNose devices, software, filters supplied free by The eNose Company

extraction_note: Model is trained on a different task (rectal cancer present vs treated controls) and then applied to post-treatment breath tests of the same group-A patients whose pre-treatment tests are in the training set, so the test set is not independent of the training patients; coded internal_holdout. Reference standard is MDT clinical response, not pathology.

title: Computed Tomography-Based Radiomics with Machine Learning Outperforms Radiologist Assessment in Estimating Colorectal Liver Metastases Pathologic Response After Chemotherapy.

data_source_detail: MSKCC prospectively maintained liver resection database, 2003-2012
n_source: Abstract/Results: 85 patients with 95 tumors (analysis at tumor level)

title: Identification and validation of a machine learning model of complete response to radiation in rectal cancer reveals immune infiltrate and TGFβ as key predictors.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal cancer treated with neoadjuvant long-course CRT

therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify patients likely to achieve pCR to CRT to select a primary radiotherapy/organ-preserving approach, and radioresistant patients for trials
treatment_context: Pelvic RT 45-50.4 Gy/25 fx with capecitabine or 5-FU (validation 50.4 Gy/28 fx with infusional 5-FU)

title: Preoperative MRI radiomic analysis for predicting local tumor progression in colorectal liver metastases before microwave ablation.

stage_detail: Oligometastatic CRC, <=10 CLM, treated with microwave ablation (86% combined with resection)
data_source_detail: IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital, institutional prospectively collected MWA database reviewed retrospectively, Sep 2015-Feb 2022
n_source: Abstract; Results (43 patients, 76 CLM lesions analyzed independently)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict local tumor progression after microwave ablation of CLM; potential add-on to address therapeutic options when considering local therapy of oligometastatic disease
treatment_context: Microwave ablation (alone or with surgical resection) of colorectal liver metastases
data_modality_detail: Pre-procedural gadoxetic acid MRI (T1-HBP and T2) radiomics (182 IBSI features, manual segmentation); combined models add clinical variables (ablation margin, TRG), not a multimodal input per rule 9

primary_outcome: Local tumor progression-free survival after MWA
performance_value: Apparent (original dataset): COMB-T1 AUC 0.98 (p=0.0001); COMB-T2 0.95; CLIN-mod 0.89; RAD-T1 0.83; RAD-T2 0.79. Bootstrap internal validation in Supplementary Tables S1-S3 (not available)
performance_source: Abstract; Results (Multivariate analysis), Figure 1, Table 3

Bootstrap-validated CIs only in Supplementary Tables S1-S3 (not available), so CI NR. Reported performance is apparent, tuned on same data (selection among all variable combinations on the full dataset). Intra-segment progression (in CLIN-mod) is observed during follow-up and cannot act as a baseline predictor, per authors. Decision coded other: ablation-site progression, not systemic therapy. ai_family statistical_model despite ML-based bootstrap ranking for variable selection (final models Cox).

title: Assessing Endoscopic Response in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Treated with Total Neoadjuvant Therapy: Development and Validation of a Highly Accurate Convolutional Neural Network.

stage_detail: Stage II/III rectal adenocarcinoma treated with total neoadjuvant therapy (T3 82.3%, cN+ 85.1%)

title: Unraveling variations and enhancing prediction of successful sphincter-preserving resection for low rectal cancer: a post hoc analysis of the multicentre LASRE randomized clinical trial.

title: Image-based consensus molecular subtyping in rectal cancer biopsies and response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.

primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (pCR) after NAT
performance_value: AUC 0.72 training (n=132); 0.60 validation (n=82)
performance_source: Results p.1288 text; Fig. 1 (95% CIs only in figure, not in text)
patient_outcomes_detail: Association of BC with pCR only; no survival outcomes
validation_detail: Random 60:40 split of single-center cohort into training (model selection) and validation; bootstrap CIs (10000)
funding: NR
key_finding: AI-measured 3D SM volume and age were positively and SCF volume negatively associated with pCR; model AUC 0.72 training vs 0.60 validation.

title: A deep neural network predictor to predict the sensitivity of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer
stage_detail: cT2-4, N0-N+ (AJCC 7th) in in-house cohort; LARC defined as T3-4 or node-positive
data_source_detail: In-house RNA-seq (Cancer Hospital CAMS, 71 LARC pts, 2010-2019) + public GEO cohorts GSE209746 and GSE46862 for validation; TCGA/GEO for pathway/survival analyses
n_source: Methods 2.1/Results 3.1 (in-house n=71); external GSE46862 n=23 (Methods 2.5); GSE209746 size not given in text
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict NCRT sensitivity (pCR vs incomplete response) to guide clinical treatment in LARC
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant long-course chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy/25 fx + capecitabine) then TME
data_modality_detail: Tumor RNA-seq; 18-gene signature selected from 428 Wnt/LA-pathway-correlated genes
algorithm: Deep neural network (H2O deeplearning; 18-9-4-2 dense layers, tanh, cross-entropy + L1); features selected by overlap of LASSO, SVM, RF and XGBoost; SMOTE oversampling
input_features: Expression of 18 genes
primary_outcome: pCR vs incomplete response (iCR) to NCRT
performance_value: AUC 0.999 training (n=70); 0.906 internal test (n=32; sens 84.21, spec 92.86, acc 93.75); 0.897 GSE209746 (external, n NR); 0.706 GSE46862 (external, n=23); 0.75 TCGA radiotherapy-only (n=5); 0.667 GSE209746 chemotherapy-only
performance_source: Results 3.5 p.6; Fig. 4D-F; abstract (0.706 and 0.897)
patient_outcomes_detail: High-PI group had longer OS in in-house, GSE209746, GSE87211 and TCGA-READ (p<0.05)

funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81972318, 82073352); CAMS Non-profit Central Research Institute Fund (2019PT310027); Sanming Project of Medicine in Shenzhen; Hospital Research Project (E010121001)
key_finding: 18-gene DNN predicted NCRT sensitivity with AUC 0.906 internal and 0.706-0.897 in two external GEO cohorts; high-PI subtype had better OS and immune activation.
limitations_as_stated: RNA-seq cost; need larger/trial validation; need to incorporate clinical factors and MSI/RAS; 18-gene signature activity differed by response only in GSE209746 (small sample) and was not associated with response by logistic regression (Fig S8)
other_models_outcomes: Pathway-level logistic regression: Wnt/beta-catenin (OR 1.1, p=0.0033) and linoleic acid (p=0.0188) pathways associated with NCRT response; four immune/DNN subtypes
extraction_note: Two external cohorts without a declared headline: primary taken as GSE46862 AUC 0.706 (lower, more demanding, n=23 stated) per rule 2b; GSE209746 AUC 0.897 has no n in text. n_analytic=71 is the development cohort (external n not summable; 1274 transcriptomes used for pathway analyses). n_train/n_test counts include SMOTE-oversampled samples (102 = 70+32) and oversampling was applied before the train/test split (possible leakage inflating internal AUC 0.999/0.906). Data: RNA-seq deposited at NGDC PRJCA019248 under reasonable request; public datasets from GEO/Xena.

title: Digitally assessed lymphocyte infiltration in rectal cancer biopsies is associated with pathological response to neoadjuvant therapy.
tumor_site_detail: Primary rectal adenocarcinoma (non-mucinous), pMMR
stage_detail: All cT3-T4; cN0 10, cN1-2 40; cM1 16 of 50 (metastatic/advanced disease included)
data_source_detail: Slagelse and Koge Hospitals, Zealand University Hospital, surgery Mar 2018-Apr 2020; diagnostic biopsies; subgroup of a prior study

primary_outcome: Good (Mandard TRG 1-2) and complete (TRG 1) pathological response
performance_value: Univariate OR for good response: CD8+/CD3+ per 10 points 2.15 (1.19-4.41); CD8+ per 100/mm2 1.20 (1.01-1.46); CD3+ and ETP not significant. Complete response: CD3+ per 100/mm2 OR 1.11 (1.02-1.24); CD8+ OR 1.33 (1.10-1.70); CD8+/CD3+ per 10 points OR 2.19 (1.12-4.87). No AUC reported

patient_outcomes_detail: Only pathological response (TRG); no survival outcomes

funding: Carl and Ellen Hertz Scholarship, Lizzi and Mogens Staal Foundation, other Danish foundations and Region Zealand Health Research Foundation; funders had no role
conflicts_of_interest: HH and BR employed at Visiopharm A/S; other authors none
key_finding: Biopsy CD8+ density and CD8+/CD3+ percentage (digitally measured) were associated with good and complete pathological response; ETP was not.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample prevents multivariable analysis; retrospective design with selection bias; heterogeneous neoadjuvant regimens

extraction_note: Association/biomarker study (AI used to quantify features), not a prediction model: no discrimination metric; headline OR used as primary metric; performance_cohort NR (whole-cohort univariate analysis). Stage coded locally_advanced_rectal (all cT3-4) although 16 cM1 included. Setting: two hospitals of the same university hospital. Multiple response definitions; good-response OR chosen as main.

title: Feasibility of delta radiomics-based pCR prediction for rectal cancer patients treated with magnetic resonance-guided adaptive radiotherapy.

title: Radiomics of skeletal muscle helps to predict gastrointestinal toxicity in locally advanced rectal cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal adenocarcinoma <=12 cm from anal verge
stage_detail: cT3-4 and/or N+; some cT2N0 (stage I) rectum-preservation patients and resectable oligometastatic (stage IV) also allowed
data_source_detail: Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center; 164 pts Jul 2017-Aug 2019 (train/internal) and 50 pts Jan 2021-Aug 2022 (external)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict grade 3-4 gastrointestinal toxicity of neoadjuvant CRT with irinotecan to inform clinical decision-making
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant IMRT 50 Gy with capecitabine and weekly irinotecan (UGT1A1-guided)
data_modality_detail: Baseline non-contrast CT at L3: manually contoured skeletal muscle radiomics (253 features) plus SMI derived from the same CT
algorithm: LASSO feature selection (5-fold CV) then logistic regression (rad-score + SMI combined model)
input_features: SMI + 8 skeletal muscle radiomics features (9 nonzero LASSO features)
comparator_detail: SMI-alone model
primary_outcome: Grade 3-4 acute gastrointestinal toxicity (diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, proctitis; CTCAE v5)
performance_value: Combined model AUC 0.856 (0.782-0.929) training n=115; 0.812 (0.667-0.956) internal validation n=49; 0.745 (0.600-0.890) external/temporal n=50. SMI alone: 0.739, 0.741, 0.697. F1 combined 0.617/0.706/0.667
performance_source: Abstract; Results: Model performance in the training, internal and external validation sets; Fig. 2F

key_finding: Skeletal muscle radiomics plus SMI predicted grade 3-4 GI toxicity better than SMI alone (AUC 0.745 vs 0.697 in the later same-center cohort).
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective design; single institution, multi-institution validation needed; no molecular (UGT1A1) features; manual segmentation; hematologic toxicity model suboptimal
other_models_outcomes: SMI-alone model AUC 0.739/0.741/0.697; hematologic toxicity model had suboptimal discrimination (values not given); decision curve analysis shows net benefit over treat-all/none
extraction_note: Authors call the 2021-2022 cohort "external" but it is from the same institution: coded temporal / temporal_same_center. n_test=49+50=99 derived. Calibration not reported (DCA only).

title: Prediction of Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy Response in Rectal Cancer Patients Using Harmonized Radiomics of Multcenter <sup>18</sup>F-FDG-PET Image.

therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy response (pCR vs non-pCR) before treatment
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery

title: Lipid metabolism-associated genes serve as potential predictive biomarkers in neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy combined with immunotherapy in rectal cancer.

title: Prediction of Pathologic Complete Response for Rectal Cancer Based on Pretreatment Factors Using Machine Learning.

title: Multiphase and multiparameter MRI-based radiomics for prediction of tumor response to neoadjuvant therapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.

title: Attention mechanism based multi-sequence MRI fusion improves prediction of response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.

Country not stated (institution masked); Brazil inferred from text ("none conducted in Brazil") and author affiliations. Ymrtrg is a radiologist-read variable, so not coded multimodal.

Delta model needs post-NCRT MRI, so it informs response assessment after CRT, not pretreatment selection. Validation is a temporal split of 16 patients (two centers pooled), no CI. Data availability: 'included in article/supplementary material; further inquiries to corresponding authors' coded upon_request. Feature importance table = explainability yes. title: Automatic treatment outcome prediction with DeepInteg based on multimodal radiological images in rectal cancer.

title: MRI-Based Radiomic Models Outperform Radiologists in Predicting Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.

title: Interpretable machine learning for predicting pathologic complete response in patients treated with chemoradiation therapy for rectal adenocarcinoma.

Code on GitHub is only an example of feature extraction. Training data restricted (data-sharing regulations; request to corresponding author).

title: MRI-based radiomics to predict neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy outcomes in locally advanced rectal cancer: A multicenter study.

Four authors are affiliated with Blot Info & Tech (the radiomics platform company) while COI states none. Radiomic feature scales from eFigures/eTables not available in main text.

funding: No funds, grants or other support received (declared); part of larger AIRC-funded study per protocol description
key_finding: Pre-treatment T2 texture parameters (entropy, kurtosis) differed between pCR and non-pCR; a Weka decision tree combining all parameters was reported to identify pCR patients at baseline MRI, without validation or quantified accuracy.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample; no comparison with DWI/DCE; no standardized TA protocol; TA software not IBSI-compliant; no follow-up; decision tree accurate only in an identical population and needs validation
other_models_outcomes: Univariable ROC of individual TA parameters (non-ML): pre-treatment entropy AUC 0.64, kurtosis 0.56, MPP 0.57, skewness 0.57; filtered SF1 entropy 0.71, kurtosis 0.63, MPP 0.61; skewness SF2 0.65
extraction_note: The authors' AI component is the Weka decision tree, but no AUC/sensitivity/specificity is reported for it; the headline numbers in the abstract (kurtosis sens 81.5%/spec 61.5%) belong to univariable ROC on texture parameters, not the ML model, so primary metric coded NR (extraction_status partial). Data statement: data archived at the institutional electronic archive, not shared (coded no). Text of the PDF is partially duplicated/garbled in extraction; values taken from clean passages.

title: CT radiomics identifying non-responders to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy among patients with locally advanced rectal cancer.
