title: Are We There Yet? The Value of Deep Learning in a Multicenter Setting for Response Prediction of Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer
stage_detail: Pre-nCRT MRI cT2-T4 (mostly cT3), N+ in most of the training cohort (CAO-ARO-AIO-12 patients); test cohort cT2 8, cT3 38, N- 25 / N+ 21
data_source_detail: Training: CAO-ARO-AIO-12 trial MRI data from Centers 1-3 (Frankfurt, Regensburg, Wurzburg; n=72); validation: Center 4a Mannheim (trial, n=11); external test: Center 4b Mannheim clinical routine data 2009-2013 (n=46)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR after nCRT from pre- and post-therapeutic MRI, to identify candidates for a watch-and-wait strategy instead of surgical resection
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by TME (CAO-ARO-AIO-12 trial regimens; routine nCRT in the external set)
data_modality_detail: Pre- and post-nCRT T2-weighted MRI, DWI (b800) and ADC maps; tumor segmented on T2w
algorithm: Retrained multitask Siamese network of two U-Nets joined at multiple layers (approach of Jin et al.), five CV models
input_features: Pre- and post-therapeutic T2w images (configuration 1) or T2w + DW b800 + ADC maps (configuration 2)
comparator_detail: T2w-only versus T2w+DWI/ADC input configurations
primary_outcome: pCR (Dworak TRG4) vs non-pCR (TRG0-3)
performance_value: External test (Center 4b, n=46): T2w+DWI+ADC AUC 0.60 (95% CI 0.48-0.71); T2w only AUC 0.54 (0.41-0.65). Cross-validation (Centers 1-3, 5-fold average): T2w only AUC 0.68 (0.59-0.77); T2w+DWI+ADC AUC 0.43 (0.35-0.52)
performance_source: Abstract; Sec 3.4; Fig 3 and 4
validation_detail: 5-fold CV on Centers 1-3 (68/12/20 split); unseen Center 4a data and an independent clinical-routine dataset (Center 4b, Mannheim, outside training distribution) applied to the five trained networks
funding: Data storage service SDS@hd (MWK Baden-Wurttemberg and DFG, INST 35/1314-1 FUGG, INST 35/1503-1 FUGG); DFG grant 428149221
key_finding: A published multitask DL response-prediction network lost nearly all discrimination in a multicenter setting (external AUC 0.54-0.60), highlighting data heterogeneity and the need for harmonization.
limitations_as_stated: Difficult rigid registration (distortion, T2w-DWI misalignment); fewer inputs than the original model; pre-trained weights not shared by original authors; hyperparameters not optimized; small and heterogeneous dataset (15 scanners)
other_models_outcomes: Configuration comparison: T2w-only external AUC 0.54 and CV AUC 0.68; T2w+DWI+ADC external 0.60 and CV 0.43
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: Results text states external-dataset T2w+DWI AUC of 0.68 ('best results') while the abstract and Sec 3.4 give 0.60 (95% CI 0.48-0.71); the 0.60 value, consistent across abstract and results, was used. The two configurations are co-primary; T2w+DWI/ADC chosen as principal (best external AUC, rule 2b, and the abstract's higher value) although T2w-only was better in CV. Center 4a and 4b are both Mannheim; n_test = 11 (Center 4a) + 46 (Center 4b); n_analytic derived from Table 1 (abstract: 83 + 46). Model requires post-nCRT MRI so it informs restaging/watch-and-wait after CRT rather than pretreatment selection. A negative generalizability study.

title: Deep Learning Model for Predicting the Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy of Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.

therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR to nCRT from pretreatment biopsy H&E to assist clinical treatment decision making before surgery (nCRT choices; watch and wait mentioned in intro)

data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide images of pretreatment biopsies, tumor regions hand-annotated, 299x299 patches at 20x

input_features: Biopsy H&E patches (WSI-level aggregation)
comparator_detail: Patch-based individual and combined models (DeepPCR without clustering/MIL) and hematology MLP model (CEA, CA19-9, LDH, lymphocytes, neutrophils)
primary_outcome: pCR vs non-pCR (TRG-based) after nCRT
performance_source: Results (pCR Candidate Prediction in the External Validation Cohort); Table 2B

funding: Guangdong Science and Technology Project; Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province; National Science Fund for Excellent Young Scholars; Guangdong Natural Science Funds for Distinguished Young Scholars

extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: abstract reports 842 patients but cohort description/Table 1 sum to 885 (783 primary + 102 external); used 885. n_test=117 internal + 102 external. Tencent AI Lab co-authors (affiliation) while COI statement declares none.

title: Ability of Delta Radiomics to Predict a Complete Pathological Response in Patients with Loco-Regional Rectal Cancer Addressed to Neoadjuvant Chemo-Radiation and Surgery.
tumor_site_detail: Loco-regional rectal adenocarcinoma
stage_detail: cT2-cT4, cN0-cN2 (Table 2); localized disease at staging; long-course C-RT then TME
data_source_detail: Three radiation oncology units (2013-2019): training dataset (n=37) and validation datasets 1 (n=33) and 2 (n=30), each with a different MRI vendor/scanner
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR after C-RT from delta texture analysis of baseline and post-C-RT MRI, to select patients who may benefit from radical surgery or avoid surgery risk
treatment_context: Long-course neoadjuvant capecitabine-based chemoradiation (45 Gy + 9 Gy boost) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pelvic MRI (T2, DWI, ADC) at baseline and 30+/-15 days after C-RT; GTV contouring, LifeX texture features; delta = (T2-T1)/T1
algorithm: Univariate/multivariate binary logistic regression on delta texture (radiomic) features; final single predictor ADC GLCM Entropy with a cut-off (-0.10) from training
input_features: Delta texture features (GLCM, shape, histogram) from T2, DWI, ADC; sex, age, stage, grading tested
comparator_detail: NR
primary_outcome: Complete pathological response (TRG 1, Mandard)
performance_value: Training (n=37): AUC 0.87, sens 70%, spec 74%, acc 73%; Validation 1 (n=33): AUC 0.92, sens 100%, spec 66.7%, acc 72.7%; Validation 2 (n=30): AUC 0.88, sens 80%, spec 80%, acc 80% (training cut-off applied; AUCs from logistic regression refitted in each validation set)
performance_source: Results 3.3; Table 4; Abstract (CI/Table S4 in supplement)
patient_outcomes_detail: Follow-up described but no outcome analysis reported
validation_detail: Two validation datasets from different institutions/scanners; training cut-off applied for sens/spec/accuracy, but logistic regression was re-run (refit) in each validation set to obtain AUC
funding: APC funded by Fondazione SIRM
key_finding: Delta ADC GLCM Entropy predicted pCR with AUC 0.87 (training) and 0.92 and 0.88 in two validation datasets; small pilot (n=100, 21 pCR).

other_models_outcomes: Other delta features (DWI Volume, T2) tested; ADC GLCM Entropy only feature remaining in multivariate analysis (OR 0.14 training; 0.08 and 0.06 in validation sets)
extraction_note: Validation AUC derived from logistic regression refitted in each validation dataset (not a locked model); chose validation 2 (AUC 0.88, n=30) as most demanding/lowest; CI in Supplementary Table S4 not available. Abstract says 21 pCR of 100 (training 10, val1 6, val2 5). Each validation dataset treated as a separate institution (three institutions stated; site-to-dataset mapping not explicit). Delta features require post-C-RT MRI (restaging).

title: Analysis of MRI and CT-based radiomics features for personalized treatment in locally advanced rectal cancer and external validation of published radiomics models.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC)
stage_detail: UICC stage I-IV distribution reported incl. cT2-4 (Table 1); nCRT followed by surgery
data_source_detail: DKTK-ROG multicentre cohort: training = Dresden (94) + Munich (28); validation = Frankfurt (56) + Freiburg (12), 2006-2015

data_modality_detail: Pre-treatment T2w MRI + treatment-planning CT radiomics (GTV) combined with clinical T stage

input_features: LoG-filtered intensity features from MRI and CT plus clinical T stage (also MFO and SOT classes)
comparator_detail: Single-modality and feature-class signatures (MFO, SOT, LoG, All) and cT-only clinical model (AUC 0.60); published signatures re-tested in separate validation study
primary_outcome: Tumour response to nCRT (Dworak TRG 3-4 responders vs TRG 0-2)
performance_value: Joint MRI-LoG + CT-LoG + cT: external validation AUC 0.70 (0.54-0.84), final training AUC 0.72 (0.62-0.80); cT alone 0.60 (0.50-0.70) validation; threshold 0.248 classified 16/21 responders and 20/47 non-responders correctly
performance_source: Results, Table 2 (joint MRI_LoG + CT_LoG + cT row) and Discussion
patient_outcomes_detail: Second endpoint FFDM: CT-based SOT signature C-index 0.69 in validation with significant KM stratification (p<0.01)

funding: BMBF grant 03WKDB2D (academia-industry cooperation); Open Access by Projekt DEAL
conflicts_of_interest: Several authors disclose research funding from industry (e.g., Merck KGaA, AstraZeneca, Attomol, GA Generic Assays, Lipotype, PolyAn); senior author states no conflict for this paper

extraction_note: Dual-aim paper (modelling study + external validation of published models); modelling study treated as main per title/abstract and conclusion. Reporting guideline: IBSI cited for radiomics extraction (coded other). Table 2 layout scrambled in text; joint+cT row values read as final training 0.72, validation 0.70 (0.54-0.84), consistent with text AUC 0.70.

title: Combined artificial intelligence and radiologist model for predicting rectal cancer treatment response from magnetic resonance imaging: an external validation study.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer after neoadjuvant treatment (restaging MRI)
stage_detail: LARC; pathological ypT3 in 45% (MSK) and 52% (ICESP); ypN0 66% and 60%
data_source_detail: Internal: Memorial Sloan Kettering (n=114, 2012-2016); external: Instituto do Cancer do Estado de Sao Paulo (n=50, 2014-2015)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR on restaging MRI after neoadjuvant treatment to improve patient selection for non-surgical (watch-and-wait) management
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant treatment (chemoradiation) followed by TME; restaging MRI
data_modality_detail: Restaging T2W MRI radiomics (tumor bed, manual segmentation) fused by majority vote with radiologist qualitative rCR/rPR call
algorithm: Random forest (1000 trees, SMOTE, 5-fold x10 CV) models A (33 texture features) and B (91 features); late-fusion majority vote of model A + model B + radiologist (A+B+R1, A+B+R2)
input_features: Radiomic texture (Haralick, Gabor, first-order) and shape/GLRLM/GLSZM/NGTDM features; radiologist label for combined models
comparator_detail: Senior (R1) and junior (R2) radiologist qualitative assessment alone
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (pCR) vs pathological partial response
performance_value: External set (n=50, 8 pCR): Model A+B+R2 sens 50% (16-84), spec 93% (81-99), PPV 57%, NPV 91%; A+B+R1 sens 38%, spec 95% (84-99), PPV 60%, NPV 89%; R1 alone sens 38%, spec 98%, PPV 75%, NPV 89%; R2 alone sens 50%, spec 90%, PPV 50%, NPV 90%; Model A AUC 0.79 (0.62-0.96); Model B AUC 0.83 (0.70-0.97); inter-reader kappa 0.25 vs 0.82 with combined model
performance_source: Table 2 (A+B+R2 specificity), Table 3 (Models A and B AUC), Abstract
validation_detail: Trained with repeated 5-fold CV on MSK; applied unchanged to held-out single-site external cohort (ICESP, Brazil)
funding: NIH/NCI Cancer Center Support Grant P30 CA008748 (in part)
key_finding: Combined radiomics + radiologist model improved inter-reader agreement (kappa 0.82 vs 0.25) and slightly raised junior radiologist specificity/PPV/NPV in predicting pCR on restaging MRI; model B AUC 0.83 externally.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective; small internal and external samples (8 pCR externally); manual segmentation; DWI not included; lymph node response not assessed; lower sensitivity/PPV in external set
other_models_outcomes: Model A AUC 0.79 (0.62-0.96, sens 50%, spec 93%); Model B AUC 0.83 (0.70-0.97, sens 38%, spec 90%); A vs B P=0.3; histogram harmonization did not change number of robust features
extraction_note: Primary model choice: title/conclusion anchor on the combined radiomics + radiologist model (A+B+R2, which has no AUC); headline value is its specificity; abstract leads with Model B AUC 0.83 (listed in performance_value). MSK cohort overlaps a previous study by the same group (ref 10). Restaging (post-treatment) MRI so decision coded as organ_preservation_watch_wait (WW named in keywords/discussion). Code stated as to be made available via GitHub (coded NR). Majority vote uses radiologist label as input; modality coded radiology_imaging.

title: Predicting pathologic complete response in locally advanced rectal cancer patients after neoadjuvant therapy: a machine learning model using XGBoost.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer after neoadjuvant therapy; upper/middle/lower third

Decision coded W&W triage per abstract/conclusion (axis inherited neoadj_pcr_ww).

title: MRI-Based Radiomics Features to Predict Treatment Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Single Center, Prospective Study.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer (T2N+ or T3/4a Nany; T4b excluded)

title: Gene-expression profiles of pretreatment biopsies predict complete response of rectal cancer patients to preoperative chemoradiotherapy.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer, pretreatment biopsies
stage_detail: cUICC II/III rectal cancer treated with preoperative CRT
data_source_detail: CAO/ARO/AIO-94 and -04 trial patients (175; six surgical departments, 2001-2012; 161 for training/test + 14 validation I); public Padua dataset (Millino, GEO, n=38); prospective TransValid A trial (n=24-25, 6 institutions)
n_source: Methods and Abstract: 175 + 38 + 24; text/figures elsewhere cite 25 TransValid patients and 238 total
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR from pretreatment biopsy gene expression to select patients for watch and wait after preoperative CRT
treatment_context: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy (5-FU +/- oxaliplatin) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Agilent 4x44K microarray gene-expression of pretreatment tumor biopsies (21-transcript signature)
algorithm: Support vector machine on 21-transcript signature (feature selection by hill-climbing over 500 random splits); alternative score-based classifier
input_features: 21 transcripts (quantile-normalised expression)
comparator_detail: Five previously published gene-expression signatures re-evaluated (AUC 0.27-0.61 on 161 samples); score-based classifier from same 21 genes
primary_outcome: pCR (absence of viable tumour in primary and lymph nodes) vs incomplete response
performance_value: Prospective TransValid A (n=24-25): AUC 0.81, sens 0.4 at FPR=0; independent I (n=14, 4 pCR): AUC 0.7, sens 0.5; independent II Padua (n=38, 8 pCR): AUC 0.76, sens 0.5; all 161 cases: AUC 0.81, sens 0.31 (FPR=0); 4-fold CV on 64 cases: AUC 0.75, sens 0.4
performance_source: Results (21-transcript classifier robustly identifies over 1/3 of patients with pCR in independent datasets); Fig. 2e-f; Abstract
patient_outcomes_detail: Classifier score applied to 468 TCGA colon/rectal cases: high scores associated with longer OS (p=0.0007) and DFS (p=0.0002)
validation_detail: Trained on 64 extreme cases (32 pCR, 32 poor response) from CAO/ARO/AIO trials; applied without retraining to three independent cohorts: 14 trial patients, public Padua cohort (38), and prospectively collected TransValid A samples (multicenter, 6 institutions)
funding: Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (KFO 179); Intramural Research Program of NIH/NCI; Open Access by Projekt DEAL
key_finding: 21-transcript SVM identified roughly one third or more of pCR cases with zero false positives (AUC 0.81 in 161 patients) and held in three independent cohorts including a prospective one; sensitivity at FPR=0 only 0.31-0.5.
limitations_as_stated: SVM dependent on quantile normalisation; TransValid samples processed in small batches (additional bias); training predominantly male (more misclassified women); relatively short follow-up for prognostic analysis
other_models_outcomes: Score-based classifier (no normalisation needed) identified >30% of pCR in independent datasets without false positives; published signatures GS1-GS5 AUC 0.27-0.61 (161) and 0.4-0.74 (38 Padua)
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: TransValid A cohort reported as 24 patients (abstract, Methods: 4 pCR + 20 non-pCR) but as 25 specimens with 5 pCR in Results and Figure 2 legends (and 238 total in Fig. 2 legend); used 24 and 237 with AUC 0.81; sens 0.4 corresponds to 2/5. Of the 161 cases used for AUC 0.81, 64 were used for feature selection/training (overlap). AUC CIs not reported. Patient tables and support vectors are in supplement.

title: Endoscopy-Based Deep Convolutional Neural Network Predicts Response to Neoadjuvant Treatment for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer, primary T3-4/N+
stage_detail: Pre-treatment T3-4 and/or N+ (cT2 3.7% in training/val table; T3/T4 majority); post-NT restaging endoscopy
data_source_detail: Sixth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, consecutive patients Apr 2013-Apr 2021 with post-NT restaging endoscopy and surgery
n_source: Abstract; Results Patient Selection (1,000 patients, 6,939 images)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify TRG0 vs non-TRG0 after neoadjuvant therapy to identify surgery candidates and avoid inappropriate wait-and-watch
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (long/short course) or neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone, then radical surgery
data_modality_detail: Post-NT white-light restaging endoscopic images (6-8 weeks after NT); 4-channel input (RGB + edge-enhanced gray)
algorithm: Modified ResNeSt-50 DCNN (ImageNet pretrained, fine-tuned, label smoothing, class weighting)
input_features: Endoscopic images only
comparator_detail: Three endoscopists (>3 y experience) on class-balanced subset of 20 test patients (142 images)
primary_outcome: TRG0 (complete response, AJCC 8th) vs non-TRG0 on surgical pathology
performance_value: Independent test (n=70 pts): AUROC 0.77 (0.65-0.93), acc 87.14, sens 61.53, spec 92.98, PPV 66.67, NPV 91.37; Validation (random 10% split): AUROC 0.95 (0.92-0.98), acc 92.13; Training: AUROC 0.94 (0.93-0.95), acc 94.21; Reader subset (20 pts): model AUROC 0.85 (0.68-1; Table 4 0.69-1), acc 85; endoscopists AUROC 0.55/0.70/0.65
performance_source: Results text p.5 and Table 2 (independent test set, Nov 2020-Apr 2021)
patient_outcomes_detail: No survival or clinical outcome analysis
validation_detail: Random 9:1 patient-level split of Apr 2013-Oct 2020 into training/validation; chronologically later independent test set (Nov 2020-Apr 2021) from same center; reader study on subset of test set
funding: National Key R&D Program of China (2017YFC1308800); NSFC (81970482); Sixth Affiliated Hospital Clinical Research 1010 Program; National Key Clinical Discipline
key_finding: DCNN on post-NT endoscopy identified TRG0 with AUROC 0.77 in temporal test set (NPV 91.4%, sens 61.5%) and outperformed three endoscopists on a 20-patient subset (AUROC 0.85 vs 0.55-0.70).
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective (selection bias); only luminal TRG assessed, not nodes/metastasis; no external validation; multimodal model suggested
other_models_outcomes: Endoscopists 1-3 reader study AUROC 0.55, 0.70, 0.65 (Table 4); Fleiss kappa 0.722
extraction_note: Image-level analysis (6,939 images) but patient-level n reported. n_train=930 is training+validation combined (split 9:1, individual counts not given). Test cohort is temporal same-center though authors call it external/independent. Decision coded as W&W (stated aim) rather than neoadjuvant_response; no COI statement found; image-preprocessing in supplement. Reader study AUROC CI 0.68-1 in text vs 0.69-1 in Table 4.

title: Automated Prediction of the Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Patients Affected by Rectal Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer (cT2-T4, 80% N+)
data_source_detail: IRCCS Sant'Orsola-Malpighi Polyclinic Bologna, primary-staging T2w MRI, Jan 2018-Dec 2020
n_source: Methods 2.1 (43 patients for segmentation; 39 for radiomic TRG analysis)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pathologic response (TRG) to nCRT from primary staging MRI as decision support for radiologists
treatment_context: Long-course nCRT (50.4 Gy IMRT + capecitabine) then TME
data_modality_detail: Baseline T2-weighted pelvic MRI (1.5T); automated U-Net tumor segmentation, then Pyradiomics features (100)
algorithm: 2D U-Net (EfficientNetB0 backbone) segmentation; Pyradiomics features; PCA (6 components, 90% variance); support vector classifier
input_features: 100 radiomic features from automatically segmented tumor ROI (T2w MRI)
comparator_detail: Literature benchmark Li et al. 2021 (manual segmentation, LASSO + LR/RF/DT/KNN, AUC 0.63-0.93), not same data
primary_outcome: TRG 0-1 vs TRG 2-3 (AJCC) on surgical pathology
performance_value: TRG prediction, repeated 10-fold CV (500 repeats): AUC 0.89 (Table 4, no CI); class TRG0-1 precision 0.70, recall 0.79, F1 0.74; TRG2-3 precision 0.84, recall 0.77, F1 0.80; MCC 0.55+/-0.09. Segmentation (test 13 pts): DSC 0.73-0.75 (text 0.74)
performance_source: Table 4 (AUC 0.89); Table 3 and Results 3.2 (P/R/F1/MCC)
validation_detail: Segmentation: disjoint 30/13 train/test split of patients. TRG classifier: 500 repeats of 10-fold CV on 39 patients (Table 4 labels it leave-one-out); PCA/standardization apparently on full set before CV
funding: No external funding; acknowledgement of EU H2020 GenoMed4All and In Silico World grants
key_finding: Fully automated U-Net + radiomics + SVC pipeline from baseline MRI predicted TRG response in 39 LARC patients with CV AUC 0.89; segmentation DSC 0.74.
limitations_as_stated: Small single-center dataset; limited generalizability; need multicenter validation with larger cohort; only 1 mucinous case; TRG missing for some patients
other_models_outcomes: Segmentation U-Net DSC 0.73-0.75 on 13 test patients (Table 2); comparison with Li et al. AUC 0.63-0.93
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: TRG class sizes 16/23 (n=39; Table 1 and Methods) vs Table 3 support 13/19 (n=32); CV described as 10-fold in Methods/Table 3 but leave-one-out in Table 4; AUC 0.89 reported only in Table 4 (Table 3 gives no AUC). Primary model taken as the TRG classifier (title/conclusion); segmentation is the upstream component. Hybrid coded: DL segmentation + handcrafted radiomics + SVC. Feature standardization/PCA before CV (possible leakage, factual). Segmentation weights on GitHub.

title: MRI-based radiomics to predict response in locally advanced rectal cancer: comparison of manual and automatic segmentation on external validation in a multicentre study.
tumor_site_detail: Biopsy-confirmed stage II/III locally advanced rectal cancer
stage_detail: Stage II/III LARC (T3/T4 or node-positive)
data_source_detail: Three Torino-area centres: A Candiolo (n=44), B Mauriziano (n=23) construction; C Citta della Salute (n=28) external validation; Oct 2010-Dec 2018
n_source: Methods/Results Patient dataset, Table 2 (95 patients; automatic pipeline excluded 4 construction patients)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy to select patients for organ-preserving strategies or alternative therapy
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (capecitabine/5-FU/CAPEOX/FOLFOX) or radiotherapy alone, then TME
data_modality_detail: Baseline multiparametric MRI (T2w and ADC from DWI); 157 Pyradiomics features; manual vs automatic (FCN) segmentation
algorithm: Ranking feature selection (AUC-based, correlation filter) + Gaussian SVM; automatic ROI from fully convolutional network
input_features: Radiomic features (ROI volume, GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, from T2w and ADC); 27 selected
comparator_detail: Manual-segmentation pipeline (Ranking + polynomial SVM) and hybrid train/validate combinations; also several FS x classifier combinations
primary_outcome: Responder (Mandard TRG 1-2) vs non-responder (TRG 3-4/5) on surgical pathology
performance_value: Automatic model external centre C (n=28): AUC 0.81 (0.60-0.89), acc 75, sens 80, spec 69, NPV 75, PPV 75; construction (n=63): AUC 0.86 (0.78-0.94), acc 78. Manual model external: AUC 0.61 (0.52-0.74), acc 68 (19/28), sens 60, spec 77; construction AUC 0.90 (0.82-0.97), acc 83. Hybrid Train_MAN+Val_AUTO AUC 0.69 acc 75; Train_AUTO+Val_MAN AUC 0.62 acc 64
performance_source: Table 4 (automatic, validation set centre C); Table 3 (manual); Results text p.9
validation_detail: Centres A+B randomly split 70/30 (6-fold CV for feature-number selection); one fully external centre C (n=28, different scanner/protocol); one external site so not multicenter-external
funding: AIRC 5 per Mille 2018 (ID 21091); FPRC 5xmille 2015 Ministero della Salute (STRATEGY)
key_finding: Radiomics pipeline had external AUC 0.81 (acc 75%) with automatic vs AUC 0.61 (acc 68%) with manual segmentation; automatic segmentation was at least as effective on external data.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective; small sample (n=95; validation n=28); 15 excluded for artifacts; many features relative to sample size (overfitting risk); TRG 3 grouped with non-responders
other_models_outcomes: Manual-segmentation model (Ranking+polynomial SVM) external AUC 0.61, acc 68; hybrid models; other FS+classifier combos in Tables 3-4 (several overfit, AUC 0.99-1.00 in construction)
extraction_note: Two co-primary models (manual vs automatic segmentation); chose automatic per rule 2b (best AUC in external cohort 0.81 vs 0.61; automatic ahead on accuracy, sensitivity). Manual model in other_models_outcomes. n_train not stated (construction 67, split 70/30; 63 for automatic). Selected features in supplement. No code statement found.

title: Simulation CT-based radiomics for prediction of response after neoadjuvant chemo-radiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Histologically confirmed locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma (low 44%, mid 50%, high 5.5%)
stage_detail: UICC stage II/III: cT2N+ 5.5%, cT3N0 20.4%, cT3N+ 63.2%, cT4 10.9%
data_source_detail: Tubingen (2007-2010; explorative/training, n=126) and Florence (2011-2017; external validation, n=75) planning CTs
n_source: Abstract and Results (201 patients; 126 TU + 75 FL)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pathologic good response to neoadjuvant chemoradiation from simulation CT radiomics
treatment_context: Long-course neoadjuvant chemoradiation (TU 50.4 Gy + 5-FU, 62% with hyperthermia; FL 45 Gy + capecitabine) then TME
data_modality_detail: Radiation-planning (simulation) CT, manually segmented rectal GTV; 1150 IBSI/wavelet radiomic features
algorithm: Correlated-feature clustering + PCA metafeatures (5-metafeature signature) + 5-nearest neighbour
input_features: 5 PCA metafeatures (wavelet GLSZM large zone emphasis, elongation, intensity histogram mean, run-level variance, cluster tendency)
comparator_detail: No comparator; other classifiers (SVM, naive Bayes, RF) compared during model selection
primary_outcome: Pathologic good response (Dworak TRG 3+4)
performance_value: External validation Florence (n=75): AUC 0.63; Tubingen explorative (5-fold CV): AUC 0.65 +/- 0.02
performance_source: Abstract; Results p.4 and Fig. 2
validation_detail: Model selection with 5-fold CV in Tubingen (n=126); fixed model tested on independent Florence cohort (different country, different treatment protocol and period); single external site
funding: No funding (Open Access via Projekt DEAL)
key_finding: A 5-metafeature planning-CT radiomics signature with 5-NN gave fair prediction of good response (AUC 0.65 CV; 0.63 external).
limitations_as_stated: Small sample; low pCR rate; TRG 3+4 clustered; low CT contrast limits GTV segmentation; signature may be a surrogate of tumour volume; unrecognized confounders (treatment heterogeneity, hyperthermia, waiting time); AUC <0.7
other_models_outcomes: NR
extraction_note: Primary metric AUC 0.63 on external cohort has no CI reported. Cohorts differ in treatment (hyperthermia in 62% of TU only, dose/chemo) and surgery interval (6 vs 9 wk); authors state they are balanced otherwise. Authors cite TRIPOD type 3 only as a classification, not as followed. Full radiomics protocol in supplement.

title: Machine learning-based multiparametric MRI radiomics for predicting poor responders after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal Cancer patients.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer treated with nCRT then surgery
stage_detail: LARC; cTNM not reported in text
data_source_detail: Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University, MRI Mar 2012-May 2020; training before Dec 2017, validation after
n_source: Results Patient characteristics, Table 2 (207 patients; training 129, validation 78)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Early identification of poor responders (TRG 3-5) after nCRT before surgery to allow patient-tailored surgery (more extensive resection) and treatment
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery
data_modality_detail: Multiparametric MRI (T2WI, DWI, CE-T1WI; 3.0T GE), 1027 radiomic features; ComBat harmonization tested
algorithm: mRMR followed by LASSO feature selection + support vector machine (20 selector x classifier combinations compared: DT, RF, SVM, LR, AdaBoost)
input_features: Radiomic features from T2WI, DWI and CE-T1WI (ICC >=0.75 retained)
comparator_detail: 19 other feature-selection x classifier combinations; ComBat vs no ComBat
primary_outcome: Poor response (Mandard TRG 3-5) vs good response (TRG 1-2) on surgical pathology
performance_value: Validation temporal (n=78): AUC 0.923 (0.862-0.985), F1 88.14, accuracy 91.03, sensitivity 89.60; training AUC 0.945 (0.896-0.994)
performance_source: Table 4 and Results Classifier performance (mRMR+LASSO+SVM, No ComBat); training Table 3
validation_detail: Chronological split at Dec 2017 within one institution (training n=129, validation n=78); feature selection on training only; best model among 20 chosen by validation performance
funding: Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University (Open Access Publishing funding program)
key_finding: SVM with mRMR-LASSO selection on multiparametric MRI radiomics identified poor responders with AUC 0.923 in a temporal validation cohort; ComBat did not improve performance.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective, selection bias (wait-and-see patients excluded); needs data from different scanners/institutions; indistinct tumour margins after nCRT may affect segmentation
other_models_outcomes: Other 19 combinations in Table 4 (validation AUC 0.43-0.89); ComBat models (best mRMR-LASSO SVM 0.887)
extraction_note: Best of 20 models selected by validation-set AUC (optimism possible; factual). Timing of the MRI relative to nCRT is not clearly stated (described as preoperative). Table 2 text extraction garbled; training/validation class counts not used. Selected features in supplement.

title: Applicability of a pathological complete response magnetic resonance-based radiomics model for locally advanced rectal cancer in intercontinental cohort.
tumor_site_detail: Pathologically proven locally advanced rectal cancer, no distant metastases
data_source_detail: Sichuan Cancer Hospital, consecutive patients Mar 2017-Jan 2018 (validation of a model previously developed in Italy, Dinapoli 2018)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Early prediction of pCR after nCRT to support tailored treatment, organ preservation or dose intensification
treatment_context: nCRT (long course 50.4 Gy + capecitabine) or short-course RT 5x5 Gy with CapOx, then TME
data_modality_detail: Baseline T2w staging MRI (1.5T and 3T Siemens), LoG-filtered skewness and entropy; cT and cN added as covariates
algorithm: Previously published multivariable logistic regression (2 radiomic features + cT + cN) applied without retraining
input_features: Skewness (LoG 0.48), entropy (LoG 0.34), cT, cN
comparator_detail: Compared to AUC of original external validation (0.75) only
primary_outcome: pCR (ypT0N0) vs non-pCR
performance_value: Whole cohort (n=59): AUC 0.83 (0.71-0.96); at fixed original threshold 0.26: accuracy 0.65, specificity 0.64, sensitivity 0.70, NPV 0.91, PPV 0.28; 1.5T subgroup AUC 0.82 (0.61-1.00); 3T subgroup AUC 0.86 (0.70-1.00)
performance_source: Abstract; Results p.4-5; Table 3
validation_detail: Fixed pre-existing model applied to one intercontinental cohort (different country, scanner vendor, field strength and RT schedules); no refitting or recalibration; original study had internal and external validation by the same group
funding: Chengdu Science and Technology Project 2021-YF05-01484-SN; Excellent Youth Foundation Project of Sichuan Cancer Hospital YB2021037; Health Commission of Sichuan Province 20PJ112
key_finding: The 4-variable MRI radiomic+clinical pCR model transported to a Chinese cohort with AUC 0.83 (NPV 0.91) but low PPV (0.28) at the original threshold.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample (59; 10 pCR); no multi-observer segmentation; heterogeneous treatment, scanners and ethnicity; requires prospective validation
other_models_outcomes: Original model internal AUC 0.73 and original external AUC 0.75 (prior publication)
extraction_note: Study is an external validation of a previously developed model (n=162 training in prior paper, not part of this analysis): n_analytic=59, n_train=NA. Logistic regression coded statistical_model; cT/cN added to an imaging model so modality kept radiology_imaging (rule 9). Cohort characteristics differ from original (N stage, RT schedule, scanners). Data availability statement says data are within article/additional files (only confusion matrices), coded NR. Authors use TRIPOD type-4 as an evidence level, not as a reporting guideline.

title: MRI radiomics independent of clinical baseline characteristics and neoadjuvant treatment modalities predicts response to neoadjuvant therapy in rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma (cT3-4 or N+, no distant metastasis)
stage_detail: AJCC 7th cT3-4 or any T N+; MRI-T3 ~75%, T4 ~21%
data_source_detail: Four Chinese centres (Peking University Cancer Hospital, Sixth Affiliated Hospital Sun Yat-sen, PUMC Hospital, Tianjin Union Medical Center), Jan 2012-Jan 2019
n_source: Methods Patient selection and Results (674 included of 735; TRG0 n=174, TRG1-3 n=500)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict complete response to neoadjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy before treatment to identify patients for organ preservation strategies and avoid overtreatment
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy: short-course RT + chemo, long-course CRT, chemo then CRT, CRT then chemo
data_modality_detail: Pre-treatment T2-weighted 3.0T MRI; 786 radiomic features (HOG, texture, wavelet, statistical), top 30 by PCA; clinical/treatment variables only in CMBR/CTMBR secondary models
algorithm: PCA (30 components) + support vector machine (MBR signature); decision tree for non-imaging C/CT models
input_features: 30 PCA-derived radiomic features from T2WI
comparator_detail: Non-imaging C model (CEA, MRI-T stage, histologic grade) and CT model (plus treatment modalities), decision tree; CMBR and CTMBR variants
primary_outcome: Complete response (TRG0 by AJCC; includes 29 cCR on wait-and-see with >2 y follow-up) vs TRG1-3
performance_source: Results Evaluation and comparison; Fig. 2c; Table 3
validation_detail: Random 5-fold cross-validation over the pooled 674 patients from four centres; no centre-held-out or temporal validation; PCA fitted on all 674 patients before CV
funding: Beijing Municipal Science & Technology Commission; Peking University Cancer Hospital; Beijing Natural Science Foundation; Beijing Hospital Authority; Capital Funds for Health Improvement and Research; NSFC (82073333, 32071156); funders had no role
key_finding: Pre-treatment T2 MRI radiomics (SVM) predicted complete response with CV AUC 0.78 across four centres, outperforming non-imaging clinical models (AUC 0.61-0.63); adding clinical/treatment variables did not significantly improve.
limitations_as_stated: T2WI only; no central TRG review; methodological variation across studies; need multi-label classification and molecular data; unclear whether response influences later treatment; prospective multicentre validation needed
other_models_outcomes: CMBR AUC 0.7871; CTMBR AUC 0.7916; C model 0.6103; CT model 0.6294 (CV validation)
extraction_note: Primary = MBR radiomics signature (title/abstract anchor); CMBR/CTMBR statistically similar. Multicentre pooled data but only random 5-fold CV, so internal_cv (not external). PCA reduction applied to all 674 patients prior to CV (possible information leakage, factual). Two authors affiliated with Blot Info & Tech (platform used); COI states none. Validation-set CIs are across folds. Outcome mixes pathologic TRG0 with clinical CR. Per-fold n not given.

title: Deep Learning-Based Model for Identifying Tumors in Endoscopic Images From Patients With Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Treated With Total Neoadjuvant Therapy.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer treated with total neoadjuvant therapy (mid-rectum, mean distance from anal verge 6-8 cm)
stage_detail: Clinical T3 74-87%, T4 6-19%, T1-2 4-7%; node positive 74-89%
data_source_detail: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, TNT patients Dec 2012-Jul 2017; endoscopic images before, during, after TNT and follow-up
n_source: Abstract and Results (1392 images from 109 patients: 1099 training/82 patients, 293 testing/27 patients)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Improve endoscopic identification of tumor presence/absence after TNT to support watch-and-wait selection
treatment_context: Total neoadjuvant therapy: induction FOLFOX/CAPEOX then long-course chemoradiation (or CRT then consolidation chemo)
data_modality_detail: White-light flexible endoscopy still images (Olympus CF-Q160S), 256x256 patches from brightest region; up to 3 images per time point
algorithm: VGG-19 CNN (ImageNet transfer learning, modified layers, 3-fold CV training)
input_features: Endoscopic image patches only
comparator_detail: No direct comparison with surgeons; literature AUROC 0.80-0.88 cited
primary_outcome: Tumor vs no tumor on endoscopic image (labels from surgeon assessment, surgical pathology, or sustained cCR >2 y)
performance_value: Test set (293 images, 27 patients): AUROC 0.83, sensitivity (no tumor) 0.66, specificity (tumor) 0.87, PPV 0.70, NPV 0.85; training 3-fold CV (1099 images): AUROC 0.83, sens 0.78, spec 0.73, PPV 0.70, NPV 0.80; test after removing poor-quality images: AUROC 0.86, sens 0.87, spec 0.72
performance_source: Abstract; Results p.5-6; Fig. 3
patient_outcomes_detail: Sustained cCR (2-year) used only as reference label; no outcome by predicted class
validation_detail: Patient-level split into training (82 patients, 1099 images, 3-fold CV) and testing (27 patients, 293 images) sets at the same center; method of allocating patients to sets not stated; image-level evaluation
funding: NCI Cancer Center Support Grant P30 CA008748 (in part)
conflicts_of_interest: Garcia-Aguilar: honoraria from Medtronic, Johnson & Johnson, Intuitive Surgical
key_finding: VGG-19 CNN classified tumor vs no tumor on post-TNT endoscopic images with AUROC 0.83 in the held-out set (sens 0.66, spec 0.87); errors clustered in post-TNT and follow-up images.
limitations_as_stated: Pilot; retrospective, single center; small number of images; excluded patients with regrowth or pCR; need larger validation and near-complete response images; interobserver variability not addressed
other_models_outcomes: NR
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: abstract calls the study a prospective pilot, whereas Discussion states it was retrospective and images were collected retrospectively; coded retrospective_cohort. Labels for during/post-TNT images derive from surgeon assessment, pathology or sustained cCR; images from the same patient across time points; per-patient/split unit of analysis is the image. Reference-standard tumor/no-tumor on image is not the same as pCR. Model details in supplement. Sensitivity defined by authors as detection of no tumor.

title: Local tuning of radiomics-based model for predicting pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma
stage_detail: cT3-4N0 or cT1-4N1-2 (AJCC 7th); no distant metastases
data_source_detail: 88 LARC patients treated at Sichuan Cancer Hospital & Institute, Mar 2017-Dec 2020 (new cohort); reference GLM (Italy-trained) also tested on 59-patient earlier cohort from same institute
n_source: Methods Patients; Results Patient characteristics, Table 1
therapeutic_decision_detail: Early prediction of pCR after nCRT in LARC (to identify candidates for less/no surgery)
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (short course 5x5 Gy or long course 50.4 Gy + capecitabine) then Capoex, TME
data_modality_detail: Pretreatment 3T axial T2w MRI, manual GTV; LoG-filtered radiomics; age added as clinical feature (one of 8 selected)
algorithm: LASSO logistic regression (5-fold CV lambda) on Mann-Whitney-screened radiomics features; Rad-score
input_features: 1643 LoG-filtered radiomics features (statistical, morphological, GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM) + cT, cN, age; final 7 radiomics + age
comparator_detail: Reference GLM (cT, cN, skewness, entropy; previously developed) AUC 0.831 original cohort and 0.828 new cohort
primary_outcome: pCR (Mandard TRG1) vs non-pCR
performance_value: Enhanced LASSO: train AUC 0.926 (95% CI 0.859-0.993); validation (25% hold-out) AUC 0.926 (0.767-1.00). Reference GLM: 0.831 (0.701-0.961) original cohort (n=59), 0.828 (0.700-0.956) new cohort (n=88)
performance_source: Abstract; Results Performance comparison; Fig 4B
validation_detail: Enhanced model: random 75/25 split of the 88-patient single-center cohort (split described as "according to their demographic"); 5-fold CV for lambda; bootstrap CIs. Reference GLM was externally applied to the new cohort but it is not the headline model.
funding: Sichuan Province Science and Technology Support Program (21RCYJ0022); Sichuan Cancer Hospital Youth Project (YB2021032)
key_finding: Previously trained GLM reproduced AUC ~0.83 in new 3T cohort; locally tuned LASSO model reached AUC 0.926 in 25% hold-out (wide CI), proposed as candidate for clinical practice.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample relative to number of predictors; only T2w MRI used (DWI etc. could improve).
other_models_outcomes: Reference GLM AUC 0.831 and 0.828 (see performance_value); training AUC enhanced 0.926
extraction_note: Main model = enhanced LASSO (anchors title/conclusion). n_train/n_test/n_performance derived: 75%/25% of 88 (66/22); exact split counts not reported (n_source derived: 75/25 of 88). pCR events 12 of 88; events in the 22 hold-out not reported. extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: text/abstract report 236 patients while Table 2 totals 237 (males 135 + females 101); used 236. Several co-reported outcomes; pCR chosen as primary because it is first in title/conclusion and is the therapeutic-response outcome; recurrence/cT/ypT/ypN in other_models_outcomes. Clinical T category sensitivity/specificity in abstract/Table 4 appear swapped vs PPV/NPV (not used). Cross-validated AUC with ADASYN oversampling in training folds only.

title: Machine learning-based random forest predicts anastomotic leakage after anterior resection for rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal cancer treated with anterior resection with TME (tumor <=15 cm from anal verge)
stage_detail: pT1-2 vs pT3-4 and pN0 vs pN+ (all stages after anterior resection); 25.7% received nCRT
data_source_detail: Changhai Hospital prospectively maintained CRC database: Aug 2009-Jun 2018 (development, n=5,220) and Jul 2018-Jun 2019 (test, n=836)
n_source: Methods Patients; Results (5,220 development + 836 test; derived sum)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict anastomotic leakage after anterior resection and advise whether to perform a temporary stoma
treatment_context: Anterior resection with TME for rectal cancer; temporary stoma decision
data_modality_detail: Demographic, laboratory, surgical and pathological variables (20 candidates; top 8 retained)
algorithm: Random forest classifier (grid-search CV, 5-fold; minority up-sampling to 9,788)
input_features: Sex, distance of tumor from anal verge, bowel stenosis/obstruction, preoperative hemoglobin, surgeon volume, diabetes, neoadjuvant CRT, surgical approach (incl. first-year laparoscopy)
comparator_detail: Logistic-regression nomogram on same 8 predictors (training AUC 0.735, test 0.724)
primary_outcome: Anastomotic leakage (clinical AL within 6 months; incidence 6.2%)
performance_value: Test (n=836, 45 AL) AUC 0.87, sens 0.844, spec 0.697; 5-fold CV validation AUC 0.85+-0.02 (sens 0.818, spec 0.67); training AUC 0.89+-0.00 (sens 0.827, spec 0.739); nomogram AUC 0.724 test
performance_source: Abstract; Results; Fig 2C
validation_detail: 5-fold CV on 2009-2018 data plus later-period test set (Jul 2018-Jun 2019) from same hospital database; authors label it external validation and "prospectively collected"
funding: Clinical Science and Technology Innovation Project of Shanghai Shenkang Hospital Development Center (SHDC12016122); 234 Climbing the Discipline Program (2019YXK032); Ethicon Excellence in Surgery Grant (HZB-20181119-30)
key_finding: Random forest on 8 predictors predicted anastomotic leakage better (test AUC 0.87) than the logistic nomogram (0.724); temporary stoma not protective after PSM.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective single center; selection bias; lacks external validation at other centers (prospective multicenter study under way); some variables (smoking) not recorded; KRAS missing in early years
other_models_outcomes: Nomogram AUC 0.735 train / 0.724 test; multivariable logistic and PSM analyses of temporary stoma (n=2,218-2,366)
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: abstract/results give test AUC 0.87 but Table 6 lists "Our model" AUC 0.850; Methods say retrospective with prospectively maintained database while Fig 2 caption calls test set prospectively collected; PSM sample 2,218 (text) vs 2,366 (Table 4). Authors call the 836-patient later-period cohort external, but it is from the same hospital, so coded temporal_same_center (rule 5). Minority up-sampling (to 9,788) is described before the 5-fold CV split, so CV/validation figures may be optimistic; test set is unaffected. No CI for AUC. n_analytic derived as 5,220+836.

title: Radiomic signature of the FOWARC trial predicts pathological response to neoadjuvant treatment in rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer (FOWARC trial)
stage_detail: cT3-4 and/or cN1-2, cStage II-III (Table 1: cTNM II 31, III 82 in primary cohort pattern)
data_source_detail: FOWARC randomized trial (NCT01211210), 177 patients with portal venous-phase contrast CT on same scanner; MRI subset n=99
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR after neoadjuvant treatment to identify patients appropriate for watch-and-wait and avoid overtreatment
treatment_context: FOWARC arms: 5-FU/RT, mFOLFOX6, or mFOLFOX6+RT neoadjuvant, then TME
data_modality_detail: Pre-treatment contrast-enhanced portal venous CT radiomics (rad-score); clinicopathological variables (CEA, MRF, tumor thickness, cN) added to the GBM, not a separate data modality; exploratory CT+MRI rad-score subset
algorithm: LASSO logistic rad-score (14 of 1218 PyRadiomics features) then gradient boosting machine with clinicopathological variables; 5x10-fold repeated CV tuning
input_features: CT rad-score plus CEA, MRF, tumor thickness, cN stage and other clinicopathological variables
comparator_detail: Logistic regression and SVM integrated models; CT vs MRI vs CT-MRI rad-score by AIC
primary_outcome: Pathological complete response (TRG 0)
performance_value: GBM validation (n=64, 11 pCR) AUC 0.822 (0.649-0.995), accuracy 0.813, sens 0.727, spec 0.830; GBM primary cohort AUC 0.997 (0.990-1.000), accuracy 0.973, sens 1.000, spec 0.946; SVM 0.961/0.811; combined CT-MRI AIC 75.49 vs CT 81.34 vs MRI 82.39
performance_source: Abstract; Results Development and validation of integrated models; Table 2

funding: National Basic Research Program of China (973 Program, 2015CB554001); NSFC (81972245, 81902877); Guangdong provincial and Sun Yat-sen University programs (see paper)

limitations_as_stated: Few pCR cases; secondary analysis of a trial; independent validation needed; CT-MRI model exploratory with limited sample
other_models_outcomes: Logistic AUC and SVM AUC 0.961 (0.909-1.000) primary / 0.811 (0.672-0.950) validation; CT-MRI integrated model on n=99 subset (AIC 75.49, Brier 0.087)
extraction_note: Factual: primary-cohort GBM AUC 0.997 vs validation 0.822 (large gap). Validation split is random within the same trial/institution. Setting coded NR: FOWARC is a multicenter trial but the paper does not state sites for the 177 imaged patients (single scanner). Logistic validation AUC not stated in text (only accuracy). Clinical variables added to a radiomics score were not coded as multimodal (rule 9).

title: Radiomics signature as a new biomarker for preoperative prediction of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy response in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal adenocarcinoma, LARC
stage_detail: cT3-4 or N+, inclusion no distant metastasis; Table 1 T3/T4, N0-2 (and M stage rows)
data_source_detail: Liaoning Cancer Hospital, patients enrolled 06/2014-08/2017, pre-nCRT 3.0T MRI (axial/sagittal T2, contrast-enhanced axial T1)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Individualized preoperative prediction of nCRT response (sensitive vs resistant) to avoid unnecessary radiotherapy/chemotherapy exposure
treatment_context: nCRT (mFOLFOX6 or CapeOX with 45-50.4 Gy IMRT) then TME
data_modality_detail: Pre-treatment multi-sequence MRI radiomics; CEA and tumor diameter added to the nomogram (clinical variables added to imaging model, not coded multimodal)
algorithm: Radiomics nomogram: mRMR/univariable then LASSO logistic signature plus CEA and tumor diameter in multivariable logistic regression; also RF, SVM, KNN and RF ensemble classifier
input_features: 30-feature radiomics signature (axial contrast T1, sagittal T2) + CEA + tumor-axis diameter
comparator_detail: RF, SVM, KNN and ensemble classifiers per MRI sequence; image-only signature (AUC 0.749)
primary_outcome: nCRT response by Mandard TRG: sensitive (TRG 1/2) vs resistant (TRG 3-5)
performance_value: Nomogram validation (n=55) AUC 0.949 (0.892-0.997), sens 0.879, spec 0.909; nomogram training (n=134) AUC 0.970 (0.942-0.997), sens 0.939, spec 0.898; image-only signature validation AUC 0.749; ensemble classifier 10-fold CV AUC 0.830
performance_source: Abstract; Results Fig 2d-e; Table 2 for ML classifiers
validation_detail: Nomogram: training/validation split of single-center cohort (134/55; method of split not described); ML classifiers: 10-fold cross-validation
funding: NR
key_finding: Multi-sequence MRI radiomics nomogram with CEA and tumor diameter predicted nCRT response with validation AUC 0.949; RF ensemble reached 0.830 by CV.
limitations_as_stated: Single hospital; small sample; manual segmentation; multicenter data and deep-learning automation needed
other_models_outcomes: RF/T1WI C+ AUC 0.827; RF sagittal T2 0.788; RF axial T2 0.748; KNN 0.688-0.776; SVM 0.570-0.624; ensemble classifier AUC 0.830, acc 75.4% (Table 2)
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: abstract gives ensemble classifier specificity 0.794/sensitivity 0.815 whereas Table 2 gives SEN 0.794/SPE 0.815 (table preferred); nomogram validation AUC CI upper bound 0.997 (abstract) vs 1.000 (text); inclusion says no distant metastasis but Table 1/text show M1 patients; Table 1 counts (e.g., sex/distance) do not sum cleanly. Co-primary models (nomogram vs ensemble classifier); main = radiomics nomogram (best AUC, abstract headline) per rule 2b, ensemble classifier in other_models_outcomes. Training AUC 0.970 vs validation 0.949; split procedure not described.

title: Pretreatment CT and PET radiomics predicting rectal cancer patients in response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer treated with NACRT
data_source_detail: Moffitt Cancer Center patients with staging PET, Jan 2011-Feb 2018; pre-treatment non-contrast RT-planning CT and 18F-FDG PET
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pathologic response (TRG) to NACRT to select patients, incl. for nonoperative management
treatment_context: NACRT (5-FU or capecitabine, 45 Gy pelvis, median 50.4 Gy to primary) then surgery
data_modality_detail: Pre-treatment non-contrast CT plus 18F-FDG PET radiomics combined as composite features (alpha*PET + (1-alpha)*CT)
algorithm: Weka logistic regression (best) vs random forest vs SVM on composite CT+PET radiomics features with correlation-based subset selection; leave-one-out cross-validation
input_features: 929 radiomic features per modality; composite alpha=0.2; 4-feature model for TRG 0 vs 1-3
comparator_detail: Logistic regression vs RF vs SVM; alpha values 0.2/0.5/0.8
primary_outcome: Pathologic complete response (TRG 0) vs TRG 1-3
performance_value: TRG 0 vs 1-3: LOOCV accuracy 88.1%, ROC 0.858, sens 77.8%, spec 89.7% (4 features); TRG 0-1 vs 2-3: accuracy 91.0%, ROC 0.951, sens 93.8%, spec 84.2% (6 features); NAR low/intermediate/high: accuracy 67.7%, ROC 0.814 (11 features)
performance_source: Abstract; Results; Table 2
patient_outcomes_detail: NAR score used as surrogate for DFS/OS; actual survival outcomes not analysed against model
validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation on 66 patients; feature selection and alpha choice done on the same data, performed per alpha
funding: NR
key_finding: Composite CT+PET radiomics signature predicted TRG 0 vs 1-3 with LOOCV accuracy 88.1% (ROC 0.858) and TRG 0-1 vs 2-3 with accuracy 91%; larger cohort needed.
limitations_as_stated: Single-institute retrospective; no multicenter/prospective validation; scanner variability; most patients lacked pretreatment MRI; small cohort
other_models_outcomes: TRG 0-1 vs 2-3 ROC 0.951, accuracy 91.0%; NAR 3-class accuracy 67.7%, ROC 0.814; RF and SVM performed worse than logistic regression (values NR)
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: median follow-up 27.9 months in text vs 25.5 months in Table 1; Discussion cites a 91-patient cohort from a prior study (not this one). Three co-reported endpoints; pCR (TRG 0 vs 1-3) chosen as main by conclusion/therapeutic relevance (rule 2a), TRG 0-1 vs 2-3 had higher ROC 0.951 and is in other_models_outcomes. Headline metric in abstract is accuracy; AUC (ROC) used as primary_metric_value. Funding section present but empty. No CIs for ROC. Leave-one-out with feature selection/alpha tuning on same data (factual, possible optimism).

title: The Heterogeneity of Skewness in T2W-Based Radiomics Predicts the Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma (mucinous excluded)
data_source_detail: IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna; staging MRI Jan 2018-Dec 2019 (85 screened, 40 included); baseline 1.5T oblique-axial T2w
therapeutic_decision_detail: Differentiate responders from non-responders to nCRT before therapy for tailored care strategies (intensification or avoiding overtreatment)
treatment_context: Long-course nCRT followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Baseline T2w MRI; 84 local first-order radiomic features from tumour ROI; single feature selected
algorithm: Univariate feature screening (one-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum, Bonferroni) of 84 first-order radiomic features, single best feature (entropy of local skewness map) with ROC/Youden cutoff; no multivariable model
input_features: 84 local first-order radiomic features from T2w ROI; selected: entropy of skewness maps (se)
comparator_detail: NR
primary_outcome: Responder (TRG 0-1, n=15) vs non-responder (TRG 2-3, n=25) by AJCC TRG
performance_value: AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.73-0.96); Youden index 0.68 at cut-off se=3.93; sensitivity 80%, specificity 88%, PPV 80%, NPV 88% (3 FP, 3 FN); same-data discrimination
performance_source: Abstract; Results 3.2; Fig 5
validation_detail: No validation; discrimination analysis on the entire 40-patient cohort (authors: only a training dataset considered due to small sample); cut-off derived on same data
funding: No external funding
key_finding: A single local-skewness-heterogeneity T2w radiomic feature differentiated TRG 0-1 from TRG 2-3 with AUC 0.90 (p~1e-5) in 40 patients; higher heterogeneity associated with better nCRT response.
limitations_as_stated: Small number of patients (no train/test split); validation with a prospective multicentre study needed
other_models_outcomes: NR
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: median age 65 years (IQR 14.5) in text vs 61 (range 46-85) in Table 2 (table preferred, not used in any coded field). Single-feature univariable ROC with selection and cut-off on the same 40 patients (selection from 84 features, Bonferroni-corrected); coded statistical_model and validation none per rule 10/5, although paper frames work as radiomics/machine learning. Text extraction of the MDPI PDF was duplicated/garbled; values cross-checked between abstract and Results.

title: Development of a Joint Prediction Model Based on Both the Radiomics and Clinical Factors for Predicting the Tumor Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Patients with Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) treated with nCRT then TME
stage_detail: Clinical stage II or III (cT1-4b, cN0-2)
data_source_detail: Nanfang Hospital (n=82, training + 10-fold CV internal validation); Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (n=107, external validation); 2012-2017
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pathological response (TRG 0-1 good vs TRG 2-3 poor) to nCRT before treatment to individualize treatment in LARC
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (IMRT 50 Gy/25 fx + capecitabine/XELOX/5-FU-oxaliplatin) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pre-CRT MRI texture radiomics (HR-T2WI and contrast-enhanced T1WI); clinical factors (CRM on MRI, CA19-9) added to the imaging model
algorithm: mRMR feature selection + random forest importance ranking + forward search; SVM classifier
input_features: Top 20 (T1+C: 16-19) texture features from 6192 (Gabor, GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, NGTDM) plus CRM and CA19-9 (CA72-4 in a variant not available externally)
comparator_detail: Radiomics-only model vs joint radiomics+clinical model
primary_outcome: Good pathological response (AJCC TRG 0-1) vs poor response (TRG 2-3) to nCRT
performance_value: Joint T1+C (CRM+CA19-9): external AUC 0.6818 (0.5659-0.7977), internal 0.9113 (0.8449-0.9776); joint HR-T2WI: external 0.6413, internal 0.9371 (0.8751-0.9997); radiomics-only T2WI: internal 0.8910, external 0.5413; radiomics-only T1+C: internal 0.8938, external 0.6089; joint with CA72-4 (internal only): T2WI 0.9350, T1+C 0.9168
performance_source: Table 3; Results (Combination of Radiomics and Clinical Characteristics); n=107
validation_detail: Training/internal validation by 10-fold CV in 82 patients from one center; external validation in 107 patients from a second center (different scanner 1.5T vs 3.0T); single external site
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81872470, 81803063, 81903125); Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province; Guangdong Medical Research Foundation; Southern Hospital Director Foundation
key_finding: Adding CRM and CA19-9 to MRI radiomics raised internal AUC to 0.91-0.94, but external AUC remained modest (0.64-0.68) with sensitivity/specificity near 0.55-0.68, despite the authors claiming external confirmation.
limitations_as_stated: Small retrospective sample with few TRG 0 cases; CEA not modeled due to small n; different MRI equipment/parameters between centers; multicenter prospective studies needed
other_models_outcomes: Radiomics-only HR-T2WI AUC internal 0.8910 / external 0.5413; radiomics-only T1+C 0.8938 / 0.6089; joint HR-T2WI (CRM+CA19-9) internal 0.9371 / external 0.6413; joint with CA72-4 internal only (0.9350, 0.9168)
extraction_note: Co-primary joint models (HR-T2WI and T1+C); chose T1+C joint (CRM+CA19-9) as best AUC in the most demanding (external) cohort, rule 2b. INCONSISTENT: external cohort size 107 (Table 2, abstract) vs 22/103 in text for TRG 0; Table 3 text-based CI values are garbled by pdftotext (external T2WI joint CI not reliable); text says good response n=55 and Table 2 shows 55/27 for training, external 60/47. Clinical variables added to imaging model, so coded radiology_imaging (rule 9) although authors call it multimodal. Primary model is pre-CRT; internal AUC from 10-fold CV.

title: Predicting treatment response from longitudinal images using multi-task deep learning.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma treated with neoadjuvant CRT and TME
stage_detail: Pre-CRT T1-T4b, N0-N2b by MRI (mostly T3-T4, N+); locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma
data_source_detail: Sixth Affiliated Hospital Sun Yat-sen Univ (SAH): training n=321 (2013-2016), internal validation n=160 (2017-2018); SYSUCC external validation n=141
n_source: Methods (Study design and patients); Abstract (2568 training scans)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR after neoadjuvant CRT to identify patients who could undergo watchful waiting and avoid radical surgery
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by total mesorectal excision
data_modality_detail: Pre- and post-CRT multiparametric MRI (T1, T1+contrast, T2, DWI); CEA used only in a secondary integrated model
algorithm: 3D RP-Net: multi-task Siamese 3D U-Net with multi-scale depth-wise convolution fusion for tumor segmentation and pCR prediction
input_features: Co-registered pre- and post-CRT 4-channel multiparametric MRI volumes
comparator_detail: Single time-point ResNet-18 (pre or post), T2-only model, single-task Siamese networks (simple concatenation and multi-scale), traditional radiomics model, post-CRT T stage, CEA-only
primary_outcome: pCR (TRG 0) vs non-pCR (TRG 1-3) after nCRT
performance_value: 3D RP-Net AUC: external (n=141) 0.92 (0.87-0.96), sens 91% spec 92%; internal temporal validation (n=160) 0.95 (0.91-0.98), sens 93% spec 94%; integrated imaging+CEA internal validation AUC 0.97 (0.93-0.99); T2-only AUC 0.86-0.88
performance_source: Abstract; Results (Model performance); Fig. 3a,e; n=141 external
patient_outcomes_detail: Association of deep learning score with TRG 0-3 only (supplementary); no survival outcomes
validation_detail: Training cohort (n=321) with cross-validation/early stopping; temporal same-center validation (n=160, 2017-2018) and independent external hospital (n=141); one external site only
funding: NR
key_finding: A multi-task Siamese 3D U-Net using longitudinal pre/post-CRT MRI predicted pCR with AUC 0.95 (internal) and 0.92 (external); adding CEA dynamics raised internal AUC to 0.97.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective with selection bias; Asian-only training data; PPV not yet sufficient for clinical use; prospective validation needed
other_models_outcomes: Integrated imaging+CEA random forest AUC 0.97 (0.93-0.99) internal validation; T2-only AUC 0.86-0.88; single-task and single time-point comparators lower by 7-19% AUC (supplementary tables)
extraction_note: Primary model = imaging-only 3D RP-Net (title/abstract anchor); integrated CEA model is secondary. Text says patients were "prospectively collected" for validation but Methods state retrospective study, so coded retrospective_cohort; internal validation is temporal same-center. Comparator/ablation tables only in supplement. Funding statement not found in the supplied PDF text (NR). Data on request via data access agreement.

title: MRI-based clinical-radiomics model predicts tumor response before treatment in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Non-mucinous locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma (>=T3 or N+) treated with long-course CRT
data_source_detail: G. D'Annunzio University of Chieti, 3.0 T staging MRI, Jan 2011-Feb 2019, 72 of 164 screened patients
therapeutic_decision_detail: Early (pretreatment) prediction of response to CRT to tailor neoadjuvant treatment (intensification/organ preservation) in LARC
treatment_context: Long-course neoadjuvant CRT (45-55 Gy with 5-FU/leucovorin or capecitabine) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Baseline T2-weighted MRI: radiomic features from tumor core and tumor border plus 9 MRI-derived visual clinical features (tumor location, volume, MRF, EMVI, T and N stage etc.)
algorithm: Partial least squares (PLS) regression with leave-one-out nested cross-validation
input_features: 9 MRI-based clinical features + 1405 radiomic features (r>0.95 inter-reader repeatability; PyRadiomics, 3 resolutions) from tumor core (TC) and tumor border (TB)
comparator_detail: Clinical-only (AUC 0.684), radiomics-only (0.700), clinical+TC only (0.689), clinical+TB only (0.541)
primary_outcome: Major pathological response (Mandard TRG 1-2) vs non-major (TRG 3-4); 3 patients with sustained clinical complete response coded as major response
performance_value: Clinical+radiomic TC+TB: AUC 0.793 (p=5.6e-5), LOO nested CV; clinical only 0.684; radiomic only 0.700; clinical+TC 0.689; clinical+TB 0.541
performance_source: Abstract; Results; Fig. 4c; n=72 (leave-one-out nested CV)
validation_detail: Leave-one-out nested cross-validation in a single-center cohort; no separate validation cohort
funding: NR
key_finding: Combining MRI-based clinical features with radiomic features from tumor core and border gave AUC 0.793 for pretreatment prediction of major pathological response; border features added value only in combination with core.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample, no validation cohort; retrospective single-center; some patients without antiperistaltic agent and scanner software upgrades; only T2w imaging; prospective multicenter studies needed
other_models_outcomes: Clinical-only AUC 0.684; radiomics-only 0.700; clinical+TC 0.689; clinical+TB 0.541
extraction_note: Positive class labelled as non-major response in ROC analysis (AUC reported for that coding). Clinical features are MRI-derived visual reads so modality kept radiology_imaging (rule 9). No CI reported for AUC (p-value from shuffle-null only). Funding statement not found in PDF text. 3 of 72 labelled via sustained clinical complete response surrogate.

title: Evaluating treatment response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer using various MRI-based radiomics models.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma (>=cT3 or N+) treated with nCRT then TME
stage_detail: >=cT3 or N+ (baseline); ypT/ypN reported in Table 2
data_source_detail: Changhai Hospital, Shanghai, June 2016-June 2019; 80 of 114 assessed patients; pre- and post-nCRT 3.0 T high-resolution T2WI (Siemens and GE scanners)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Evaluate treatment response (TRG and pCR) to nCRT to aid treatment decisions, e.g. reassessing need for TME / watch-and-wait
treatment_context: nCRT: 50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions plus oral capecitabine, then TME
data_modality_detail: Radiomics (PyRadiomics, Radcloud) from pre- and post-nCRT high-resolution T2-weighted MRI
algorithm: LASSO or PCA feature reduction, then logistic regression, random forest, decision tree and KNN classifiers with leave-one-out CV
input_features: 2818 radiomic features (1409 pre + 1409 post nCRT); 2561 robust (ICC>=0.8); LASSO selected 3 (TRG) or 11 (pCR); PCA top 5 components
comparator_detail: Four classifiers (LR, RF, DT, KNN) and two reduction methods (LASSO vs PCA) compared with DeLong tests
primary_outcome: pCR (ypT0N0) vs non-pCR (selected as primary model; second target TRG 0-1 vs 2-3)
performance_source: Abstract; Results (Radiomics models of pCR classification); Table 3; n=80 (LOOCV)
validation_detail: Leave-one-out cross-validation within a single-center cohort; no external or hold-out validation; unclear whether feature selection was nested within LOOCV
funding: National Key Clinical Specialist Construction Programs of China; Youth initiative fund of Naval Medical University (2018QN05)
key_finding: In 80 LARC patients, LASSO-reduced radiomics from pre/post-nCRT T2WI gave LOOCV AUC 0.943 (RF, TRG) and 0.945 (KNN, pCR), superior to PCA reduction and net benefit on DCA.
limitations_as_stated: Manual segmentation; retrospective single-center; no external validation, small uneven sample; clinical factors (tumor markers, molecular) not included
other_models_outcomes: TRG good vs poor response: RF/LASSO AUC 0.943, RF/PCA 0.930; other classifiers lower (see performance_value)
extraction_note: Two co-primary targets (TRG and pCR) with several models; chose pCR/KNN/LASSO as best AUC (0.945 vs 0.943 for TRG/RF), rule 2b; the conclusion does not single out one model (needs_review). Inputs include post-nCRT MRI, so model is a post-treatment response assessment rather than pretreatment prediction. Two authors affiliated with Huiying Medical Technology (Radcloud platform vendor); COI statement says none. Consent for publication statement reported although consent waived.

title: MRI Radiomics for Prediction of Tumor Response and Downstaging in Rectal Cancer Patients after Preoperative Chemoradiation.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer without distant metastases, treated with nCRT then TME
data_source_detail: University of California Davis, Sept 2010-Feb 2018; 39 patients; 1.5 T GE Signa HDxt pre- and post-CRT high-resolution T2WI
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict response (pCR, good response TRG 0-1, T-downstaging) to nCRT to aid patient-tailored treatment (intensification, organ/sphincter preservation)
treatment_context: nCRT (infusional 5-FU or capecitabine/UFT concurrent) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Radiomics (IBEX, 294 features) from pre-CRT, post-CRT T2WI and delta features; clinical N stage included in the best GR model
algorithm: Univariate Wilcoxon + correlation filtering, then Gaussian-kernel SVM multivariate classification with leave-one-out validation
input_features: 38 independent radiomic features (pre-CRT, post-CRT, delta) plus clinical variables (age, sex, cT, cN, grade, chemo type)
comparator_detail: Pre-CRT vs post-CRT vs delta-radiomic models (permutation test, no significant difference)
primary_outcome: Good response (TRG 0-1) vs non-GR (TRG 2-3) after nCRT
performance_value: GR vs non-GR, pre-CRT global minimum + cN stage: training (LOO) accuracy 100%, test 100% (n=7); post-CRT cN + 0.025 quantile + local entropy min: train 100%, test 83.3%; pCR vs non-pCR pre-CRT GLRLM-GLN + max 3D diameter: train 92.3%, test 57.1%; T-downstaging pre-CRT GLCM-correlation+NIDM+GLCM-variance: train 92.3%, test 71.4%; post-CRT NIDM busyness: train 92.3%, test 50.0%
performance_source: Results (SVM-based multivariate classification); Table 2; test n=7

input_features: 4 radiomic texture features
comparator_detail: Alternative feature selection schemes (mRMR, LASSO), 2-6 features and whole-GTV features (hold-out AUC 0.634); univariate clinical/MRI variables non-significant
primary_outcome: Pathologic complete response (AJCC TRG 0 vs 1-3)
performance_value: Hold-out external (n=44; 10 pCR): AUC 0.712, accuracy 70.5, sensitivity 70.0 (7/10), specificity 70.6 (24/34); discovery CV (n=60, 50 runs of 3-fold): AUC 0.699 +/- 0.076; whole-GTV model: discovery AUC 0.595, hold-out AUC 0.634 (accuracy 63.6, sens 30, spec 73.5)

title: Predicting the Response to FOLFOX-Based Chemotherapy Regimen from Untreated Liver Metastases on Baseline CT: a Deep Neural Network Approach.

input_features: Bounding boxes or segmentations of all untreated lesions on baseline CT

Test N not stated: n_train 267, n_test/n_performance 76 derived: 70%/20% of 381 lesions; text says 27 of 34 poor responders correct (79%), at odds with specificity 59.5%; Discussion refers to TACE-treated lesions and TACE classification although regimen studied is FOLFOX. title: Radiomics performs comparable to morphologic assessment by expert radiologists for prediction of response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy on baseline staging MRI in rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma (non-mucinous) treated with long-course CRT
data_source_detail: Maastricht UMC (center 1, n=86) and Zuyderland Medical Center Heerlen (center 2, n=47), 2007-2013, baseline staging MRI

input_features: Radiomic features (intensity, texture, shape) from T2W, DWI and ADC; only 415 stable features eligible

primary_outcome: Good response (TRG1-2) to CRT; second outcome complete response (ypT0/TRG1 or sustained cCR >2 y in W&W)
performance_value: Good response, center 2 validation, radiomics exp_segm1 0.79 [0.66-0.93], exp_segm2 0.69, non-exp_segm1 0.78, non-exp_segm2 0.70, semi-automatic 0.60 (ns); radiologists R1 0.68, R2 0.67. Complete response, center 2: radiomics exp_segm1 0.77 [0.58-0.96], exp_segm2 0.69 (ns), non-exp_segm1 0.73 [0.51-0.94], non-exp_segm2 0.66 (ns), semi-aut 0.63 (ns); radiologists R1 0.83, R2 0.74. performance_source: Table 4 (center 2 validation, good response, exp_segm1); Results text

funding: Dutch Cancer Society (KWF) grant 2016-2/10611
conflicts_of_interest: Dr. Aerts declares stock options in Sphera and Genospace; other authors none
key_finding: Radiomics from baseline MRI with manually corrected segmentations achieved external AUC 0.69-0.79 (good response) and 0.73-0.77 (complete response, only 2 of 4 models significant), comparable to expert radiologists (0.67-0.83); semi-automatic segmentations alone not significant.
limitations_as_stated: Small dataset with wide CIs, overfitting risk (strong regularization), subjective radiologist scoring, only locally advanced tumors, needs multicenter validation
other_models_outcomes: Complete-response radiomics models (exp_segm1 AUC 0.77 external); models per segmentation; radiologists R1/R2 AUC 0.83/0.74 complete, 0.68/0.67 good; no significant differences radiomics vs radiologists (DeLong P 0.18-0.93)
extraction_note: Multiple co-primary models (good vs complete response, 5 segmentations) with no declared winner and no conclusion-anchored model; chose best external AUC (good response, expert segmentation 1). n_performance 46: 1 center-2 patient lacked TRG (3 in center 1, so train 83). Feature details in Supplementary 2 not needed.

title: Radiomics Model Based on Non-Contrast CT Shows No Predictive Power for Complete Pathological Response in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal carcinoma treated with neoadjuvant CRT then TME
data_source_detail: Consecutive patients, University of Leipzig, 2010-2018, single CT scanner (planning non-contrast CT)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict pCR after neoadjuvant chemoradiation from non-contrast planning CT radiomics (replication of Bibault et al.)
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant CRT (mean 50.4 Gy, infusional 5-FU) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Non-contrast treatment-planning CT; 1819 radiomics features from manually segmented tumor
algorithm: Random forest (default parameters) with recursive feature elimination (63 features), 100x repeated 4-fold CV
input_features: CT radiomic features (shape, first-order, texture, filtered/wavelet)
comparator_detail: Same pipeline run on computer-generated random data as negative control
primary_outcome: pCR vs non-pCR after neoadjuvant CRT

other_models_outcomes: NR

title: Predicting pathological complete response by comparing MRI-based radiomics pre- and postneoadjuvant radiotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma treated with nCRT then TME
stage_detail: cT3-4 or N+ (c-Stage II-III); cT3 ~57-78%, cT4 11-34%, cN2 ~54-67% per Table 1
data_source_detail: Consecutive LARC patients, Xiangya Hospital, Mar 2011-Mar 2018; random 2:1 split into primary and validation cohorts

treatment_context: nCRT (46-50 Gy/23-25 fx + 5-FU/capecitabine or mFOLFOX6/CAPOX) then TME
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted MRI pre-nRT and within 1 week post-nRT; delta of 165 IBEX radiomics features (post minus pre); post-treatment imaging required
algorithm: LASSO logistic regression (10-fold CV for lambda) producing 7-feature Rad-score; multivariable logistic regression
input_features: Delta radiomic features (7 selected: GOH-Skewness, GLRLM-RLNU, ID-Local Entropy Max, ID-Local Range Min, NIDM-Coarseness, max 3D diameter, surface area density); clinical variables tested in multivariable analysis
comparator_detail: NR (clinical factors only in multivariable model)
primary_outcome: pCR (ypT0N0, TRG 0) vs non-pCR
performance_value: Primary cohort AUC 0.92 (0.86-0.99); validation cohort AUC 0.87 (0.74-1.00); Rad-score OR 23.581 (4.445-125.090) multivariable

validation_detail: Random 2:1 split of single-center cohort (87 primary, 44 validation); "independent cohort" is a random internal hold-out

key_finding: Delta T2 MRI radiomics signature (7 features) distinguished pCR in the random hold-out cohort (AUC 0.87) and was an independent predictor of pCR (OR 23.6).

title: Prediction of Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy by MRI-Based Machine Learning Texture Analysis in Rectal Cancer Patients.
