title: Predicting the tumor response to chemoradiotherapy for rectal cancer: Model development and external validation using MRI radiomics.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma treated with CRT then TME
stage_detail: Development: cT3-4N0 or T1-4N1-2; validation: T4Nx or TxN2 or T3 with threatened mesorectal fascia (mucinous excluded)
data_source_detail: Development: 70 of 85 patients from a prospective clinical trial (2012-2015, Philips Ingenia 3T); validation: 55 patients from an observational prospective study (2008-2011, Philips AchievaTX 3T); authors at Leuven, sites not stated explicitly
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict (near-)complete pathological response (ypT0-1N0) to CRT to select patients for organ-preserving strategies (watch-and-wait/local excision)
treatment_context: CRT (45-50 Gy + 5-FU or capecitabine) then TME
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted MRI and DW-MRI (b800, ADC) before and after CRT; 2131 radiomic features per sequence plus 4 semantic volumetric/ADC parameters (post-CRT imaging required)
algorithm: Standardization + PCA + LASSO logistic regression; 42 models developed with 5-fold CV tuning, 3 selected by precision and AUC>0.75
input_features: Quantitative radiomic features from T2, b800 and ADC pre/post CRT, with or without four semantic parameters (DeltaVolume%, Sphere_post, ADC_avg_post, ADCratio_avg)
comparator_detail: Previously established four-feature semantic MRI model (AUC 0.87 in validation); radiomics models did not outperform it
primary_outcome: (Near-)complete pathological response ypT0-1N0
performance_value: External validation: semantic_dwi_post AUC 0.86 (0.76-0.97), PPV 80%, sens 33%, spec 97%; t2_dwi_pre_post 0.83 (0.70-0.95), PPV 80%, sens 33%, spec 97%; semantic_dwi_adc_pre 0.49 (0.24-0.74); four-feature semantic model 0.87 (0.76-0.97). Development CV: t2_dwi_pre_post 0.83 (0.73-0.93, sens 50, spec 90, PPV 67); semantic_dwi_adc_pre 0.86 (0.75-0.98); semantic_dwi_post 0.84 (0.75-0.94, sens 63, spec 88, PPV 67)
performance_source: Results text (validation cohort), Table 2, Abstract (CI 0.76-0.97 in text, abstract 0.76-0.97)
validation_detail: Separate independent cohort (different period, scanner and protocol) of 55 patients, from prospective studies but model applied retrospectively; one validation cohort; institution(s) not stated, so external site status assumed per authors
funding: Belgian IWT agency; FWO fellowships; De Drie Lichten and Dr. Catharine van Tussenbroek foundations; NIBIB R01EB020527; funders had no role

other_models_outcomes: t2_dwi_pre_post (pure radiomics, post-CRT data) external AUC 0.83 (0.70-0.95); semantic_dwi_adc_pre pretreatment external AUC 0.49; four-feature semantic model external AUC 0.87 (0.76-0.97)
extraction_note: Three co-primary selected models, no declared winner; chose best external AUC among radiomics-based models (semantic_dwi_post, 0.86), alternative is t2_dwi_pre_post 0.83 (pure radiomics, abstract-first). Both selected models use post-CRT MRI (restaging, not pre-treatment selection). Validation cohort called external by authors but sites not named, coded external_retrospective. Primary-cohort CI text for validation semantic_dwi_post 0.75-0.97 in Results vs abstract 0.76-0.97; used 0.76-0.97.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics Predicts Tumor Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.

title: Machine learning for prediction of chemoradiation therapy response in rectal cancer using pre-treatment and mid-radiation multi-parametric MRI.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer without distant metastasis (AJCC), CRT then TME
stage_detail: LARC by AJCC TNM, no distant metastasis (examples cT3N+M0); stage distribution not tabulated
data_source_detail: 51 LARC patients receiving neoadjuvant CRT: 45 with pre-treatment MRI, 41 with mid-RT MRI, 35 with both; 3.0T GE Signa HDxt; institution not stated in methods (authors from Hangzhou, China and US)

performance_value: pCR ROI+radiomics ANN AUC: pre-treatment 0.80 (n=45), mid-RT 0.82 (n=41), both 0.86 (n=35); GR: 0.91, 0.92, 0.93; CNN pCR mean AUC 0.59/0.74/0.83, GR 0.52/0.55/0.74
performance_source: Table 2 (pCR vs non-pCR, pre-treatment + mid-RT, ROI+Radiomics); Abstract

extraction_note: Co-primary models across time points with no declared winner; chose conclusion-anchored combined pre-treatment + mid-RT ROI+radiomics pCR (AUC 0.86, n=35), which is also the best pCR AUC. Mid-RT inputs are not available at baseline decision; pre-treatment-only pCR AUC 0.80 (n=45) is in other_models_outcomes. Performance evaluated on the entire dataset by pooled CV predictions; no CIs reported. Setting/country not stated in methods; COI statement absent from the author manuscript text.

title: Radiomics-Based Pretherapeutic Prediction of Non-response to Neoadjuvant Therapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.

title: Delta Radiomics and Tumor Size: A New Predictive Radiomics Model for Chemotherapy Response in Liver Metastases from Breast and Colorectal Cancer.

key_finding: ResNeXt50-based CCIM-Net on 7-colour mIHC images predicted chemotherapy response with AUC 0.99 in an independent 45-patient test set; FOLR2+ macrophage targeting enhanced chemotherapy response in mice.
limitations_as_stated: Background differences between in-house biopsy and public cohorts; two in-house samples dominate myeloid/epithelial populations; multicenter validation and clinical trials needed
other_models_outcomes: CCIM score (transcriptomic) stratified prognosis in training (n=1405) and 4-5 validation cohorts (n=682); FOLR2-RM neural network AUC 0.797
extraction_note: Stage and detailed clinical data only in supplementary tables S7/S8 (stage_context NR). Mixed multiomics/in vivo study; main model CCIM-Net taken as the one named in the summary. Best of seven listed architectures (text says 8) chosen on the test cohort itself, with test AUC 0.99 n=45 (small test set, selection on test performance). Whether the test cohort is from a different center is stated ambiguously ("two cohorts from different centers"). Study design not stated (coded other).

title: An automated deep learning pipeline for EMVI classification and response prediction of rectal cancer using baseline MRI: a multi-centre study.
tumor_site_detail: Non-metastatic biopsy-proven rectal adenocarcinoma
stage_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer undergoing long-course nCRT (cT1-2 7%, cT3 81%, cT4 12%; cN0 13%, cN1 24%, cN2 63%)
data_source_detail: Dutch multicentre dataset (9 centres, 2008-2018): development 317 (6 centres; 4 train, 2 internal validation 95) and external validation 97 (3 centres)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Baseline MRI EMVI classification as prognostic risk-stratification marker (primary task); secondary task: complete response prediction to inform subsequent treatment plans/organ preservation
treatment_context: Long-course neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (50-50.4 Gy + capecitabine-based chemotherapy)
data_modality_detail: Baseline MRI: DWI (high b-value) and T2W
algorithm: nnUNet tumour segmentation + MLNet (3D ResNet10 with injected multi-level nnUNet feature maps)
input_features: Baseline DWI (pipeline DWI) or DWI+T2W images plus nnUNet multi-level feature maps
comparator_detail: Logistic regression on age, gender, cT, cN (external AUC 0.62); ablations: plain 3D ResNet10 and single-stage feature maps
primary_outcome: mrEMVI status (positive vs negative) by expert radiologist on baseline MRI
performance_value: EMVI external (n=97), DWI pipeline: AUC 0.76 (0.66-0.84), sens 0.67, spec 0.70; DWI+T2W external 0.73 (0.62-0.83); internal DWI 0.76 (0.66-0.85), DWI+T2W 0.78 (0.68-0.87); clinical LR 0.62; ResNet10 0.51. CR task external: DWI+T2W 0.66 (0.55-0.77), DWI 0.62 (0.49-0.73), LR 0.53; segmentation mDice external 0.73 (DWI), 0.74 (DWI+T2W)
performance_source: Table 3 (EMVI, external cohort); Results text
validation_detail: Temporal/centre-wise split: 4 centres train, 2 centres internal validation, 3 different centres as external validation (n=97); 4-fold CV for segmentation
funding: EU Horizon 2020 Marie Sklodowska-Curie grant 857894
key_finding: Fully automated nnUNet+MLNet pipeline on baseline MRI classified EMVI (external AUC 0.76) and predicted complete response (external AUC 0.66, DWI+T2W) with generalisation to external centres.
limitations_as_stated: Low sensitivity/PPV for CR; no standardised MRI response protocol; EMVI reference by radiologist MRI not pathology; heterogeneous long-period data and scanners; only 509 Dutch patients; retrospective; no CEA/other modalities
other_models_outcomes: CR prediction (co-primary): external AUC 0.66 (0.55-0.77) DWI+T2W, 0.62 DWI; Schurink clinical-imaging model AUC 0.60 on same external cohort; CR defined as pCR or sustained cCR >2 years
extraction_note: Co-primary tasks (EMVI and CR). Per rule 2(a) the conclusion states pipeline applicable "particularly for EMVI classification", so EMVI/MLNet DWI chosen as main (best external AUC 0.76) and CR moved to other_models_outcomes; therapeutic_decision coded other because EMVI is a staging/prognostic marker; if CR were primary it would be neoadjuvant_response (external AUC 0.66, n=97).

title: Deep radiomics-based fusion model for prediction of bevacizumab treatment response and outcome in patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases: a multicentre cohort study.
tumor_site_detail: Colorectal cancer with initially unresectable liver-limited/liver-dominant metastases, RAS-mutant
stage_detail: Initially unresectable CRLM (synchronous), RAS-mutant, first-line conversion therapy
data_source_detail: BECOME trial (NCT01972490) Arm A as training (n=103) and Arm B as negative-control cohort (n=37); consecutive Zhongshan Hospital (ZSH) cohort 2018 (internal validation n=65); external cohort 2020 from Zhongshan Hospital-Xiamen and First Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University (n=102); histology cohort n=82 (patients with biopsies drawn from training/internal cohorts)
n_source: Methods "Study design"; Results "Study cohort" and Table 1/Fig 2
therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify bevacizumab-sensitive patients with unresectable CRLM before conversion therapy; non-sensitive could receive intensified chemotherapy (FOLFOXIRI) without bevacizumab
treatment_context: mFOLFOX6/FOLFOX plus bevacizumab (conversion therapy)
data_modality_detail: Baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT of liver metastases + clinical factors (SUVmax, preoperative CEA, primary tumour site) + IHC scores (GLUT1, PKM) of colonoscopy biopsy
algorithm: DERBY+: ResNet-34 (CT) and EfficientNet-b3 (PET) deep features, GMM transformation, random forest classifier with LASSO-selected clinical and IHC features; weighted voting over image pairs
input_features: Deep PET/CT image features (Fimg), 3 LASSO-selected clinical features, 2 histological IHC scores (GLUT1, PKM)
comparator_detail: Single-signature models (clinical 0.66, imaging 0.72, histological 0.72) and DERBY (no histology) in external cohort; negative control cohort with chemotherapy alone
primary_outcome: Objective response (PR; RECIST 1.1) to first-line bevacizumab plus chemotherapy
performance_value: DERBY+ external validation (n=102): AUC 0.83 (0.75-0.92), sens 0.80, spec 0.77, PPV 0.74, NPV 0.83; histology cohort (n=82) AUC 0.95 (0.91-1.00); negative control (chemo alone, n=37) AUC 0.58 (0.39-0.76); DERBY training 0.92, internal validation 0.84, external 0.77 (0.67-0.87)
performance_source: Table 2; Results "Evaluation and predictive performance of the DERBY+ model"; Abstract
patient_outcomes_detail: DERBY+ predicted responders vs non-responders in external cohort: PFS 9.6 vs 6.3 months (HR 0.52, p=0.002); OS 27.6 vs 18.5 months (HR 0.50, p=0.010); conversion resection 30.0% vs 5.8%
validation_detail: Trained on single-center trial/histology cohort; evaluated in external cohort from two other hospitals (ZSHX, HWMU) with different scanners and geography
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82072653, 81602035, 82172816); Fujian Provincial Health Commission; Xiamen Science and Technology Agency; Clinical Research Plan of SHDC; Shanghai Science and Technology Committee; Zhejiang Provincial Natural Science Foundation; National Science Foundation of Xiamen
key_finding: Multimodal DERBY+ (PET/CT deep features + clinical + IHC) predicted bevacizumab response in an external cohort (AUC 0.83) and stratified PFS/OS; failed in chemotherapy-alone negative control (AUC 0.58).
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective with selection bias (baseline PET/CT and biopsies unavailable for some patients); semi-automatic segmentation needing manual initialisation; IHC markers selected from literature; prospective validation needed (NCT05354674 registered)
other_models_outcomes: DERBY (PET/CT + clinical): training AUC 0.92, internal validation 0.84, external 0.77; single signatures clinical 0.66, imaging 0.72, histological 0.72 (external); DERBY+ decision curve analysis
extraction_note: DERBY+ chosen as main model (title/interpretation: multimodal PET/CT + clinical + histology; best external AUC) vs DERBY (external AUC 0.77). DERBY+ was trained on the histology cohort (n=82), which is composed of patients drawn from the training and internal validation cohorts (Table 1 note: overlap); the histology-cohort AUC 0.95 is therefore not independent; n_train taken as 82. Some methodological details in online supplement.

title: PAIP 2020: Microsatellite instability prediction in colorectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Colorectal cancer H&E whole-slide images (challenge dataset; title/keywords also say colon cancer)
stage_detail: NR (dataset stage not reported; discussion refers to MSI-H relevance in stage II/III and stage IV)

treatment_context: Immune checkpoint inhibitor eligibility via MSI-H status (no treatment given in study)
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide images (Aperio AT2, 200x) with tumour-area annotations
algorithm: Top-ranked team (Nateghi, SUTECH): FPN with EfficientNet-B5 tumour segmentation, then VGG-16 patch feature extractor + LSTM for slide-level MSI-H vs MSS

comparator_detail: Other top-10 challenge team algorithms (F1 0.7895-0.9048)
primary_outcome: MSI-H vs MSS (reference: MSI-PCR with five Bethesda markers, confirmed by NGS and MMR-IHC)

Test set artificially enriched for MSI-H (50%); F1 only for MSI-H class reported. No patient count given (118 WSIs, one slide per case presumed but not stated); n_unit images. Setting coded multicenter (three SNU-affiliated hospitals).

title: Association of collagen deep learning classifier with prognosis and chemotherapy benefits in stage II-III colon cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Stage II-III colon cancer after R0 radical resection
stage_detail: AJCC 8th stage II-III colon cancer (stage I/IV excluded); adjuvant chemotherapy benefit analysed in high-risk stage II and stage III
data_source_detail: Nanfang Hospital (training n=303, 2009-2011; internal validation n=287, 2012-2013) and Sixth Affiliated Hospital Sun Yat-sen University (external validation n=292, 2013)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict prognosis and identify high-risk stage II/III colon cancer patients who benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy
treatment_context: Adjuvant chemotherapy after radical surgery (received by 495/882, 56.1%; non-randomised)
data_modality_detail: Multiphoton imaging (second-harmonic generation of collagen plus two-photon fluorescence) of unstained serial tumour sections, 3 ROIs of 512 um per section; H&E used to select invasive area
algorithm: collagenDL classifier: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 fine-tuned on multiphoton images (sigmoid output, recurrence probability averaged over 3 images; cut-off 0.436 from training cohort)
input_features: Multiphoton images (224x224) of tumour invasive area
comparator_detail: Clinicopathological model (VELIPI, T stage, N stage) and TNM stage; collagenDL nomogram integrates classifier with these
primary_outcome: Disease-free survival (co-primary overall survival)
performance_value: collagenDL classifier DFS C-index: training 0.699, internal validation 0.692, external 0.697; OS C-index: 0.678, 0.660, 0.692. Nomogram DFS C-index 0.788/0.795/0.778; OS 0.777/0.763/0.822
performance_source: Results 2.2 (C-indexes for DFS, external validation cohort)
patient_outcomes_detail: High vs low collagenDL: 5-yr DFS 59.0% vs 90.6% and OS 68.6% vs 93.2% in training; independent predictor (DFS HR 5.848, 95% CI 3.140-10.890; OS HR 5.382, 2.538-11.411); high-collagenDL patients benefited from adjuvant chemotherapy, low did not (interaction analysis)
validation_detail: Training and temporally separate internal validation from Nanfang Hospital; independent external validation cohort from a second hospital (single external site)
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82103041, 82273360); China Postdoctoral Science Foundation (2020M682789); President Foundation of Nanfang Hospital (2019Z023); Sixth Affiliated Hospital Sun Yat-sen University grants
key_finding: ResNet-50 collagen classifier on multiphoton images stratified DFS/OS in stage II-III colon cancer (external DFS C-index 0.697) and identified patients who benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy; nomogram added incremental value over clinicopathology/TNM.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective multicenter design; adjuvant chemotherapy choice not random; prospective validation needed; MMR/MSI status not tested for all patients
other_models_outcomes: collagenDL nomograms (classifier + T, N, VELIPI): DFS C-index 0.788/0.795/0.778 and OS 0.777/0.763/0.822 (training/internal/external); clinicopathological model and TNM comparators in supplement
extraction_note: Classifier (title) chosen as main model over nomogram; DFS taken as primary (listed first; OS external C-index 0.692). Stage II-III adjuvant coded early_resectable. Chemotherapy-benefit interaction values (Table S8) and comparator C-indexes (Table S4) only in supplement. Optimal cut-off derived in training cohort.

title: Tumor-infiltrating immune cells based TMEscore and related gene signature is associated with the survival of CRC patients and response to fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy.
tumor_site_detail: CRC (GEO/TCGA cohorts)
stage_detail: GSE72970 (TMEscore derivation) metastatic CRC only; other pooled cohorts (GSE39582, TCGA, etc.) stage not reported
data_source_detail: GEO GSE72970 (124), GSE39582 (585), GSE87211 (363), GSE104645 (193), GSE28702 (83); TCGA-COADREAD (635); expression-validation GEO sets and 40 clinical tumor/adjacent pairs (RT-PCR)
n_source: derived: 124+585+363+193+83 listed GEO datasets + 635 TCGA (Methods); text says 2061 GEO patients
therapeutic_decision_detail: predict response to fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy / precise treatment options
treatment_context: Fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy (FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX, +/- bevacizumab)
data_modality_detail: Gene expression microarray; CIBERSORT immune cell fractions; TMEscore
algorithm: SVM, decision tree and XGBoost for key-gene selection (7:3 split); 3-gene (ADH1C, SLC26A2, NANS) multivariate logistic regression signature; TMEscore by PCA
input_features: Expression of 3 genes (from 2267 TIIC-related DEGs)
comparator_detail: Individual ML key-gene sets (XGBoost/SVM/DT) vs 3-gene logistic signature; TMEscore alone
primary_outcome: Response (CR+PR vs SD+PD) to fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy
performance_value: 3-gene signature: external GSE104645 AUC 0.616; external GSE28702 AUC 0.719; TCGA 5-FU-only subset (n=36) AUC 0.764; discovery/training logistic AUC 0.867; ML key genes internal test AUC XGBoost 0.690, SVM 0.663, DT 0.729; TMEscore (GSE72970, n=124) AUC 0.642
performance_source: Results, Validation of the three-gene signature; Figure 6A (GSE104645)
patient_outcomes_detail: TMEscore high vs low associated with better survival (KM) in GSE72970, GSE39582, GSE87211, TCGA; signature predicts response better than survival

extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: text states 2061 GEO patients but listed datasets sum to 1348; train/test 768/321 (1089) cannot be reconciled with response-labelled datasets. Primary model = 3-gene signature (title/conclusion); two external cohorts, chose GSE104645 (larger, n=193; 0.616) vs GSE28702 (0.719). stage_context coded mixed_all_stages (pooled cohorts; TMEscore derived in metastatic GSE72970). Public datasets, sites not stated so external_retrospective not multicenter. Multiple datasets pooled for gene selection with test-set used to select genes.

title: Gene-Mutation-Based Algorithm for Prediction of Treatment Response in Colorectal Cancer Patients.
tumor_site_detail: CRC; MSK unresectable CRC (82% distant metastasis) and TCGA CRC
stage_detail: MSK: stage I 2%, II 7%, III 19%, IV 73%; TCGA: I 4%, II 24%, III 65%, IV 7% (Table 1)
data_source_detail: cBioPortal MSK cohort (n=471; training) and TCGA Firehose Legacy (n=191 of 221; validation)
therapeutic_decision_detail: predict treatment response (progression vs non-progression after first-line chemotherapy) at diagnosis for personalized therapy

input_features: Mutation status of 7 genes
comparator_detail: Cancer stage, adjuvant therapy, surgery on primary, MSI, and their combination (logistic regression)
primary_outcome: Progression vs non-progression after treatment (responder vs non-responder) during 50-month follow-up
performance_value: TCGA validation: AUC 0.97 (95% CI 0.95-0.99), sens 96%, spec 77%; MSK training: AUC 0.98 (0.95-1.02), sens 83%, spec 98%, PPV 74%, NPV 99%; PFS HR 16.9 (7.2-39.6) MSK and TCGA
performance_source: Results 3.4 and Table 2 (TCGA); Figure 5A
patient_outcomes_detail: High algorithm score associated with worse PFS (HR 16.9, p<0.001) in MSK and TCGA
validation_detail: Trained on MSK (471), tested on TCGA subset; single external dataset; no prospective validation
funding: EU REVERT (848098), Swedish Cancer Society, Swedish Research Council, Umea University and others

other_models_outcomes: Clinical comparators AUC: stage 0.50, adjuvant therapy 0.41, surgery on primary 0.41, MSI 0.34 (MSK); combination similar to 7-gene alone
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: abstract gives AUC 0.97 (MSK) and 0.98 (TCGA) but Results give 0.98 (MSK) and 0.97 (TCGA); TCGA n given as 221, 191 (Table 1/2) and 119 (Section 3.4). Used Results/Table values and n=191. Marked class counts in Table 1 imply very few responders (MSK 24 non-progressed); extreme AUC/specificity with low prevalence; MSK performance evaluated on training data (not CV). Employed 10-fold CV only for gene-combination selection.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of Microsatellite-Related Transcriptomic Signature and Identify Its Clinical Value in Colon Cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Colon adenocarcinoma (TCGA-COAD, R0 resection)
stage_detail: TNM stage used as covariate; stage distribution NR in text; R0-resected only
data_source_detail: TCGA-COAD (UCSC Xena, n=318 after R0 filter); GSE39582 (prognostic validation, n NR); GSE146771 (scRNA-seq)
n_source: Methods and Figure 1 (318 TCGA-COAD samples); GSE39582 n not reported
therapeutic_decision_detail: MSRS as predictor of response to immunotherapy (and prognostic factor) in colon cancer
treatment_context: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (response inferred via TIDE score cutoff 1.0); cisplatin sensitivity via pRRophetic
data_modality_detail: Bulk RNA-seq (FPKM) and scRNA-seq; MSI-related DEGs
algorithm: LASSO Cox regression (MSRS, 24 genes); separate 3-hidden-layer neural network (100/50/25) to predict MSI status from 238 DEGs
input_features: Expression of 24 genes (MSRS); 238 DEGs (NN)
comparator_detail: Age, gender and TNM stage in time-dependent ROC / multivariable Cox
primary_outcome: Predicted immunotherapy response (TIDE-based responder vs non-responder) and overall survival
performance_value: MSRS for TIDE-inferred immunotherapy response AUC 0.624 (TCGA-COAD, n=318); cisplatin AUC 0.548; time-dependent AUC for OS >0.8 most of the time (figure only); NN for MSI status Kappa 0.706 (30% test)
performance_source: Results, Associations between the MSRS and Response to Immunotherapy; Figure 8E
patient_outcomes_detail: High MSRS associated with poor OS in TCGA-COAD and GSE39582; independent after adjusting for age, sex, TNM

key_finding: MSRS is a robust prognostic factor for OS but a barely satisfactory predictor of immunotherapy response (AUC 0.624, TIDE-inferred).
limitations_as_stated: RNA-seq not routine in clinic; different expression platforms need standardization; in-silico immune estimation; many censored survival data in TCGA-COAD.

extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: text says prognostic validation in GSE39582 (Methods/Results/Abstract) but Discussion cites GSE146771 as the validation cohort. Response label is the TIDE algorithm output (surrogate), not observed treatment response; ICI-response AUC derived in-sample. Primary outcome choice: abstract highlights both OS prognosis and ICI-response AUC; chose ICI-response AUC (only numeric headline) as primary metric, validation coded as outcome_association (OS in GSE39582); performance_cohort set to train because no held-out data. conflicts_of_interest: no statement in PDF text read.

title: Histopathologic and Molecular Biomarkers of PD-1/PD-L1 Inhibitor Treatment Response among Patients with Microsatellite Instability‒High Colon Cancer.

title: Identifying Cell Type-Specific Chemokine Correlates with Hierarchical Signal Extraction from Single-Cell Transcriptomes.
tumor_site_detail: MMR classification in CRC (colorectal atlas, 60 patients); ICI-response task pooled across tissue types (incl. non-CRC)
stage_detail: NR; public single-cell datasets without clinical stage context
data_source_detail: GEO scRNA-seq: GSE178341 (CRC atlas), GSE123814, GSE120575, GSE144469 (ICI response); GSE146771 and GSE132465 (independent CRC MMR validation); simulated scRNA-seq (20,000 cells)
n_source: Results 3.2.3 (60-patient CRC atlas, GSE178341); ICI-response and independent-dataset patient counts not reported
therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify cell type-specific chemokine correlates of ICI response and of DNA mismatch repair status (MMRd) for determining prognosis and treatment
treatment_context: PD-1/immune checkpoint inhibitors (response task); MMR status as ICI-eligibility proxy

input_features: Chemokine and chemokine-receptor expression of 100 sampled cells per pseudo-sample
comparator_detail: Logistic regression, RNN, LSTM, GRU
primary_outcome: dMMR vs pMMR classification of CRC tissue samples (secondary task: ICI response RECIST R vs NR)
performance_value: MMR task: atlas held-out test AUC 0.8701 +/- 0.0954; independent GSE146771 colon10x 0.8691 +/- 0.2201, GSE146771 colonSS2 0.9041 +/- 0.0843, GSE132465 colon10x 0.7275 +/- 0.0321; ICI response (pooled datasets) test AUC 0.7583 +/- 0.1588 (50 random splits); simulated AUC 1.000
performance_source: Table 4 (GSE132465 colon10x); Table 3 and Table 2 for other tasks

other_models_outcomes: ICI response prediction (multi-tissue) AUC 0.7583 vs LogReg 0.7119, RNN 0.6443, LSTM 0.6889, GRU 0.7028; simulated-data experiments
extraction_note: Method paper; CRC-specific task = MMR classification (used as primary, ICI-response task is pooled multi-tissue, scRNA datasets of non-CRC origin e.g. melanoma). Three independent test rows in Table 4 (two datasets); chose GSE132465 (an independent group dataset; lowest AUC, most demanding) as primary; others in performance_value. Patient Ns for external sets not reported. Labels are MMR status, not treatment response, for the CRC task.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-radiomics evaluation of response to chemotherapy for synchronous liver metastasis of colorectal cancer.

data_modality_detail: 3.0T MRI (T2WI, DWI, portal-phase CE) radiomics, 396 features per sequence (1188 total); nomogram adds CA19-9 and clinical N stage

title: Treatment response prediction using MRI-based pre-, post-, and delta-radiomic features and machine learning algorithms in colorectal cancer.

primary_outcome: Pathologic response (AJCC/CAP TRG 0-1 responder vs 2-4 non-responder)

performance_source: Abstract; Results 3.3; Tables 3 and 4 (delta, RF, AUC)

Delta features require the post-nCRT MRI (4 weeks after nCRT), so not a purely pre-treatment predictor. Test n=17 with bootstrap CIs (narrow). Training and external classes: 15/21 responders in training, 11 responders of 17 in external. Hyperparameters tuned by 1000 bootstraps in train data; ComBat harmonization fitted across both centers.

comparator_detail: Radiomics-only (RI) and clinical-only (RC) XGBoost models

title: Multi-modal radiomics model to predict treatment response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer.

stage_detail: T3-T4b, N0-N2, no distant metastasis (cT/N by imaging)

algorithm: mRMR + LASSO feature selection, SMOTE balancing, logistic regression; nomogram (radiomics score + EMVI)

Combined radiomics model: validation AUC 0.908, train 0.921. EMVI: validation AUC 0.578, train 0.73. HR-T2WI validation AUC 0.859; ADC 0.828; DCE-T1 0.812; CT 0.766

key_finding: Multi-modal CT+MRI radiomics nomogram (radiomics score + EMVI) predicted response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in LARC with validation AUC 0.93, outperforming single-sequence models and EMVI alone (though differences vs single sequences were not significant).
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective with possible selection bias; small sample because the neoadjuvant chemotherapy protocol is new at the hospital; results need testing with other protocols/CRT; biological markers (HER2, Ki-67) not available in all patients.
other_models_outcomes: Validation AUC: HR-T2WI 0.859, ADC 0.828, DCE-T1 0.812, CT 0.766, combined radiomics 0.908, EMVI 0.578

title: Deep learning-based radiomic features for improving neoadjuvant chemoradiation response prediction in locally advanced rectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Locally advanced rectal cancer
data_source_detail: 43 consecutive LARC patients treated Dec 2015-Dec 2016 at a single institution (country not stated in text; inferred from affiliation of Cancer Hospital CAMS, Beijing)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict response to nCRT; early prediction may allow individualized management and potential avoidance of TME
treatment_context: Neoadjuvant chemoradiation (capecitabine + 50 Gy/25 fx) followed by TME
data_modality_detail: Pre-treatment DWI-derived ADC map (MRI), GTV contoured
algorithm: Pre-trained VGG19 (ImageNet) deep features + LASSO-penalized logistic regression
input_features: 105 DL-based features (from 1472, highest variance) from ADC ROI
comparator_detail: Handcrafted PyRadiomics features (105) + LASSO logistic regression; fused classifier
primary_outcome: Good response (pathologic complete/partial response or MRI/colonoscopy complete response) vs non-good response to nCRT
performance_value: DL-based classifier mean AUC 0.73 (SE 0.05) over 20x repeated stratified 4-fold CV; handcrafted 0.64 (SE 0.08); fused 0.71; corrected resampled t-test p=0.049
performance_source: Results 3.2; Abstract
validation_detail: Repeated (20x) stratified 4-fold CV on the single 43-patient cohort; hyperparameters tuned by grid search in the same CV scheme
funding: NR
key_finding: DL-based (VGG19) radiomic features from pre-treatment ADC maps gave a significantly higher mean CV AUC (0.73) than handcrafted features (0.64) for predicting nCRT response in LARC.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample with unstable accuracy estimates; only 9 pCR patients so pCR vs non-pCR not modeled; single modality (DWI) only; larger dataset needed.
other_models_outcomes: Handcrafted-feature classifier AUC 0.64 (SE 0.08); fused classifier AUC 0.71
extraction_note: Hyperparameter grid search and evaluation both in the same repeated CV (no nested CV stated). Funding/COI not found in PDF text. Country inferred from affiliation. Response label partly based on MRI/colonoscopy, not only pathology.

title: FOLFOX treatment response prediction in metastatic or recurrent colorectal cancer patients via machine learning algorithms.
tumor_site_detail: Metastatic or recurrent colorectal cancer (primary and metastatic lesion biopsies)
stage_detail: Metastatic or recurrent CRC receiving first-line FOLFOX
country: Japan; Europe (REGP/COSIVAL/BIOCOLON cohorts) per GEO dataset table

data_modality_detail: Affymetrix HG-U133 Plus 2.0 expression of 18 candidate DEGs from microarray meta-analysis

input_features: Expression of 18 candidate genes (WASHC4, HELZ, ERN1, RPS6KB1, APPBP2, IRF7, EML3, LYPLA2, DRAP1, RNH1, PKP3, TSPAN17, LSS, MLKL, PPP1R7, GCDH, C19ORF24, CCDC124)

other_models_outcomes: SVM test AUC 0.827; neural network 0.800; applied to FOLFIRI dataset GSE62080: SVM 0.676, RF 0.667, NN 0.778
extraction_note: Authors name SVM and RF jointly as best; RF chosen as primary by highest test AUC (rule 2b). n_test=33 and n_train=50 derived from 60/40 split of 83 and consistent with sens/spec CIs (20 responders, 13 non-responders). n_analytic=83 refers to modelling cohort; 144 specimens used in meta-analysis (the 18 genes were selected using all 3 datasets including GSE28702 test samples: possible feature-selection leakage, stated factually).

title: Predicting Clinical Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer Using Machine Learning.
tumor_site_detail: Colon (55%) and rectal (45%) carcinoma, resected
stage_detail: TNM I-IV; subgroup analyses of stage II (n=134) and III (n=97)

therapeutic_decision_detail: Radio-chemotherapy response (RCT-R) and relapse predictions proposed to help decide for or against neoadjuvant/adjuvant radiochemotherapy

data_modality_detail: RCT-R model used gene expression only (RT-qPCR, 59 genes); relapse/DFS models added localization, epidemiology, cancer type, TNM stage

input_features: mRNA expression of pre-selected genes (RCT-R model)
comparator_detail: Several ML algorithms compared per outcome; stage II relapse model compared with literature risk groups (Merkel) by log-rank
primary_outcome: Radio-chemotherapy response (Dworak 3-4 vs 0-2)
performance_value: RCT-R (C5.0, test): accuracy 0.70, specificity 0.85, sensitivity 0.53. Relapse (glmnet, test): accuracy 0.71, spec 0.73, sens 0.63. DFS C-index 0.76 test; OS C-index 0.86-0.87 test; DFS stage II C-index 0.83 test (1.0 train); DFS stage III C-index 0.20 test (0.98 train); relapse stage III accuracy 0.54 test (0.71 train)
performance_source: Results 3.1 and Discussion; Abstract
patient_outcomes_detail: Stage II relapse-model groups gave stronger survival-curve separation (Kaplan-Meier) than literature risk groups
validation_detail: Test data withheld before model building (split ratio not reported); feature selection used three data splits; no external validation
funding: German Research Foundation (FOR 2438 subproject 2), W. Lutz Stiftung, Forschungsstiftung Medizin, IZKF Clinical Center Erlangen (grants to M.S.)
key_finding: Automated ML pipeline on 564 CRC patients gave test accuracies ~0.70-0.71 for RCT response and relapse and C-index 0.76 (DFS) and 0.87 (OS); stage III models overfit.
limitations_as_stated: Limited data (feature selection split data in three sets; subgroup analyses reduced data); gene importance depends on prediction problem; test data for stage II/III relapse had only 1 and 3 positive cases.
other_models_outcomes: Relapse acc 0.71 (glmnet); OS C-index 0.86-0.87 (glmnet); DFS C-index 0.76 (glmnet); DFS stage II 0.83 (coxph); DFS stage III 0.20 test (rfsrc); relapse stage III acc 0.54; predicting all 5 Dworak levels accuracy 0.40
extraction_note: Multi-outcome study with no single declared primary model. RCT-R (neoadjuvant response) C5.0 model chosen as principal because it is the treatment-response outcome, which the conclusion highlights; relapse (acc 0.71) and survival models listed in other_models_outcomes. Abstract gives OS C-index 0.86, results 0.87. Test-set size, RCT-R sample size and split ratio not reported. Therapeutic axis inherited as other.

title: Urine metabolomics as a predictor of patient tolerance and response to adjuvant chemotherapy in colorectal cancer.

title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Colorectal Cancer Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making: A Retrospective Single-Center Comparison of Guideline-Integrated General-Purpose vs. Domain-Specialized Models.
stage_detail: TNM I 32, II 99, III 117, IV 52; settings adjuvant 217, neoadjuvant 26, metastatic 40, recurrent 17

treatment_context: Multimodality CRC management across adjuvant, neoadjuvant, metastatic and recurrent settings
data_modality_detail: De-identified standardized case summaries (~3200 tokens) mirroring MTB presentation
algorithm: Gemini 2.5 (cloud, NCI guidelines in-context ~85k tokens, T=1.0); MedGemma 27B text-it (local, no guidelines, T=0.0 and T=1.0)

MedGemma T=0: kappa 0.566, accuracy 70.3%, F1 0.64, recall 0.61, full concordance 57.0%, safe 62.3%. title: Comprehensive machine learning analysis of a radiomics-based model for predicting microsatellite instability in right Colon Cancer.

performance_value: Habitat+Peri-5 test AUC 0.870 (95%CI 0.786-0.954), acc 0.853, sens 0.800, spec 0.867; train AUC 0.994 (Table 3). Clinical test AUC 0.697; Intra 0.769; Peri-5 0.825; Peri-10 0.816; Habitat 0.812
performance_source: Table 3 (test cohort, Habitat + Peri-5)
patient_outcomes_detail: Only immediate/early local ablation response; no survival outcomes
validation_detail: Random 4:1 split at lesion level (412/103); multiple lesions per patient; single center; no external validation
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82272095); Shanghai Anticancer Association EYAS Project
key_finding: Habitat+Peri-5 radiomics signature achieved the best test AUC for immediate RFA response, above clinical and intratumoral signatures.
limitations_as_stated: Single-center retrospective, limited sample size; habitats not pathologically confirmed; needs multicenter prospective validation
other_models_outcomes: Test AUC: Clinical 0.697, Intra 0.769, Peri-5 0.825, Peri-10 0.816, Habitat 0.812 (Table 3)
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: Results text gives Habitat+Peri-5 test AUC 0.846 whereas abstract, Discussion and Table 3 give 0.870; Table 3 value used. Lesion-level random split (515 lesions from 233 patients) so lesions of the same patient may fall in both train and test; train AUC 0.994 in Table 3 vs 0.972 in text.

title: A computed tomography-based multitask deep learning model for predicting tumour stroma ratio and treatment outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer: a multicentre cohort study.

stage_detail: Resected CRC; 1846/2268 (81.4%) stage II-III per Results; AJCC 8th pTNM

therapeutic_decision_detail: Noninvasively predict TSR and prognosis; secondary aim: predict benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in stage II/III
treatment_context: Adjuvant chemotherapy after radical surgery
data_modality_detail: Preoperative portal-venous CT, largest tumour slice (TSR label from histology WSI via separate DL model)
algorithm: Multitask deep learning network (multiscale features, receptive field attention, MMD-AE) predicting TSR status and overall survival
input_features: Preoperative CT tumour ROI (manual delineation)
comparator_detail: Single-task TSR and survival networks, single-scale model, module ablations, fine-tuned multitask VGG16 and DenseNet121
primary_outcome: Tumour-stroma ratio status (high >50% vs low) on histology; also OS/DFS
performance_source: Results text and Fig 2A; most demanding external cohort chosen as EVC1 (largest, n=509)

limitations_as_stated: Retrospective bias and distribution differences; only largest CT slice used; adjuvant chemotherapy non-randomized; biological meaning of DL features unclear
other_models_outcomes: Survival head: C-index 0.757-0.779 in validation cohorts, 0.672 in EVC3; integrated nomogram (MDLS + clinicopathology) improved prognostic accuracy; single-task TSR AUC 0.799-0.827
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: abstract chemo-benefit HRs (stage II 0.391, stage III 0.467) differ from Results (0.405, 0.446); Results used. Primary outcome is TSR (surrogate histology) and prognosis; adjuvant-chemo selection coded as the clinical claim. Reporting followed STROCSS (coded other). n_test = IVC+EVC1+EVC2 (TSR-evaluated).

title: Identifying Genetic Mutation Status in Patients with Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases Using Radiomics-Based Machine-Learning Models.

stage_detail: Initially unresectable liver-only CRLM (CAIRO5); external NKI cohort of CRLM with biopsy/NGS

therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify KRAS mutation status non-invasively, used in treatment selection (anti-EGFR) and prognostication
treatment_context: Systemic therapy incl. anti-EGFR targeted agents in CRLM
data_modality_detail: Pre-treatment portal-venous contrast CT; radiomics of all CRLM combined into one VOI per patient
algorithm: Random forest, gradient boosting, GB+LightGBM, and voting ensemble on Pyradiomics features (RF-based selection, 10 features)
input_features: 10 selected radiomics features (851 extracted; original and wavelet); ComBat applied to external set
comparator_detail: Comparison among RF, GB, GBM, Ensemble
primary_outcome: KRAS mutant vs wild-type
performance_source: Results text, Fig 5 and Table 2 (external validation, GBM)
validation_detail: Stratified 80:20 split of CAIRO5 (204/51) with 5-fold CV tuning; external validation in one centre (NKI, n=129)
funding: Dutch Cancer Society (KWF) projects 14002/2021-2 and 10438; Cancer Center Amsterdam Foundation unrestricted grant; CAIRO5 supported by unrestricted grants; SAS in-kind support
conflicts_of_interest: C.J.A.P. advisory role Nordic Pharma; H.A.M. co-founder/shareholder of Nicolab; funders had no role
key_finding: Radiomics ML models identified KRAS status with AUC 0.72-0.86 in the internal test set but performed at chance level (AUC 0.47-0.56) in the external cohort.
limitations_as_stated: Selected unresectable CRLM population; slice thickness differences; single radiologist verification; segmentations not tested for feature stability; all CRLM combined assuming uniform mutation status; no RAS/BRAF analysis
other_models_outcomes: Ensemble internal-test AUC 0.86 (0.76-0.95) but external 0.47 (0.37-0.56); RF external 0.54; GB external 0.52
extraction_note: No single declared primary model (four co-equal classifiers). Per rule 2(b), GBM chosen as best AUC in the most demanding (external) cohort (0.56); Ensemble is the best internal-test model (0.86). n_test = 51 internal + 129 external. Data availability: statement says a GitHub will be created (not yet available) coded NR. Reporting follows Radiomics Quality Score (coded other).

title: Investigating the Feasibility of Predicting KRAS Status, Tumor Staging, and Extramural Venous Invasion in Colorectal Cancer Using Inter-Platform Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomic Features.
tumor_site_detail: Colorectal cancer with rectal MRI (rectal MRF/EMVI assessment); site split not reported
stage_detail: Stages 2 (n=7), 3 (n=22), 4 (n=23) among 52 staged patients

treatment_context: EGFR-targeted therapy eligibility (KRAS)
data_modality_detail: T2W and DWI/ADC MRI radiomics (features from both sequences combined)
algorithm: Neural network (KRAS); SVM (TNM stage), KNN (MRF), logistic regression (EMVI); PCA dimensionality reduction
input_features: 1702 radiomic features from ADC and T2W, reduced by PCA
comparator_detail: Different classifiers per task; no head-to-head across algorithms on KRAS
primary_outcome: KRAS mutation status (KRAS+ vs KRAS-)
performance_value: KRAS NN: train acc 72.93%, AUC 0.71; test acc 62.48%, AUC 0.68 (CI 0.41-0.93). TNM SVM test AUC 0.69, MRF KNN 0.578, EMVI LR 0.595 (Table 3)
performance_source: Table 3 and Results text (testing, scanner 2)
validation_detail: Training on scanner 1 (n=32, repeated 5-fold CV) and testing on scanner 2 patients from the same hospital (n=28); same center, so not external
funding: Deanship of Scientific Research, Prince Sattam bin Abdulaziz University (2022/03/20090)
key_finding: MRI radiomics (ADC + T2W) with NN gave modest KRAS discrimination (test AUC 0.68, wide CI) and similarly modest staging/EMVI performance; feature stability across platforms was low.
limitations_as_stated: Small sample; single-center design with selection bias
other_models_outcomes: TNM stage SVM test AUC 0.69 (acc 72%); MRF KNN test AUC 0.578; EMVI logistic regression test AUC 0.595
extraction_note: INCONSISTENT: test set n=28 in Methods but 30 in Results text (KRAS counts 9+19=28); staged cases sum to 52 of 60 (22+23+7). Table values used. Cross-scanner ICC feature stability reported >0.7 (low). Data availability: patient-level data in Supplementary Table S1 (coded yes). KRAS was taken as main model because it anchors title/abstract; other tasks (TNM, MRF, EMVI) in other_models_outcomes.

title: CT-based deep learning model for the prediction of DNA mismatch repair deficient colorectal cancer: a diagnostic study.
tumor_site_detail: Primary colon and rectal cancer
stage_detail: Primary CRC with surgery; clinical T and N stages recorded; stage mix not summarized
data_source_detail: Institution 1 Sixth Affiliated Hospital Sun Yat-sen (n=1606, temporal split 2012-2018/2018-2020); Institution 2 First Affiliated Hospital Zhengzhou (n=206 external)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Stratify MMR status to enable individual clinical treatment decision making (immunotherapy eligibility, adjuvant chemo)
treatment_context: dMMR/MSI-H: immunotherapy; no benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy
data_modality_detail: Pretreatment contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT, ROI-free, three axes
algorithm: MMRnet: ResNet101 per axis (x,y,z) fused by Gaussian process regression
input_features: Whole-volume portal venous CT slices in three axial directions (no tumor segmentation)
comparator_detail: ResNet101 vs VGG-19; ROI-based vs ROI-free preliminary experiment; uniaxial vs multi-axis
primary_outcome: dMMR vs pMMR by IHC
performance_source: Table 2 (external validation cohort)
validation_detail: Temporal internal validation (institution 1, n=482) and one external institution (n=206)
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82001765, 82272800)
key_finding: ROI-free CT deep learning (MMRnet) predicted dMMR with AUC 0.986 internally and 0.915 externally.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective with selection bias; prospective multicenter validation needed; (external cohort limitations per Discussion)
other_models_outcomes: ResNet101 outperformed VGG-19 (AUC 0.997 in the ResNet-only analysis, Fig S2); uniaxial AUCs 0.944, 0.762, 0.984 (X, Y, Z)
extraction_note: n_test = 482 temporal internal validation + 206 external. Methods state images were divided into training and test files by axial direction (slice-level split) in model development; unclear whether patient-level separation held for the ResNet-only comparison (AUC 0.997). A 100-patient preliminary experiment (ROI vs ROI-free) used institution-1 data. External dMMR prevalence 44.2% vs 24.3% internal.

title: Predicting Mismatch-Repair Status in Rectal Cancer Using Multiparametric MRI-Based Radiomics Models: A Preliminary Study.
tumor_site_detail: Rectal cancer, surgically resected, treatment-naive (no prior pelvic therapy)
stage_detail: No stage restriction; palliative resections excluded; pathologic TN stage recorded (Table 1)
data_source_detail: Changhai Hospital 2018-2019 (111; 78 train/33 test) and Ruijin Hospital Luwan Branch 2020 (65 external)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Preoperative MMR status for personalized treatment strategies (ICI eligibility; nCRT response)
treatment_context: Immune checkpoint inhibitors for dMMR; also nCRT considerations in discussion
data_modality_detail: Preoperative rectal MRI: T2WI, DWI (b=1000), CE-T1WI, radiomics
algorithm: LASSO feature selection + linear-kernel SVM (Radcloud, SMOTE for imbalance)
input_features: 4 selected radiomics features from combined T2WI, DWI, CE-T1WI (of 3770)
comparator_detail: Single-sequence models (T2WI, DWI, CE-T1WI) vs combined model
primary_outcome: dMMR vs pMMR by IHC on surgical specimen
performance_value: Modelcombination: external validation (n=65) AUC 0.874 (0.768-0.943), sens 0.909, spec 0.815, acc 0.831; test (n=33) AUC 0.901 (0.746-0.977), acc 0.939; train (n=78) AUC 0.910 (0.823-0.963), acc 0.859
performance_source: Table 3 (validation set, Modelcombination)
validation_detail: Random 70/30 split at Changhai (78/33) plus one external hospital (65, different scanners)
funding: Action Plan of Major Diseases Prevention and Treatment (2017ZX01001S12); Shanghai Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine Special Project (ZHYY-ZXYJHZX-201901)
key_finding: Multisequence MRI radiomics SVM predicted MMR status in rectal cancer with AUC 0.874 in the external set, outperforming single-sequence models.
limitations_as_stated: Small, unbalanced sample with selection bias and low generalizability; manual segmentation; deep learning not explored
other_models_outcomes: External AUC: T2WI 0.721, DWI 0.603, CE-T1WI 0.702; test AUC 0.707, 0.568, 0.691
extraction_note: Stage context coded mixed_all_stages as the paper applies no stage restriction (not explicitly stated). n_test = 33 internal test + 65 external. Only 31 dMMR cases overall (20 + 11). SMOTE applied in training only.

title: Evaluation of stromal cell infiltration in the tumor microenvironment enable prediction of treatment sensitivity and prognosis in colon cancer.
tumor_site_detail: Colon cancer (GEO meta cohort, TCGA-COAD, SYSUCC)
stage_detail: Stage I-III colon cancer (GSE39582 stages I-III in Table 1); chemo-benefit effect strongest in stage II
data_source_detail: Five GEO colon datasets (meta-GEO, GSE39582 main) N=990; TCGA-COAD n=382; SYSUCC in-house RNA-seq n=30; plus pan-cancer TCGA (4898) and 4 immunotherapy cohorts (467) as extensions
n_source: Abstract: GEO 990 + TCGA-COAD 382 + SYSUCC 30 (colon only; pan-cancer and immunotherapy cohorts excluded)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Stromal infiltration score to identify patients who benefit from fluorouracil-based adjuvant chemotherapy and prognosis
treatment_context: Fluorouracil-based adjuvant chemotherapy after surgery
data_modality_detail: Bulk gene expression (31-gene signature, ssGSEA-derived TME cell clusters)
algorithm: Unsupervised TME clustering + elastic net + LASSO-Cox (glmnet) producing 31-gene SIIS
input_features: Bulk transcriptome; 31 genes (11 positive, 20 negative Cox coefficients)
comparator_detail: NA (published signatures only compared descriptively in TCGA-COAD)
primary_outcome: Relapse-free and overall survival; adjuvant chemotherapy benefit
performance_value: Multivariable HR per unit SIIS in meta-GEO: RFS 1.58 (1.26-1.96), OS 1.42 (1.14-1.78); univariable RFS 1.52 (1.36-1.70), OS 1.36 (1.18-1.56) (Table 1). SIIS discriminating TMECS1 vs TMECS2 AUC 0.90, vs all others 0.82 (Fig 2F). TCGA-COAD and SYSUCC validation reported qualitatively/graphically
performance_source: Table 1 (MVA RFS, meta-GEO development cohort)
patient_outcomes_detail: High SIIS associated with higher relapse/mortality and no adjuvant chemotherapy survival benefit; also lower response to immunotherapy in 4 non-CRC cohorts
validation_detail: Development in meta-GEO (990); validation of associations in TCGA-COAD (382) and SYSUCC (30) public/retrospective cohorts; no classification metric in validation cohorts
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82102731, 82073303); Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province
key_finding: A 31-gene stromal infiltration score was an independent prognostic factor and identified high-stroma colon cancers that did not benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy; associations replicated in TCGA-COAD and SYSUCC.
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective datasets; prospective validation needed; optimal SIIS cutoff not established
other_models_outcomes: SIIS AUC 0.90/0.82 for TMECS1 vs others; pan-cancer survival association and 4 immunotherapy cohorts (n=467) with lower response in high SIIS; mechanistic CRISPR SAM screen (ADCY4, WNT-PCP, SIAH2-GPX3)
extraction_note: Primary metric is the development-cohort multivariable HR (continuous SIIS), so performance_cohort=train; validation cohorts support only outcome association (basis outcome_association). N analytic covers colon cohorts only. GEO data public (GSE39582 etc.); SYSUCC data upon request. Treatment context partly inferred; SYSUCC n=30.

title: A multitask dual-stream attention network for the identification of KRAS mutation in colorectal cancer.
tumor_site_detail: CRC in title; rectal cancer in keywords/contributions (pelvic T2 MRI); MSD pretraining CT from MSKCC
stage_detail: NR
data_source_detail: Shanxi Province Cancer Hospital pelvic T2 MRI (Nov 2016-Jun 2018; 369 patients, 306 retained) plus public Medical Segmentation Decathlon colon CT (126 patients) used only to pretrain segmentation part
n_source: Methods (Local data set: 306 patients retained, 3817 lesion patches)
therapeutic_decision_detail: Identify KRAS mutation status for prognosis and personalized treatment (anti-EGFR resistance)
treatment_context: Anti-EGFR antibody therapy (cetuximab, panitumumab)
data_modality_detail: T2-weighted pelvic MRI lesion patches (150x150 resized to 128x128) with segmentation mask
algorithm: MTDSAN: multitask dual-stream attention network (U-Net-variant segmentation + identification subnetworks, interlayer loss)
input_features: T2 MRI patch plus predicted lesion mask; segmentation encoder features as attention guidance
comparator_detail: VGG16, ResNet50, AlexNet, MobileNet, DenseNet121, InceptionV3, Xception and published radiomics/DL KRAS methods; ablations of attention modules and interlayer loss
primary_outcome: KRAS mutant vs wild-type (biopsy)
performance_value: 15-fold CV mean+-SD: acc 89.95+-1.23%, sens 89.29+-1.79%, spec 90.53+-2.45%, AUC 95.73+-0.52%; Dice 88.11+-0.86% (segmentation). Held-out test of 382 images from 36 cases mentioned but separate results not clearly itemized
performance_source: Abstract and Table 1 (MTDSAN row, mean +- SD across 15 folds)
validation_detail: 15-fold CV with an additional ~10% random case-level test set (36 cases, 382 images); single device; no external data; unclear whether folds split by patient or patch
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (61972274, 61872261); Natural Science Foundation of Shanxi (201801D121139); Taiyuan 2019-nCoV project (XG2020-5-04)
key_finding: MTDSAN reported KRAS mutation identification AUC 0.957 and accuracy 89.95% in 15-fold CV on single-center T2 MRI, outperforming comparator CNNs.
limitations_as_stated: Patches resized to 128x128 may distort structure; training and test data from the same imaging device with no cross-device evaluation
other_models_outcomes: Segmentation Dice 88.11%; comparator CNNs and ablated variants lower accuracy (Tables 1-6)
extraction_note: Stage not reported (stage_context NR) so status partial. Abstract reports metrics from 15-fold CV while also stating a 36-case test set (382 images); the paper does not clearly separate test-set results, so performance_cohort coded cross_validation. Lesion patches (3817 from 306 patients) are the modeling unit; fold assignment may be patch-level (possible leakage; not stated). n_train/n_performance derived as 306-36=270 patients.

title: Development and validation of a weakly supervised deep learning framework to predict the status of molecular pathways and key mutations in colorectal cancer from routine histology images: a retrospective study.
tumor_site_detail: TCGA-CRC-DX colon and rectal adenocarcinoma (primary tumours); PAIP external cohort colorectal
stage_detail: TCGA stages I-IV (stage-stratified AUROC in appendix); PAIP stage NR
data_source_detail: TCGA-CRC-DX (502 slides, 499 patients; labels from Liu et al. and Kather et al.); external PAIP challenge cohort (47 slides, PCR-based MSI)
n_source: derived: 499 TCGA patients (502 slides; Methods) + 47 PAIP slides (Methods/Table); PAIP patient count NR so 47 slides treated as units
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict MSI (and other molecular pathways/mutations) from H&E to stratify patients for targeted therapies and immunotherapy; "crucial for optimal therapeutic decision making"
treatment_context: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (MSI-high); anti-EGFR (KRAS/BRAF); encorafenib+cetuximab (BRAF)
data_modality_detail: H&E whole-slide images, tile-based
algorithm: Three-model pipeline: ResNet18 tumour-tile detector; adapted ResNet34 trained by iterative draw and rank sampling (IDaRS, weakly supervised) for slide labels; HoVer-Net nuclear segmentation + SVM feature importance for cellular composition analysis
input_features: Tumour tiles (256 um) from H&E WSIs
comparator_detail: Published AUROCs from Kather 2019 (train-test split), Echle 2020 (3-fold CV) and Kather 2020 for the same TCGA-CRC-DX cohort
primary_outcome: MSI status (MSI vs MSS) from H&E; also hypermutation, CIN, CIMP, BRAF, TP53, KRAS status
performance_value: MSI: external PAIP (n=47) AUROC 0.98, AUPRC 0.95; TCGA Kather split (n=359, 62 MSI) AUROC 0.90 (SD 0.01), AUPRC 0.72; TCGA 4-fold CV (n=428) AUROC 0.86 (SD 0.04), AUPRC 0.62. Other labels (4-fold CV): hypermutation 0.81, CIN 0.83, CIMP-high 0.79, BRAFmut 0.79, TP53mut 0.73, KRASmut 0.60
performance_source: Table (Validation of prediction on TCGA-CRC-DX and PAIP datasets; MSI external row); Results text reports internal split/CV values
patient_outcomes_detail: Association of predicted labels with cell composition/TIL only; no patient outcomes
validation_detail: 4-fold CV in TCGA-CRC-DX; Kather train/test split; model trained on TCGA and tested on PAIP external cohort (47 slides from 3 centres in South Korea, 12 MSI/35 MSS, PCR labels)
funding: UK Medical Research Council (MR/P015476/1); PAIP data funded by Korea Health Industry Development Institute
conflicts_of_interest: MI grants from Roche; DS personal fees from Royal Philips; NMR research funding from GSK and PathLAKE (partly funded by Royal Philips); others none
key_finding: IDaRS outperformed prior methods on TCGA-CRC-DX for hypermutation, MSI, CIN, BRAF and TP53; MSI AUROC 0.90 on Kather split and 0.98 on a small external cohort; TIL/necrosis associated with MSI.
limitations_as_stated: Small external cohort (47 slides); sampling/hyperparameters possibly suboptimal; imperfect nuclear classification; needs large-scale multicentre validation before clinical use
other_models_outcomes: Per-label models trained separately; see performance_value
extraction_note: Multiple co-primary molecular labels; MSI chosen as primary (immunotherapy selection; only label with external validation). External AUROC 0.98 has no CI; n_train NR (CV folds, not a fixed split). PAIP is 3 centres so coded external_multicenter (external set drawn from a single challenge dataset). Code available subject to IP constraints.

title: Quantitative Prediction of Microsatellite Instability in Colorectal Cancer With Preoperative PET/CT-Based Radiomics.
tumor_site_detail: Colon and rectum (rectum 36.4%); primary tumour ROI
stage_detail: Stage I-IV (I 6.4%, II 26.6%, III 37.6%, IV 29.4%); patients with neoadjuvant therapy excluded
data_source_detail: Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center; 154 patients 2010-2018 + 19 MSS patients 2018-2020 with preoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT
therapeutic_decision_detail: Non-invasive preoperative MSI status to "optimize the treatment decision support" (prognosis, adjuvant chemotherapy and immunotherapy selection)
treatment_context: Immunotherapy (anti-PD-1) and adjuvant chemotherapy decisions according to MSI status
data_modality_detail: Preoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics (PyRadiomics, 2,492 features); clinical features were candidates in selection but final model used only 2 radiomic features
algorithm: BalancedBagging ensemble with AdaBoost base classifiers; random-forest ensemble feature selection after random under-sampling
input_features: Two wavelet radiomic features (PET LHH first-order skewness; CT HHL first-order root mean squared)
comparator_detail: CEA-only, CT-feature-only, PET-feature-only and CEA+CT+PET versions of the model (Table 2)
primary_outcome: MSI-H vs MSS/MSI-L (by MMR IHC, PCR if doubtful)
performance_value: Independent validation (n=82): AUC 0.828, accuracy 0.768, sensitivity 0.833, specificity 0.763 (CT+PET); CT only AUC 0.832, PET only 0.684, CEA only 0.692, CEA+CT+PET 0.803; no cross-validation or training performance reported
performance_source: Abstract; Results (Performance of the Radiomics Signature); Table 2
validation_detail: 2010-2018 patients randomly split 6:4 (train/validation); 19 additional 2018-2020 MSS patients added to the validation set; single centre; validation set n=82 includes only about 6 MSI-H
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (81771861, 81971648); Shanghai Scientific and Technological Innovation Program; National Key R&D Project
key_finding: A two-feature PET/CT radiomics ensemble predicted MSI status with AUC 0.828 (sens 83.3%, spec 76.3%) in a small single-centre validation set; selected features correlated with clinical variables.
limitations_as_stated: NR (no explicit limitations section); authors note imbalanced data prevented cross-validation
other_models_outcomes: Ablations: CT only AUC 0.832 (acc 0.817); PET only 0.684; CEA only 0.692; CEA+CT+PET 0.803
extraction_note: Validation set mixes random hold-out of the 2010-2018 cohort and 19 later MSS patients, so coded temporal_same_center / temporal (judgement). Validation counts: sens 83.3% and spec 76.3% imply ~6 MSI-H and 76 MSS in n=82; the text TP/TN/FN/FP labels (5 TP, 58 TN, 18 FN, 1 FP) appear inconsistent with these. n_train derived: 173-82. CT-only model had slightly higher AUC (0.832) than the CT+PET model chosen by authors. No COI statement found.

title: Prediction of clinically actionable genetic alterations from colorectal cancer histopathology images using deep learning.
tumor_site_detail: TCGA-COAD and TCGA-READ combined; SMH surgically resected sporadic CRC
stage_detail: NR (stage not reported for TCGA or SMH cohorts)
country: USA (TCGA); South Korea (Seoul St. Mary Hospital)
data_source_detail: TCGA-COAD/READ frozen and FFPE WSIs (629 patients); own SMH cohort of 142 patients (2017-2019) with panel sequencing as external set
therapeutic_decision_detail: Predict "clinically actionable" mutations (APC, KRAS, PIK3CA, SMAD4, TP53) from H&E as complementary method to determine optimal therapeutic strategy / personalized treatment
treatment_context: Mutation-guided therapy (e.g., anti-EGFR resistance with KRAS/PIK3CA mutations)
data_modality_detail: H&E WSIs, 360x360 px patches at 20x; frozen and FFPE slides
algorithm: Inception-v3 patch classifiers (separate per gene and per tissue type) after CNN tissue/non-tissue and Inception-v3 normal/tumour classifiers; slide score = mean patch probability
input_features: Tumour patches (tumour probability >0.9) from H&E WSIs
comparator_detail: None; TCGA-only vs TCGA+SMH training compared
primary_outcome: Mutation status (mutant vs wild-type) of TP53 (chosen primary; also APC, KRAS, PIK3CA, SMAD4)
performance_value: TP53 TCGA-FFPE-trained classifier on external SMH (n=142) AUC 0.775; SMH external other genes: APC 0.654, KRAS 0.581, PIK3CA 0.570, SMAD4 0.652. TCGA 10-fold CV concatenated AUC frozen/FFPE: APC 0.771/0.742, KRAS 0.778/0.645, PIK3CA 0.713/0.690, SMAD4 0.693/0.763, TP53 0.809/0.783. TCGA+SMH mixed training, 10-fold CV on SMH: APC 0.812, KRAS 0.832, PIK3CA 0.769, SMAD4 0.782, TP53 0.845; on TCGA: 0.766, 0.694, 0.708, 0.791, 0.822
performance_source: Results, Tests on external cohorts paragraph (Supplementary Figure 1 per text); Figures 2-8
validation_detail: Patient-level 10-fold CV within TCGA (frozen and FFPE); TCGA FFPE-trained classifiers applied to single-centre SMH cohort (142 patients); then mixed TCGA+SMH training with 10-fold CV. Best of at least 5 classifiers per gene chosen by AUC on test data
funding: Research Fund of Seoul St. Mary's Hospital (program year 2018)
key_finding: Five gene mutations were predictable from H&E (TCGA AUCs 0.645-0.809) but generalised modestly to an external Korean cohort (AUC 0.570-0.775); adding SMH data to training improved performance.
limitations_as_stated: Classifiers sensitive to dataset differences (frozen vs FFPE need separate models); black-box interpretation; separate classifier per gene; not yet sufficient for clinical use
other_models_outcomes: Other genes and frozen vs FFPE variants in performance_value; mixed TCGA+SMH models reported separately
extraction_note: No single primary model: five co-primary gene classifiers; chosen TP53 as best AUC in the most demanding (external) cohort per rule 2b, though KRAS is the most therapeutically actionable (external KRAS AUC 0.581). stage_context NR (stage not reported), so status partial. n_train NR: balanced sampling (<1.4 fold) applied but per-gene numbers only in Supplementary Table 1.
